### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Exact upstream SVG revision/author has not been recovered. Existing rivers and the original metro alignments are inherited illustration; the Shanghai timeline is a history source, not geographic evidence.

- [Songjiang Tram 1](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14251681), [Tram 2](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/16159672) and [Line 9](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/214629) were recovered as alignment cross-checks. T2’s old Canghua spur uses the current T1 alignment as geometric context; historical service still needs the dated route description.
- Songjiang University Town’s short branch and local offsets at Sports Center depict simplified tram connections. They must not be read as survey-accurate co-location.
- Shanghai Railway Station, West Nanjing Road, Caoyang Road and other walking transfers need separate paid-area identities. A shared name or fare concession does not justify merging all markers or highlighting every line’s platforms.
- The early Jinjiang Park/Shanghai South and Zhangjiang High-Tech Park replacement alignments require historical maps. Modern line geometry cannot independently verify removed surface stations.
- Line 5's first track (2003-11-25) started inside the Line 1 Xinzhuang circle, 13 units past its own terminus. It now ends at the Line 5 circle, and the run into the joint station is a separate track from 2005-12-25 (0.3 km of the unchanged 16.6); nothing visible changes, since both circles covered the overrun. Likewise Line 3's 2005 track started 5.4 units behind the centre of the 2005 Line 3 circle at Shanghai South, at the circle's edge rather than its centre (spec §4); it now starts at the centre, and the run into the 2005 and 2021 interchange markers is a separate track from 2005-12-25 (0.1 of the unchanged 1.2 km).
- 2026-09-30 OSM audit (route relations, platform ways and stop positions; local affine fits cross-checked with the network fit). The Airport Link track was redrawn along its OSM alignment (both directions averaged) from Hongqiao Airport Terminal 2 to Pudong Airport Terminal 1 and 2; its South Sanlin, East Kangqiao and Shanghai International Resort circles sit on their stops. Its Hongqiao T2 and Pudong T1&2 circles stand just outside the metro interchange markers (separate stations, §6), about 2 W from the Airport Link platforms that lie under those markers. On the Pudong Airport approach the three lines are drawn in their real order, Airport Link | Maglev | Line 2, touching (centre distance exactly 1 W since 2026-10-03; before, 0.12–0.25 units over or apart); the Pudong interchange marker spans the Maglev and Line 2 ends. At Longyang Road Line 2 lies midway between Line 7 and the Maglev (its OSM position; the three tracks are about 0.5 W apart there); east of the station it follows its OSM course (2026-10-03): touching the Maglev for about 30 units, then curving north away from it (previously drawn straight, 1 W north of the Maglev, up to 3.8 units off).
- The Line 11 Anting branch between Shanghai Circuit and East Changji Road follows OSM (previously up to 1.8 W west of it). The Pujiang line's bend south of Dongchengyi Road is rounded with a 9-unit radius, within 0.4 W of OSM. The historical Line 2 elevated section (2000–2010) and Line 1's original surface alignment via Xinlonghua (1993–2004) are drawn as smooth curves through their original endpoints; their exact historical alignment is not surveyed. Songjiang tram joins at Zhongchen Road and Xinmiaosan Road are rounded; the Canghua Road spur (2018-12-20 – 2019-08-10) keeps its reversing junction.
- Historical out-of-station circles now sit on their real platforms along their own tracks: Yishan Road Line 4 (2005–2010, stacked north of the Line 3 circle, as the Line 4 platform is about 130 m north; OSM has only stop positions here, which put both lines' stops over the same 160 m, so the 2026-10-03 audit kept this documented layout rather than move it on that evidence — the Line 4 station is underground below the elevated Line 3 one, per [zh.wikipedia 宜山路站](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/宜山路站)), Loushanguan Road Line 15 (2021–2024), South Shaanxi Road Line 10 (2010–2015), West Nanjing Road Line 2 (1999–2015, the same position as its 2015 replacement) and Dashijie Line 8 (2007–2021). Longju Road appears in OSM but has never opened; Jinji Road is open (OSM station node) although OSM's Line 9 route relation omits its stop.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: each line's platform is the mean of its OSM stop positions (median 0.16 units from the mapped platform ways), projected onto the drawn track. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. 36 bridges follow the Wikimedia line map's bends (Xujiahui, Lujiazui, Guilin Road, Middle Huaxia Road and others). The same pass redrew ten track stretches more than 1 W off OSM (Lines 1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 ×2, 11, 14, 15) and Line 11 one track width east of Line 16 through Luoshan Road; 67 circles moved onto their OSM platforms (largest Zhumei Road 2.0 W, Gulang Road 1.7 W). Track ends lie on their line's platform point. Historic out-of-station pairs keep their recorded spacing.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): every station circle lies exactly on its own line's drawn track (54 circles snapped across the track by at most 0.47 units, along-track positions unchanged), and every track end at a station lies on its platform point (Line 12's 2014 Qufu Road start moved 0.29 onto the Line 8/12 crossing). Twelve out-of-station or no-transfer pairs whose circles touch slightly stay at their real platforms (South Shaanxi Road 2010–2015, Shanghai Railway Station, Xinzhuang 2003–2005, Zhongshan Park 2000–2005, West Nanjing Road, Hongqiao Airport Terminal 2, Yishan Road 2005–2010, Xinlonghua 2000–2004).
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): every track is tangent-continuous (no direction jump over 12°; `corners.py` reports 0, down from 119). Micro segments under 0.3 units were dropped, runs of straight segments simplified at 0.25 units, and every remaining angular joint replaced by a cubic fillet tangent to both neighbours (within 1.2 units of the old corner, 2.4 for the few turns over 45°). Outside Luoshan Road no track moved more than 0.52 units (0.1 W). Track-end trims no longer leave hooks: a track that the new end point lies on is cut there rather than extended back (Line 1's 1993 Xinlonghua–Caobao Road 180° hook removed). Lines 11 and 16 share one OSM corridor from where Line 11 joins north of Luoshan Road to where it turns east south of Xiuyan Road. They are drawn as smooth offsets 1 W apart around the corridor's OSM centre: Line 11 on the west north of Luoshan Road, crossing at the station, where the two lines interleave cross-platform and the marker is one circle, then on the east. Round Xiuyan Road, which Line 16 passes without stopping, they were widened to 2 W until 2026-10-03; they now touch there as well (5.00 units centre to centre, within 0.03, to where Line 11 turns east), because their viaducts are only 0.7–1.1 units (about 20 m) apart. The pair is centred on the corridor, so each line stays within 2.4 units of its own OSM track (OSM ways 411264073, 427782946 for Line 11; 1044602537, 1044602536 for Line 16), Line 16 returns onto its own course south of the parting instead of rejoining it near East Zhoupu, and Xiuyan Road's circle moved 2.4 units west with the Line 11 track, re-projected from its OSM stop positions.
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01, spec §5 rule 1, reference map; amended 2026-10-02 by the 0.4 R rule, spec §5 rule 3, see below): the README's Wikimedia Shanghai Metro line map sets the composition at every station it shows. Each station was checked by eye against a crop of that map. Platforms stay at their real OpenStreetMap positions (no sliding to copy the reference's spacing), so separate dots often overlap. Lines and stations newer than the reference (Airport Link, Jinshan Railway at Xinzhuang) follow rule 2 and are separate dots. **One shape** only where the reference draws one dot or pill:
  - Shared track: the Lines 3/4 stations (Hongqiao Road to Baoshan Road), drawn as one pill.
  - Reference one shape: South Xizang Road 4/8, West Gaoke Road 6/7, Yaohua Road 7/8, Siping Road 8/10, Qufu Road 8/12, Lujiabang Road 8/9, Lantian Road 9/14, Longde Road 11/13, Luoshan Road 11/16 and Changyi Road 14/18 are each one circle on the crossing. Oriental Sports Center 6/8/11 is one pill. Hanzhong Road 12/13 is one dot, with Line 1 a separate dot. Hongqiao Railway Station 2/17 is one pill, with Line 10 a separate lobe.
  - Everything else is separate dots joined by bridges, as the reference draws them. This includes the overlapping "cↄ" pairs whose dots are at least 0.4 R apart: Lancun Road, Gangcheng Road, Dongming Road, Middle Longhua Road, Jiangpu Road, Dashijie, Shendu Highway, Jinhai Road, Shanghai West Railway Station, Yuqiao, Jiangpu Park, Lianxi Road and Tongchuan Road.
  - It also includes Xujiahui (1, 9 and 11), South Shaanxi Road, People's Square (1, 2 and 8), Xinzhuang, Hongqiao Airport Terminal 2 and Longyang Road.
  - One shape by the 0.4 R rule (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3: separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump, so they become one shape through the same real platform points): Zhongshan Park (Line 2 joins the 3/4 pill, 0.06 R), Century Avenue (Lines 2 and 6 from 2007, 0.14 R; Line 9 joins them from 2009; Line 4 stays a separate lobe), Dalian Road (12/4), Pudong Avenue (14/4), Damuqiao Road (12/4), Dong'an Road (4/7), Changshou Road (13/7), Zhaojiabang Road (7/9), Laoximen (10/8), Jiashan Road (12/9), Madang Road (13/9, 2010 and 2015), Jiao Tong University (10/11), Xintiandi (10/13), Tiantong Road (10/12) and Zhenru (11/14). Middle Longhua Road (12/7) was merged on 2026-10-02 at 0.38 R; on 2026-10-03 its Line 12 platform moved 2.1 units with the realigned Line 12 track, the two platforms are now 0.56 R apart, and it is two dots with a bridge again.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): Line 1's opening of 1993-05-28 (three pieces) grows as one path and is handed over in place on 1997-07-01 and 2004-12-04. The Pearl Line opening of 2000-12-26 (two pieces, handed over 2004-01-01) and Songjiang Tram 2 of 2018-12-20 (two pieces, handed over 2019-08-10) are each one path too. 15 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.

- Final audit (2026-10-03), tracks: every track was compared with its line's OSM route centreline (2026-10-01 snapshot, projected through the same transform the 2026-10-01 markers were placed with; both running tracks averaged). The 42 stretches more than 2 units (0.4 W) off that are not the side-by-side convention, plus the Jinshanwei and Huamu Road terminus approaches and both Line 5 branches at Dongchuan Road, were redrawn on that centreline, smoothed over about 3 units (OSM vertex noise) and spliced in tangent-continuously: Lines 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 and 15, the Pujiang line, the Jinshan Railway and the Airport Link. The largest were the Jinshan Railway into Jinshanwei (6.0 units, now ending at the Jinshanwei platform), Line 7 at Zhenping Road and across the Huangpu (4.7 and 4.6), Line 9 east of Century Avenue (4.7), Line 1 near People's Square (4.5), Line 4 north of Lancun Road and at Century Avenue (4.4), Line 2 at West Nanjing Road and People's Square (4.0) and east of Longyang Road (3.8); the redrawn stretches stay within about 1 unit of OSM. At Dongchuan Road the Line 5 Minhang branch now runs through the station on its OSM course (it was up to 3.3 units east) and the Fengxian branch starts at the Dongchuan Road platform. Kept as drawn (side-by-side convention or station layout, where the real tracks are closer than one line width): the Lines 3/4 shared corridor, Lines 11/16 round Luoshan Road, the Airport Link | Maglev | Line 2 Pudong approach, the Jinshan Railway beside Line 1, Line 6 beside Line 10 at Gangcheng Road and beside Line 11 east of Oriental Sports Center, Line 1 beside Line 8 at People's Square, Lines 2/10/17 at Hongqiao Railway Station, Line 13 beside Line 7 at Changqing Road, Line 12 at Longhua, Line 9 beside Line 2 under Century Avenue and the Jinshan Railway's start at Shanghai South. `data-km` values are published lengths and are unchanged.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), side by side: lines drawn side by side now touch exactly (centre distance W = 5 units) where they partly overlapped or left a hairline gap: Line 16 and the Maglev east of Longyang Road, the Jinshan Railway beside Line 1 (Xinzhuang – Jinjiang Park), the Airport Link, Maglev and Line 2 on the Pudong approach, Line 6 and Line 10 at Gangcheng Road, Line 11 beside Line 6 from Oriental Sports Center to South Lingyan Road, Line 9 beside Line 2 under Century Avenue, Lines 11 and 16 round Luoshan Road, Line 1 beside Line 8 at People's Square and beside Line 14 near South Huangpi Road, Line 2 beside the Maglev east of Longyang Road, Line 4 beside Line 6 north of Lancun Road and Line 2 beside Line 17 at Hongqiao Railway Station. Hairline gaps on the Lines 3/4 shared corridor were closed (shared track keeps its 4–5 unit offset, spec §4). Terminus track ends were not moved by this. The overlaps that remain are crossings or lines converging into an interchange: Longyang Road (2/7), Lancun Road south (4/6), Hanzhong Road (1/13, a shallow crossing) and Century Avenue (2/4).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), joints: every same-line joint is exact and tangent-continuous. Corners fixed: Line 5 east of Xinzhuang (4.3°, the joint at the old out-of-station Line 5 terminus, not covered by a marker), Line 17 at Oriental Land (3.5°), Line 3 at Jiangwan Town (2.7°), Line 2 at NECC, Songhong Road and Zhongshan Park (about 2°, Zhongshan Park also a 0.003 gap), Line 1 at Shanghai Railway Station (1.6°), Line 12 at Tiantong Road (1.4°) and the historic Line 2 elevated section's start at Longyang Road (38.7°, 2000–2010). Where a redrawn track met an unchanged one at a station, the redrawn one bends to the unchanged one's tangent over 16 units. Line 3's 2000 Pearl Line track again lies exactly on its 2004 continuation (`data-takes-over`).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), stations: 187 platform points moved. Every platform on a redrawn track was re-projected onto it at its OSM platform centre (stop-position mean), and every other platform more than 1.0 unit (24 m) along its track from that centre was moved to it; 87 moved more than 1 unit. The largest: Jinshanwei 11.6 (with its terminus), Zhongning Road 3.6, Dongchuan Road 3.5, the Airport Link platforms at Jinghong Road 3.3 and 3.0, Shanghai Children's Medical Center 3.0, Changping Road 2.6, and Caohejing Hi-Tech Park, Songhong Road, Lingkong Road, Xiepu Road and Pudong Football Stadium 2.4–2.5. The stacked-crossing circles (Hanzhong Road, South Xizang Road, West Gaoke Road, Yaohua Road, Siping Road, Qufu Road, Lujiabang Road, Lantian Road, Longde Road, Luoshan Road, Changyi Road) follow the new crossings; out-of-station circles staggered within 3 R of their partner keep their position and were only snapped onto their redrawn tracks (Changqing Road Line 7 moved 2.2 that way); the National Exhibition and Convention Center, South Pudong Road and Jinghong Road out-of-station pairs are real distances apart and moved like any station, with their connectors. Track ends at moved stations follow them (Songhong Road, Gongfu Xincun, Fujin Road, NECC, Yaohua Road, North Jiading, Huamu Road and Jinshanwei among them), and bridges follow their dots. People's Park (1999–2000, no transfer) and Yishan Road keep their documented layouts. No separate shapes are closer than 0.4 R afterwards; Middle Longhua Road was split again (above).
- Geography (2026-10-03): the artwork's Huangpu source 竖潦泾 (towards 大泖港) ended in a flat cut at y 2606.44, the bottom edge of the original artwork's water (present already in `c4fe500`; the 2026 continuity audit checked the 2843.75 canvas edge, not this one). It now continues along the OSM river area ([way 8002643](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/8002643)) to where it divides into 大泖港 and 张泾河, both narrower than the rivers the map draws, in the `damaogang-continuation` group (fill plus outer banks, joined tangent to the artwork's banks). Coastline check: inside the original canvas the drawn shores lie a median 1.1 units from the OSM coastline; the expanded shores are 6–8 units off (about 1 px at the overview, nothing to compare against at full zoom) and were left; islets not drawn are below the spec's 4 overview px² rule; the Nanhui shore keeps the restored original line rather than OSM's newer seawalls.
- Events checked to 2026-10-02 (research 2026-10-02): no opening, extension, infill station, rename, interchange change, closure or operator handover after 2025-12-27; the network is still 21 lines, 523 stations and 906 km ([QQ News, 2026-08-29](https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260829A059JY00)). South Jiangyang Road (Line 18) remains closed ([QQ News, 2026-09-04](https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260904A0AIK300)). Not yet open and not drawn: Line 22 (Chongming line; testing since 2026-08-26, [Shanghai government](https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/nw31406/20260507/fba2622a1dc1441f9365f45794e83a3a.html)), the Line 13 east and west extensions (target 2026-12-31), the Nanhui branch (target 2027-06-30), Line 21 phase 1 (with Shanghai East, 2027), Lines 19, 20 and 23, the Line 12 and Line 15 extensions, the Jiamin line and the Demonstration Zone line. Temporary closures are not drawn (spec §7): Baoshan Road and Dongbaoxing Road 2026-02-16 – 02-22 while Baoshan Road was rebuilt ([Shanghai government](https://www.shanghai.gov.cn/nw4411/20260207/826c36c83a5a43df8e3f39c1f59237a6.html)), and NECC and Panxiang Road on the morning of 2026-09-23. The 2024–2025 entries were re-confirmed: the 2024-09-21 renames took effect with the 2024 network map from that day ([The Paper](https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_28825374)); the Airport Link opened 2024-12-27 with Zhongchun Road in-station and the other transfers out-of-station; Jinghong Road's temporary underground passage opened 2025-07-05 ([The Paper](https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_31114507)); the Jinshan Railway's Xinzhuang station opened 2025-01-05 with an out-of-station transfer ([The Paper](https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_29852772)); Loushanguan Road became in-station on 2024-12-31 ([Changning district](https://www.shcn.gov.cn/col6991/20250102/1275679.html)).

<a id="taipei"></a>

## Taipei (`taipei`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/taipei/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/taipei/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/taipei/map.svg).

Scope follows [Taipei Metro's official route map](https://web.metro.taipei/pages/assets/images/routemap2026-en.png), which draws New Taipei Metro's Circular, Sanying, Danhai and Ankeng lines and the Taoyuan Airport MRT as part of the network (spec §8). Danhai and Ankeng are light rail, drawn as tracks only; Hongshulin and Shisizhang list them in `data-lines` from their openings. Taipei Metro operated the Circular Line from its opening until 2023-05-22; from 2023-05-23 its stations show New Taipei Metro ([Wikipedia](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_line_(New_Taipei_Metro)>); registered to New Taipei on 2023-01-31, physically handed over on 2023-05-23 per [zh 新北捷運](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/新北捷運)), using the text-free symbol from [its Chinese Wikipedia logo file](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:New_Taipei_Metro_logo.svg) with editor metadata removed. That file is marked non-free (a trademark used under fair use); no free text-free version was found. Airport MRT stations show Taoyuan Metro's symbol, `taoyuan-metro.svg`, from [File:Taoyuan Metro logo plain.svg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taoyuan_Metro_logo_plain.svg). That file is tagged PD-ineligible (US only; Taiwan) and trademarked, and its colours match the [operator's own logo](https://www.tymetro.com.tw/tymetro-new/_images/all/logo.png). Editor metadata and nested transforms were flattened, and it contains no lettering. Historical romanization revisions are not modelled: labels use current Hanyu Pinyin names throughout, although the operator used Wade-Giles names until 2003 (e.g. Hsimen, Tamshui, Kuting; [Epoch Times, 2003-11-23](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/3/11/23/n416727.htm)) and Danshui from 2003 to 2011.

### Primary records and other focused references

- [Taipei Metro: Chronicles][p-tp-official] — **New**. Operator opening chronology and section lengths. Use the dated entries, not a later line name applied retrospectively.
- [Taipei Metro: 大事紀][p-tp-chronicles-zh] — **New**. Native-language operator chronology; cross-check opening/renaming wording against English translations.
- [Taipei Metro annual report 2015][p-tp-report-2015] — **New**. Operational route-name convention and Dingpu opening. Naming announcements and earlier through-service changes are not necessarily the same date.
- [Taipei Metro annual report 2007][p-tp-report-2007] — **New**. Historical sections and lengths; use to reconcile SVG kilometres instead of measuring the drawing.
- [Maokong Gondola: Chronicles][p-tp-gondola-history] — **Recovered**. Passenger opening 4 July 2007; later temporary suspensions are operational history, not demolition.
- [Maokong Gondola: system introduction][p-tp-gondola-profile] — **Recovered**. 4.03 km, four passenger stations and two angle stations. Only passenger stations contribute to the map count.
- [Maokong Gondola: transport connections][p-tp-gondola-access] — **Recovered**. Taipei Zoo MRT–gondola walking connection, approximately 350 m; not one paid-area station.
- [Taipei Metro route map 2026 (English)](https://web.metro.taipei/pages/assets/images/routemap2026-en.png) — **New**. Scope source (spec §8) and badge colours for LB, V and K.
- [New Taipei City: Sanying Line opens 30 June](https://www.ntpc.gov.tw/ch/home.jsp?id=e8ca970cde5c00e1&dataserno=9eddd1f8da661071318da507f2acbc87) — **New**. Official opening at 14:00 on 2026-06-30; trial operation, fare-free, until 31 August ([hours extended, CNA](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aloc/202607300233.aspx)); fares from 1 September.
- [NTMC: Ankeng LRT opens 10 February](https://www.ntmetro.com.tw/basic/?mode=detail&node=578) — **New**. Opening ceremony in the morning, first public train 13:00 the same day; free trial operation to 12 March ([Focus Taiwan](https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202302100016)).
- [CNA: Blue Coast Line opens 15 November 2020](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/firstnews/202011140019.aspx) — **New**. Fare-free until 14 December; first-day riders reported by [TVBS](https://news.tvbs.com.tw/life/1417251).
- [Taipei Times: Danhai LRT first section opens](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2018/12/24/2003706693) — **New**. Ceremony 23 December 2018, public service from 24 December ([Taiwan News](https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/3601751)).
- [China Post: Airport MRT begins commercial operations (archived)](https://web.archive.org/web/20170302095929/http://www.chinapost.com.tw/taiwan/national/national-news/2017/03/02/492718/Airport-MRT.htm) — **New**. 2 March 2017. Invited group rides from 2 February (government bodies and the rail industry, not counted), then free public trial rides with 20,000 numbered tickets a day, 8:00–16:00, from 16 February: the date used (spec §7).
- [CNA: Laojie River station opens 31 July 2023](https://www.cna.com.tw/news/ahel/202307270118.aspx) — **New**. Opened to passengers at 11:50 ([Taoyuan Metro notice](https://www.tymetro.com.tw/tymetro-new/tw/_pages/news/show-1822-1.html)).
- [Taoyuan Metro: A1 Taipei Main Station transfers](https://www.tymetro.com.tw/tymetro-new/tw/_pages/travel-guide/A1) — **New**. Walking transfers (10–15 min) to Taipei Metro Taipei Main Station and Beimen; drawn as out-of-station connectors.
- [LTN: Sanying Dingpu transfer](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/life/breakingnews/5249474) — **New**. Tap out of the Bannan Line, tap in to the Sanying Line: an out-of-station transfer (connector from 2026-06-30).

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Exact upstream SVG revision/author has not been recovered. The pre-existing metro map provides the base geography; sources for openings are independent of that artwork.

- [Xiaobitan branch](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/4250381) and [Songshan–Xindian](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/4250357) underpin the branch correction: continue roughly south with the main line from Qizhang before bending west.
- [Maokong Gondola track way 71266575](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/71266575) and [route relation 17787820](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/17787820) supply the added cable alignment and four passenger stops. Intermediate angle facilities influence the route but are not passenger markers.
- The operator specifies a walk from Taipei Zoo MRT to the gondola. Banqiao/Circular Line and Xinpu/Xinpu Minsheng similarly need separate identities, not automatic grouping by proximity/name.
- Compare stored section lengths against operator historical tables: for example the operator chronology quotes 10.5 km for the initial Muzha section and 8.4 km for the Guting–Xindian extension, whereas existing allocations use different totals. These require reconciliation, not a blanket “verified” label.
- The four added lines follow OSM route relations ([Airport MRT 2108764](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2108764), [Sanying 21066080](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/21066080), [Danhai 9154523](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9154523) / [Blue Coast 13611116](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13611116), [Ankeng 15443525](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/15443525); Geofabrik Taiwan 2026-09-23, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0). They are projected through the existing Taipei affine fit, with a Gaussian local correction from the matched stations near the existing network, and drawn as smooth Béziers with stations as forced vertices. The Airport MRT follows its real course past Beimen and New Taipei Industrial Park: the local clearance offsets of up to 8 units it once had there were removed on 2026-10-03 (spec §5, accuracy over clearance), so it passes the edge of the Beimen dot as it does on the ground. At Dingpu (2026-09-30 OSM audit) both terminus circles sit on their real platforms: the Sanying track follows OSM into its elevated platform, and the Bannan circle moved about 25 units north-east onto the Bannan platform, touching the Sanying circle (connector hidden).
- North of Hongshulin the Danhai LRT runs beside the Tamsui–Xinyi Line for about 0.3 km (OSM tracks 1–2 map units apart, centrelines 2–4 units apart through the local station fit). Since 2026-10-03 it touches the Tamsui–Xinyi Line exactly (2.8 units centre to centre, (W + 1.6)/2, within 0.02) on its diverging side: it starts at Hongshulin's marker centre, reaches the touching offset just outside the marker and leaves in one smooth curve where the real tracks part. It had been drawn as a parallel offset about 4.5 units away, leaving a 1.3-unit background sliver. The Tamsui–Xinyi Line itself was not moved there (between Hongshulin and Tamsui it runs up to 3.3 units from its OSM course).
- Separate identities: `station-taipei-main-station-a1`, `station-sanchong-a2`, `station-new-taipei-industrial-park-a3` and `station-dingpu-lb01` are separate stations from their Taipei Metro namesakes (out-of-station connectors).
- Canvas re-extended on 2026-09-26 to `-6916 -1589 13513 8393` so the Airport MRT fits between the panels (the extra legend pills also make the legend taller). The ring outside the previous frame uses the same OSM snapshot, fit and thresholds as the earlier expansion. It adds 頭前溪, 鳳山溪, Shimen Reservoir and 寶山第二水庫, and shades Taipei, New Taipei and Taoyuan as the operator's land. Geography inside the previous frame is unchanged, except that fills are merged across the seam and hairline strokes on the old frame edges are removed. `initialBounds`/`initialView` are unchanged, and opening transforms were verified identical at five laptop sizes and on mobile. On 2026-10-02 the original river artwork that lay more than about 2 units off OpenStreetMap (大漢溪, 新店溪, 淡水河, 基隆河, 塭仔圳/大窠溪, 中港溪, the 貴子坑溪 and 五分港溪 creek bands, and 三重埔埤, 新庄仔埤 and 水鳥觀察區) was redrawn onto OSM with the same local fit and displacement field as the earlier water fixes, simplified at 0.3 units and painted over the untouched original paths; median offset 1.0 → 0.15 units.
- 2026-09-30 OSM audit: between Banqiao and Xinpu the Circular Line runs exactly 1 W west of the Bannan Line (the two share the corridor); the Xiaobitan branch runs 1 W west of the Songshan–Xindian Line from Qizhang to where it really diverges, then follows OSM. Far Eastern Hospital moved about 15 units south onto its platform.
- Station markers and accuracy pass (2026-10-01). Platform points are OSM platform centres (platform ways beside the route-relation stop positions, else the stops), projected with a local 10-station fit onto each line's drawn track and then corrected along the line from their OSM neighbours' spacing (fit-free), which also slid 18 circles 1.6–4.6 W along their tracks to their platforms (largest Fu Jen University 4.6 W, Sanchong Elementary School 3.8 W, Zhonghe 3.2 W, Taipei Arena 2.8 W, Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall 2.7 W; Yongning and Fu Jen University moved their track joints with them). Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Every track end at a station lies on its line's platform point; the Xiaobitan branch now starts at its own platform at Qizhang. Dates and kilometres are unchanged.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): seven circles 0.2–0.4 units beside their own line were put on it (Xindian District Office, Wanlong, Taipower Building, Zhongxiao Dunhua, Jingping, Hongshulin, Beimen). At Ximen the 2000–2014 Xiaonanmen Line uses the Songshan–Xindian platform point, the same platform, and its track starts there; the Circular Line's end at Dapinglin curves into the shared platform point. Dingpu's two terminus circles still touch, as recorded.
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): the inherited polyline sections of the Wenhu Line (54 vertices) and the Zhonghe–Xinlu and Bannan lines (12) had angular vertices of 12–30°; each is rounded with a short tangent-continuous curve (at most 0.3 units, 0.06 W, from the old line; five Wenhu circles re-snapped by at most 0.11 units). Right-angle and hairpin stubs left by end trims at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, Zhongxiao Xinsheng, Tucheng, Xinpu, Nangang, Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Dazhi, Taipei Zoo and New Taipei Industrial Park are replaced by curves that leave each platform point along the line (largest change 0.76 units, 0.19 W, on the Tamsui–Xinyi Line at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall). No angular corners or weaving remain.
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01), spec §5 rule 2 (Taipei follows the spec, not the Wikimedia reference): one shape only where the lines share track or their platforms cross in plan, one over the other. Full stacked crossings, one shape on the drawn crossing: Songjiang Nanjing (a fully underground "+" interchange, Songshan–Xindian B2 over Zhonghe–Xinlu B4) and Zhongshan (the Songshan–Xindian platform crosses under the middle of the Tamsui–Xinyi platform; OpenStreetMap footprints overlap near both platforms' middles). The cross-platform stations are separate dots too (2026-10-02; Guting is drawn as one shape because its dots are under 0.4 R apart, see Close platforms): at Dongmen, Ximen, Guting, Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and Qizhang each line runs on its own tracks beside the other (within 25° of parallel) and both use the same OpenStreetMap island platform ways, so the lines neither share track nor cross; each dot is the island's centre projected onto its own line, 0.4–0.7 R from the other and drawn overlapping, joined by a straight bridge across the island. The Xiaonanmen Line (2000–2014) shares the Songshan–Xindian track and dot at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and its platform at Ximen, so each of those two is one marker from 2000 on. Every other interchange is separate dots at the real platforms (each line's own OpenStreetMap platform) joined by a bridge: T layouts where one platform's end meets the other (Minquan West Road, where the Tamsui platform's end sits over the middle of the Zhonghe–Xinlu one, and Zhongxiao Xinsheng, 丁字型), perpendicular platforms that do not overlap in plan (Daan, Taipei Main Station, Nanjing Fuxing, Dapinglin), the Xinbeitou branch platform beside the main line at Beitou, and elevated/underground pairs on opposite sides of the road (Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center, Jingan, Touqianzhuang, Zhongxiao Fuxing).
- Close platforms (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump even fully zoomed in, so they are drawn as one shape through the same platform points, which do not move: Guting (Songshan–Xindian and Zhonghe–Xinlu, 0.37 R). Pairs 0.4 R or more apart stay separate dots.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), tracks. Every track was compared again with its OSM route relations through the local station fit (the frame the tracks and platforms use). Five stretches more than about 1 W off were redrawn onto the mapped course: the Wenhu Line beside Dahu lake (up to 4.5 units; it ran over the lake edge, while the viaduct is about 20 m from the shore), the Airport MRT past Beimen (5.1) and between Sanchong and Xinzhuang Fuduxin (4.0; the A3 circle re-derived 2.6 units onto the corrected track at its OSM platform, its connector following), the Circular Line from Xingfu through Touqianzhuang to the Dahan River bridge (5.8; the Touqianzhuang Circular Line platform re-derived 3.75 units west onto the corrected track) and the Xiaobitan branch curve (4.9). Side-by-side runs now touch exactly, one track width apart (their real tunnels are 10–20 m apart), instead of leaving a hairline background gap or a partial overlap: the Songshan–Xindian and Bannan lines north of Ximen, the Songshan–Xindian and Zhonghe–Xinlu lines south of Guting, and the Zhonghe–Xinlu and Tamsui–Xinyi lines from the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall curve through Dongmen (the Dongmen Zhonghe–Xinlu platform and its 2012–2013 circle re-derived 0.32 units onto the track, so the dots stay separate, 0.65 R apart). The 561 remaining polyline vertices of 3–12° on 20 tracks were rounded with short tangent-continuous curves (at most 0.18 units from the old line); no corner above 3° remains. Kilometres, dates and segmentation are unchanged.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), geography frame. The 2026-10-02 realignment drew OpenStreetMap water through fit_ext plus a displacement field fitted to the original artwork (up to 21 units, locally stretching by more than 100 %), so where the artwork was off the redrawn rivers kept part of its offset; the network itself is drawn in a different frame (the local station fit, median 3–4 units from fit_ext). Measured against OSM relative to the network (crossing positions between consecutive stations, track-to-bank clearance and station-to-water distance), the geography was up to 10 units off at river crossings (景美溪 at Muzha 10.2, 基隆河 at Nangang Software Park – Donghu 8.5, 大漢溪 at Touqianzhuang 8.3, 新店溪 at Jiangzicui 7.9, 基隆河 at Dazhi 7.3). The whole geography layer (artwork, earlier fixes, the extension and the clip outline alike, so every seam is kept) was moved by one smooth field into the network frame: a moving-least-squares similarity fit (650 m Gaussian) on the 142 station control points, tapered to zero 100–350 units from the tracks and 250–500 units from the stations and smoothed over 30 units. Crossings are now within 5.2 units (most within 2.5), the 90th-percentile track-to-bank error fell from 7.1 to 3.6 units, the median station-to-water error from 5.0 to 3.5, and no station dot touches water. A smooth translation-only field and a raw nearest-station affine field were tried and rejected (worse clearances or local kinks).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), geography fixes. Removed five pieces of artwork water with no mapped water: two wedges near the 塭仔圳 mouth (Luzhou), a blob in the 大漢溪 floodplain at Tucheng and a creek-mouth wedge beside it, a tongue on the 新店溪 west bank opposite Xindian, and a sliver under the 淡水河 bank at the old top edge. 塭仔圳 no longer stops abruptly where the artwork ended (y 1468): its mapped channel continues into 大窠溪 ([r5145474](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5145474)), 大窠溪 continues upstream as a 3-unit centreline band to the end of the mapped way past the old west edge, and 中港大排, the 40–50 m open drainage channel the Airport MRT crosses between New Taipei Industrial Park and Xinzhuang Fuduxin, is drawn from its mapped areas. The 基隆河 and the 景美溪 band are redrawn across the old right canvas edge, removing 1–3 unit steps between the artwork and the extension. Smaller mapped channels with banks that the artwork never drew (五重溪, 塔寮坑溪, 磺溪 at Mingde) are still left out, as are the riverside wetland ponds.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), checked and left. Station platform points were rechecked against a leave-one-out local fit: the largest differences are at termini (Tamsui, Xinbeitou) and where OSM gives one point for several platforms (Taipei Main Station, Nanjing Fuxing), so the platform points set by the 2026-10-01 pass stay. Interchange shapes follow the shapes bullet below (no two shapes of one marker are closer than 0.4 R). No opening, closure or rename up to 2026-10-02 is missing: Taoyuan Metro's Green Line first phase (Kengkou – Arts District, 7 stations) still targets the end of 2026 ([Business Today, 7 July 2026](https://www.businesstoday.com.tw/article/category/183030/post/202607070009/); [UDN](https://udn.com/news/story/7324/9654110)), and the Wanda Line's first phase the end of 2027 ([Storm Media](https://www.storm.mg/lifestyle/11134464)).

## Singapore (`singapore`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/singapore/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/singapore/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/singapore/map.svg).

### Primary records and other focused references

- [LTA: Rail Network][p-sg-network] — **New**. Official network map, line inventory, names and interchanges; current layout does not establish historic opening dates.
- [LTA: Downtown Line][p-sg-dtl] — **New**. Stages 1–3, Hume opening and published lengths; distinguish complete project lengths from operating sections.
- [LTA: Thomson-East Coast Line][p-sg-tel] — **New**. Opening stages, deferred stations and planned extensions; lists Stage 4 opening 23 June 2024.
- [LTA: Sengkang–Punggol LRT][p-sg-splrt] — **New**. Network layout and system-level opening years, not every later infill station day.
- [SBS Transit: Ridership][p-sg-sbs] — **New**. Operator states Sengkang LRT opened 18 January 2003 and Punggol LRT 29 January 2005.
- [National Library Board: Woodlands MRT station][p-sg-woodlands] — **New**. Historical account with primary newspaper and government references for the Woodlands extension.
- [SMRT operations review 2020: milestones][p-sg-smrt] — **New**. Operator historical milestones; useful corroboration of early network stages, not every exact date.
- [LTA: Punggol Coast to open for passenger service][p-sg-punggol] — **New**. 10 December 2024 opening and North East Line extension.
- [LTA: Circle Line 6][p-sg-ccl6] — **New**. Three new stations, closed loop, passenger opening 12 July 2026; links the separate 4 July preview notice (the preview is the date used for the new stations, spec §7).
- [LTA newsroom: Circle Line 6 notices][p-sg-ccl6-preview] — **New**. 14 May 2026 notice explicitly distinguishes 4 July public preview from 12 July passenger service; exact article should replace this index link when available.
- [LTA annual report 2024/25][p-sg-report-2025] — **New**. Recent network milestones, including Teck Lee LRT opening; simplified LRT markers intentionally omit most intermediate stops.
- [SGTrains: Circle Line Stage 6 to open on 12 July 2026, public preview on 4 July](https://blog.sgtrains.com/2026/05/) and [SGTrains, July 2026](https://blog.sgtrains.com/2026/07/) — **New** (secondary, 2026-10-03). Corroborate the 2026-07-04 preview and 2026-07-12 opening. The same blog's [September 2026](https://blog.sgtrains.com/2026/09/) posts and the Downtown Line integration-test notice (early closures 10 July – 5 September 2026) still give the Downtown Line extension (Xilin, Sungei Bedok) and Thomson–East Coast Line Stage 5 (Bedok South, Sungei Bedok) as opening in the second half of 2026: neither had opened by 2026-10-02, so neither is drawn; add them (with their public preview, if any) when they open. Mount Pleasant (TE10) remains unopened; the Bukit Panjang LRT closures of 20 and 27 September 2026 (renewal works) are temporary and not drawn.

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Exact upstream SVG revision/author has not been recovered. LTA’s official network maps substantiate station names and connectivity, but they are schematic and do not certify geographic coordinates. The inherited artwork is geographic: its coastline matches the OpenStreetMap coastline through one affine transform (Web Mercator to SVG, fitted by ICP on the coastline strokes; median 0.19 units, p90 0.93 units inside the original canvas, at 211.5 units/km), and stations and tracks were checked against OSM through the same transform (2026-10-03 audit below). Away from the shared corridors the railway was drawn about 0.5–1 W (30–60 m) off its real course in places; offsets up to about 1.2 W that are smooth and consistent are left as drawn.

- Use LTA’s line pages for operating length and stage maps, plus the station tables below for opening chronology. Do not count planned TEL stations merely because they appear on a project map.
- Bukit Panjang, Sengkang and Punggol LRT are marked `simplified` in the legend and use simplified track coverage. Intermediate stop openings are not all separate markers/events; this is a scope choice, not evidence those stops never existed. The Bukit Panjang LRT is drawn without the Ten Mile Junction spur (closed 13 January 2019), so that closure is not a map change. Near the Sengkang, Punggol and Bukit Panjang hubs the loops are drawn up to about 2–2.7 W off their real course so that they meet the heavy-rail markers (spec §8).
- Document line-total rounding and branch accounting before treating section `data-km` as precise engineering measurements. The completed Circle Line’s ring and Marina Bay spur need consistent treatment. Geometry corrections do not change `data-km` (published lengths; spec §4).
- Cartographic adjustment (present before the 2026-09-26 audit): around Outram Park, Chinatown and Tanjong Pagar the East–West, North East, Circle, Downtown and Thomson–East Coast tracks were re-routed locally, seven circles moved (Chinatown by about 16 units) and the Outram Park markers made more compact. Dates, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged; it is a drawing change, not a relocation. The 2026-09-30 OSM audit moved Chinatown's Downtown Line point about 25 units east onto the Downtown Line platform; the two platforms are separate dots joined by a bridge.
- 2026-09-30 OSM audit (route relations, platform ways, stop positions): Pasir Ris, Punggol Coast and Bayshore termini were extended or retraced along OSM onto their platforms; Hume, Downtown and Tanjong Rhu slid along their tracks onto their platforms. Between Promenade and Bayfront the Downtown Line runs 1 W west of the Circle Line, touching it (they share the corridor), with a dot on each line at Promenade and Bayfront; the Changi Airport branch leaves the East–West main line at a branch junction where the real tracks diverge, about 11 W east of Tanah Merah, and then follows OSM to Expo. (The Tuas Link offset noted then was corrected on 2026-10-03; Pasir Ris and Punggol Coast were refined again then.)
- Station markers and accuracy pass (2026-10-01). Interchange platform points are OSM platform centres (platform ways beside the route-relation stop positions, else the stops) projected with a local 10-station fit onto each line's drawn track; there is no line-map reference, so composition follows the platform layout; which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Bishan's bridge follows the OSM walkway with one bend. Earlier single-line circles sit on their line's dot (up to 16 units at Paya Lebar and Serangoon). Five stations slid along their tracks to their platforms, all confirmed by fit-free neighbour checks: Gardens by the Bay 2.7 W (the 2022–24 terminus joint with it), Canberra 2.7 W, Marine Parade 2.4 W, Tampines (East–West) 2.3 W and Tanjong Katong 1.8 W. Every track end at a station lies on its line's platform point (Marina Bay 1989–2014 North–South terminus, Promenade, Dhoby Ghaut, Bugis, Expo, Stevens, Caldecott joints). The local station fit absorbs systematic errors of the drawn network (it hid Tuas Link's 10.9 W overshoot); the 2026-10-03 audit rechecked every station through the geography's own transform.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): at Promenade the Circle Line platform is the junction of its three tracks, with the Downtown Line opposite, so the Circle Line no longer doubles back into the marker; Promenade, HarbourFront and Caldecott are two platform dots joined by a bridge (see the interchange shapes bullet for every station). Outram Park's East–West point is the same in every period, so the 1987 track starts on it.
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): the East–West Line joint at Gul Circle, the Circle Line joint at Keppel and the three-way Circle Line junction at Promenade (Nicoll Highway, Marina Bay and Dhoby Ghaut tracks) had right-angle stubs left by end trims; each track now leaves the platform point along a common tangent (the through pair at Promenade), with changes of at most 1.9 units (0.16 W, at Promenade). No angular corners or weaving remain.
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01), spec §5 rule 2 (no README reference map for Singapore): one shape only where the lines share track or their platforms cross in plan, one over the other. The only full stacked crossing is Little India, one circle on the drawn crossing (the Downtown line passes under the North East line inside both stations; OpenStreetMap tracks cross 13–19 m from both stops). No Singapore interchange shares track. Every other interchange is separate dots at the real platforms joined by a bridge: the cross-platform pairs on their own tracks (City Hall, Raffles Place and Jurong East on the North–South/East–West lines, Bayfront on the Circle/Downtown lines), Promenade (the Downtown platforms run parallel beneath the Circle line station), T and L layouts where one station meets the end of the other (MacPherson, Stevens, and Expo, whose Downtown station lies beyond the end of the East–West platforms; its East–West dot and 2001–17 circle now sit on that platform, about 115 m south-west of the old point), and the stations joined by linkways or transfer halls (Bishan, Orchard, Dhoby Ghaut, Outram Park, Buona Vista, Marina Bay, Paya Lebar, Bugis, Woodlands, HarbourFront, Chinatown, Serangoon, Caldecott, Botanic Gardens). No two separate shapes are closer than 0.4 R (the closest are MacPherson 0.59 R, HarbourFront 0.63 R since 2026-10-03, Bayfront 0.65 R and Promenade 0.72 R), so the close-shape exception merges none.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): the Circle Line opening of 2010-04-04 (three pieces) grows as one path. 12 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.
- Stations, final audit (2026-10-03). Every platform point was compared with OSM (platform ways beside the line's own track, else the route stop positions, with the station area as a cross-check) through the coastline transform; the median along-track error was 0.3 W. Dots more than about 1 W from the platform centre were moved along their own track onto it: **Tuas Link** sat 10.9 W (about 620 m) beyond its platform at the end of the depot tracks, so the dot and the 2017 terminus moved back onto the platform and the track no longer runs on towards the depot; Prince Edward Road 1.7 W, Cantonment 1.6 W, Springleaf 1.5 W, one-north 1.5 W, Kallang 1.4 W, Rochor 1.4 W, Ang Mo Kio 1.3 W (its platform ways) and Great World 1.0 W slid along their tracks; Clementi moved 1.7 W south-east onto its platform ways, with the 1988 terminus joint of the two East–West tracks (geometry unchanged); Punggol Coast (1.4 W) and Bukit Panjang's Downtown Line terminus (1.4 W, to the OSM station-box centre because its stops sit at the crossover end; the Bukit Panjang LRT's hook that meets the marker follows it) were trimmed back, and Woodlands North (2.4 W) and Pasir Ris (1.3 W, its platform ways) extended straight on to their platforms. The Newton out-of-station pair moved only as far as the 2R stagger allows (the circles now touch where the lines cross; each is about 0.95 W from its platform). Left as drawn: Promenade's Circle Line point (1.1 W from its stops, the junction of three tracks), Bishan's Circle Line (platform ways and stops disagree), Upper Thomson and Bright Hill (1.0 W from the stops, the station areas disagree).
- Tracks, final audit (2026-10-03). Tracks were compared with the OSM route ways through the same transform. Retraced onto their real courses (smoothed OSM centrelines, tangent-continuous where they rejoin the old drawing), with the stations on them re-projected onto the corrected track at their real platforms: Circle Line Labrador Park – Telok Blangah (was up to 1.8 W north); Circle Line Cantonment – Keppel – HarbourFront (up to 1.6 W south), now touching the North East Line where the real tunnels run side by side, with the North East Line's last stretch into HarbourFront beside it, so the HarbourFront dots are 12 units apart (0.63 R) instead of 26; North East Line Hougang – Kovan and Serangoon – Woodleigh – Potong Pasir – Boon Keng (up to 1.5 W west); North–South Line Bukit Batok – Bukit Gombak (1.4 W); Downtown Line Telok Ayer – Chinatown – Fort Canning across the Chinatown joint (1.5 W) and Hume – Hillview – Cashew (1.3 W). The joints at Choa Chu Kang (4.5°) and Tanah Merah (4.3°) are now tangent-continuous. Larger offsets that remain are the side-by-side convention (North–South/East–West between City Hall and Raffles Place, Downtown/Circle between Promenade and Bayfront, Jurong East, Outram Park), plus smooth artwork offsets of about 1 W (the North–South Line between Bishan and Orchard, the Circle Line round Tai Seng and Dakota, the Thomson–East Coast bend at Tanjong Rhu). Checked and left: the Circle and Thomson–East Coast lines north of Caldecott cross at a shallow angle (real); the North–South/East–West gap just north of Raffles Place (0.2–3.7 units, under the dots) and the 0.05–0.2-unit gap between the Downtown and Circle lines south of Promenade are below a pixel at the app's maximum zoom.
- Geography, final audit (2026-10-03). The artwork's land and sea were compared with the OSM coastline (Overpass, 2 October 2026) and OSM water areas through the coastline transform. Land reclaimed since the artwork was drawn is now painted as land in a `coast-fixes` group above the preserved artwork (the original paths are untouched): each patch is filled in the land colour of its side of the border (Singapore `#f6f6f3`, Johor and the Riau Islands `#eceeef`), the artwork's old shoreline under it is covered by a non-scaling stroke in the same colour, and the new shoreline is the OSM coastline with the usual `#c0cfd9` stroke. Patched: the Tuas Port reclamation (land and basins), the Tuas west coast, Changi East, Pulau Tekong's polders and south-east reclamation (their ponds and drains stay water), small reclaimed areas on Jurong Island and at Pasir Panjang; in Johor the Forest City islands and the Tanjung Kupang – Gelang Patah coast, the Johor Bahru waterfront island, Pasir Gudang and the coast at Pengerang and the Sungai Johor mouth; three reclamations on Batam; eight small places where the artwork's land lay in the OSM sea (Changi coast, Johor). The old horizontal canvas-edge notch on the Johor coast west of Woodlands is gone with them. Poyan Reservoir's eastern arm, behind its dam, was missing and is drawn. Not patched: river widths that differ from OSM (Sungei Kranji/Kadut, Sungei Serangoon and several Johor rivers), Johor mangrove channels and a Batam aquaculture area, which the artwork simplifies; small ponds and quarries below the lake threshold; reservoirs that sit 5–10 units off their OSM outline (MacRitchie, Lower Peirce, Jurong Lake, Serangoon). No station sits in water. The background is present-day geography throughout playback, so reclamation completed after a date (for example Tuas Port) is drawn on every date.

<a id="tokyo"></a>

## Tokyo — Metro / Toei (`tokyo`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/tokyo/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/tokyo/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/tokyo/map.svg).

Scope: Tokyo Metro and Toei and their predecessors, including Toei's Toden Arakawa Line and Nippori–Toneri Liner (both tracks only); JR and private railways appear on the subway map only as connections and are excluded (spec §8). The Arakawa Line's Oji Electric Tramway predecessor starts the timeline on 1911-08-20, so the slider starts in 1911. The same company's Akabane branch (Toden route 27 north of Oji-ekimae) is drawn from 1932-12-01, the day it was linked to the network, until it closed on 1972-11-12. The header shows both the Tokyo Metro and Toei logos; station tooltips use `metro` and `toei` (alt text "Toei", also used for Toden and Liner stops). Eidan's 2004 corporatisation as Tokyo Metro is a rename, not a handover, and is not modelled (spec §5). The Ueno Zoo Monorail (Toei, 1957-12-17 to 2019-11-01, 0.3 km inside Ueno Zoo) is left out: it had no connection to the rest of the network and would only appear as an isolated fleck.

### Primary records and other focused references

- [Tokyo Metro: corporate history (Japanese)][p-ty-metro-history] — **New**. Primary opening milestones and corporate chronology; company establishment 4 July 1941 is distinct from operating takeover 1 September.
- [Tokyo Metro: corporate history (English)][p-ty-metro-en] — **New**. English cross-check for principal openings and English line nomenclature.
- [Toei: subway history][p-ty-toei] — **New**. Detailed primary chronology for all four Toei lines, extensions, line names and station renames.
- [Toei Asakusa Line 60th anniversary][p-ty-asakusa60] — **New**. Historical opening stages and station names, supplementing the operator chronology.
- [Tokyo Metro corporate profile][p-ty-profile] — **New**. Current station counts and operating lengths; branch/shared-track accounting requires care.
- [Toei business plan 2025: current network][p-ty-toei-profile] — **New**. Operator line lengths and station inventory; not historical segment measurements.
- [Tokyo Metro: historical Ginza platforms][p-ty-platforms] — **Recovered**. Original Ginza Line platform context; supports historical arrangement, not exact coordinates of every drawn old platform.
- [Tokyo Metro: Shibuya station relocation plan][p-ty-shibuya] — **Recovered**. 2020 Ginza platform relocation and station layout.
- [Toei: Toden Arakawa Line history][p-ty-toden-ayumi] — **New**. Operator chronology: Oji Electric Tramway's 1911-08-20 Asukayama-ue – Otsuka opening, full route 1930-03-30, 1942-02-01 integration into Tokyo City, routes 27/32 combined and renamed Arakawa Line 1974-10-01, nickname 2017-04-28.
- [Toei: Nippori–Toneri Liner history][p-ty-nt-ayumi] — **New**. Opening 2008-03-30 (Nippori – Minumadai-shinsuikoen).
- [Toei: Liner opening date announced (2007)][p-ty-nt-open] — **New**. Press release fixing the 30 March 2008 opening.
- [Toei: Arakawa Line nickname decided (2017-04-28)][p-ty-sakura] — **New**. Japanese 東京さくらトラム, English "Tokyo Sakura Tram", to be used from the announcement.
- [Toei: Toden stop pages][p-ty-toden-stops] and [Toei: Liner station pages][p-ty-nt-stops] — **New**. The "乗換え案内" section of each page is the transfer test for §8: Minowabashi (Minowa), Machiya-ekimae (Machiya), Oji-ekimae (Oji), Shin-koshinzuka (Nishi-sugamo), Higashi-ikebukuro-yonchome (Higashi-ikebukuro), Kishibojimmae (Zoshigaya) and Liner Nishi-nippori (Chiyoda Line). Toden-Zoshigaya, Waseda and Otsuka-ekimae list no Metro/Toei transfer.
- [Eidan SUBWAY NEWS 2000-16 (2000-11-15), annex 1](https://web.archive.org/web/2001/http://www.tokyometro.go.jp/news/2000-1601.html) (primary: the 16 Eidan–Toei transfer stations before 2000-12-12 and the 11 added that day) — **New (2026-10-03)**. Dates the Eidan–Toei out-of-station transfers: Korakuen ⇔ Kasuga is one of the 11 added on 2000-12-12, not a 1972 transfer. Its pre-2000 list of 16 matches every other Metro–Toei connector on the map.
- [Tokyo Metro FAQ: stations where you exit the gates to transfer][p-ty-metro-faq204] — **New**. 2022-08-25 list of Tokyo Metro exit-gate transfers (Ueno, Mitsukoshimae, Otemachi, Ikebukuro, Iidabashi, Shibuya Ginza–Fukutoshin, Shinjuku-sanchome and the differently named pairs). At Shinjuku-sanchome, Otemachi and Ikebukuro (Marunouchi–Fukutoshin) an exit transfer is optional beside an in-gate route; the list covers no Toei transfers.

Toei's subway chronology records line names only on 1978-07-01 (Lines 1, 6 and 10 become Asakusa, Mita and Shinjuku) and 2000-04-20 (Line 12 becomes Oedo). The earlier "Toei Asakusa/Mita/Shinjuku Line → Asakusa/Mita/Shinjuku Line" renames on 2000-04-20 had no source and were removed on 2026-09-26; the unprefixed names match Toei's English line list and the Tokyo Metro names.

The Arakawa Line had no line name before 1974. Following the Ginza Line's "Tokyo Underground Railway → Eidan Subway" precedent, its legend names the operator of each period: Oji Electric Tramway (to 1942-02-01), Tokyo City Tram (to 1943-07-01, the metropolis system) and Toden (to 1974-10-01). Toden route numbers 27 (Minowabashi–Akabane) and 32 (Arakawa-shakomae–Waseda) are not used as names, because their start dates are unverified and both ran over Arakawa-shakomae–Oji-ekimae. The 2017-04-28 nickname "Tokyo Sakura Tram" is treated as a rename, like Oshiage (SKYTREE).

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Recovered original artwork: [Tokyo Subway Linemap en.svg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tokyo_Subway_Linemap_en.svg), Yveltal, CC BY-SA 4.0; the source used was the June 2020 map. Keep its file-history attribution rather than substituting a similarly named Tokyo map. Only Tokyo Metro/Toei and their predecessors are in scope; faded private/JR connecting railways in the supplied map were excluded.

- Recovered alignment comparisons: [Ginza](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/8026074), [Yurakucho](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/443269), [Fukutoshin](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/5375678), [Hanzomon](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/443279), [Namboku](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/7730199), [Mita](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/443286), [Oedo](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3355612).
- Smoothing and shorter interchange symbols intentionally move local control points/markers slightly. These are cartographic edits, not track relocation events. The latest pass (present before the 2026-09-26 audit) smoothed 26 central track sections around Otemachi, Kasumigaseki, Hibiya, Toranomon, Shimbashi, Mitsukoshimae and Nihombashi, moved 17 circles by up to about 3 units and shortened or re-angled 8 capsules; its four walking connectors were then straightened back to single segments (spec §5). Dates and `data-km` are unchanged. Modern OSM cannot prove historic Manseibashi, Shimbashi, Omotesando or pre-2020 Shibuya platform coordinates.
- Geometry scan (2026-09-29): the Fukutoshin Line track between Senkawa and Kanamecho (1994-12-07 section) had a spike and crossed itself at a bend; it is rebuilt as a smooth curve; since 2026-10-01 it runs 1 W beside the Yurakucho Line around their OSM centreline. The Mita Line's Meguro end had a hook bulging beside the station marker; it now curves straight into it. Track ends are unchanged.
- Shibuya (Ginza Line), 2026-09-29: both Ginza markers and the tracks west of Omote-sando were moved to OSM (current platform way 759134298; pre-2020 platforms from OSM data at 2019-10-01, the 玉電ビル/東横店西館 3F over the JR station, 119 m west of the new one). The old circle is 18 m from its platform centre. The new platform lies above the Fukutoshin platform, inside the Hanzomon/Fukutoshin marker, so its circle sits 96 m east of the platform centre, clear of that marker (spec §5 out-of-station spacing). The 1938–2020 stub crosses under the Hanzomon/Fukutoshin marker, as the line crossed Meiji-dori above the Fukutoshin station. Tracks follow OSM within 4 m.
- Nihombashi: the Asakusa Line station (Edobashi until 1989-03-19) is south of the Edobashi-itchome crossing, reached from the Tozai Line's Edobashi-itchome gate by a public connecting passage (ja.wikipedia 日本橋駅). The 1989 rename only unified the name, so it stays a separate circle with a connector renamed Nihombashi; its marker is now at the platform centre, on the Tozai track, where that line runs.
- OSM position audit, rest of network (2026-09-30; route relations, platform ways and stop positions, local and whole-network fits, markers >1.5 W and tracks >2 W): tracks redrawn along OSM on the Honancho branch (up to 4 W off), the Namboku/Mita approach to Meguro (4.2 W), the Asakusa Line into Oshiage (2–3 W), the Yurakucho Line Kojimachi–Nagatacho (2.1 W) and at Ikebukuro (Yurakucho and Fukutoshin platforms; the 1983 approach had joined east of the station), and the Fukutoshin Line south of Ikebukuro. Lines drawn on top of one another now run 1 W apart around the OSM centre of their shared corridor: Ginza/Hanzomon Shibuya–Akasaka-mitsuke, Shinjuku/Hanzomon Kudanshita–Jimbocho, Asakusa/Hanzomon at Ningyocho, and (from 2026-10-01) Yurakucho/Fukutoshin Wakoshi–Kanamecho; they cross once where they really cross. Interchange platform points were re-measured on OSM platforms (see the 2026-10-01 "Station markers" bullet). Eighteen circles slid 3.8–11.6 units along their tracks to their platform centres (Toranomon Hills, Tochomae, Nishi-magome, Shiodome, Nishidai, Yoyogi-koen, Sengoku and others). Where real platforms coincide, circles just touch at the nearest positions within about 1.1 W (Ueno Ginza/Hibiya; the pre-2013 Kudanshita circles), and Ueno-hirokoji/Ueno-okachimachi and Awajicho/Ogawamachi keep their touching arrangement, so their connectors cross the third circle. Dates, labels, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged.
- Toei–Tokyo Metro interchanges (rule applied 2026-09-29): Toei and Tokyo Metro are separate fare systems, so every transfer between them passes gates, except where platforms are shared (Meguro, Shirokanedai, Shirokane-takanawa, Kudanshita from 2013). Passing gates therefore does not decide the marker; the real platform geometry does, as with Longyang Road (§6). A station drawn from real OSM platform points stays one interchange marker where the platforms are stacked, side by side or directly adjacent, so that circles at their real positions would overlap or just touch: Aoyama-itchome, Oshiage, Ningyocho, Higashi-ginza, Roppongi, Monzen-nakacho, Jimbocho, Tsukishima, Sumiyoshi, Higashi-shinjuku and Kiyosumi-shirakawa (under about 150 m, ≤ 2.75 r). It is drawn as separate circles with a walking connector where the platforms are about 150 m or more apart in separate structures, so that a single marker would need a long bridge: Asakusa (200 m), Shimbashi (207 m), Otemachi Mita Line (257–420 m), Shinjuku-sanchome Shinjuku Line (211–237 m), Nakano-sakaue (163 m), Hibiya Mita Line (221–308 m), Iidabashi Oedo Line (249–307 m), Ichigaya Shinjuku Line (131 m to the Yurakucho Line, 213 m to the Namboku Line) and Azabu-juban (173 m). Nihombashi (formerly Edobashi) is a connector for the same reason. Each connector dates from the day the operators designated the transfer, normally the day the pair first existed, and is noted in that day's events. Korakuen – Kasuga is the exception: Eidan added it to its Eidan–Toei transfer list only on 2000-12-12 (SUBWAY NEWS 2000-16, annex 1), so its 1972 and 1996 connectors were removed on 2026-10-03. Metro-only in-gate pairs stay one interchange marker (Otemachi, Shinjuku-sanchome Marunouchi–Fukutoshin, Ichigaya Yurakucho–Namboku, Iidabashi Yurakucho–Namboku). Kudanshita keeps its recorded history. Distances are between OSM platform centres (stop positions by line ref and platform ways, 2026-09-29), converted with local 12-station fits.
- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: platform points from OSM platform ways and stop positions by line ref, projected with leave-one-out 12-station local fits; bridges follow OSM footways and corridors where these leave the straight line by more than 1 W (at least 88% of each bridge's length within 1 W of a mapped walkway). Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. The same audit redrew ten track stretches 1.5–2.3 W off OSM (Hanzomon Jimbocho–Mitsukoshimae, the Honancho branch junction, Tozai Nakano–Ochiai and others), moved Nakai, Nakano-shimbashi, Togoshi, Shinjuku-nishiguchi, Yushima and Kita-senju's Hibiya platform onto their platforms, and put every track end on its platform point. The Yurakucho and Fukutoshin lines, which share one pair of tracks from Wakoshi to Kotake-mukaihara and run in stacked tunnels on to Kanamecho, are drawn 1 W apart centred on the OSM shared track (up to 2.5 W off before), as the Wikimedia map draws them.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): Tochomae sits on the Nerima–Shinjuku track it has served since 1997 (it was 0.87 units off), and the 2000 loop track ends on it. The Yurakucho/Fukutoshin pair stays 1 W apart from Kanamecho to their crossing near Ikebukuro, as OSM shows, each ending on its own Ikebukuro station (replacing S-bends east of Kanamecho). Separate stations that still touch at their real positions: Hongo-sanchome, Korakuen/Kasuga, Ichigaya and Kudanshita 2013–2020, besides the recorded Ueno, Awajicho/Ogawamachi, pre-2013 Kudanshita and Shibuya arrangements. Ichigaya (Namboku/Yurakucho, from 1996) is two dots joined by a bridge, as in the reference map: the platforms are separate, linked by a passage, so they are not drawn as one shared-platform blob.
- Smoothness pass: Eight angular vertices (13–36°) were made tangent-continuous, each keeping its station point on the track: the Ginza near Ueno-hirokoji, the Asakusa near Asakusa and at Ningyocho, the Hibiya near Hibiya, the Asakusa at Mita, the Oedo at Tochomae/Shinjuku, and the Fukutoshin at Shinjuku-sanchome. The Oedo loop now curves onto Tochomae instead of ending in a 0.9-unit hook. Between Takebashi and Otemachi the Tozai runs 1 W west of the Hanzomon, where OSM puts the two in one corridor, and crosses it once instead of twice.
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01, spec §5 rule 1, reference map): the README's Wikimedia Tokyo subway line map (Tokyo_Subway_Linemap_en, June 2020) sets the composition at every station it shows. Every interchange was checked against that map: its 291 white station dots were measured against its line centrelines, and each station was checked by eye on a crop. Platforms stay at their real OpenStreetMap positions, so separate dots may overlap. No station or line is newer than the reference, so rule 2 is not used. **One shape** only where the reference draws one dot:
  - Shared track: the eight Yurakucho/Fukutoshin stations from Wakoshi to Kanamecho, and Meguro, Shirokanedai and Shirokane-takanawa (Namboku/Mita).
  - Reference one shape: Akasaka-mitsuke (Ginza/Marunouchi cross-platform) and Sumiyoshi (one circle on the crossing). Ginza/Hanzomon at Aoyama-itchome and Omote-sando, and Shinjuku/Hanzomon at Kudanshita (from 2013), are each one pill. Jimbocho (2026-10-03) is separate dots although the reference draws one pill: its Shinjuku platform (B1, east) and Hanzomon platform (B3, west, under the Shinjuku tracks) lie end to end, the station is about 375 m from end to end and the transfer passes through the gate level (ja.wikipedia 神保町駅), so the pill ran 2.0 R along the line (spec §5 rule 2: a shape never runs along a line between platforms apart along it). The Hanzomon and Shinjuku dots are joined by a bridge, and the Mita dot keeps its bridge to the Shinjuku one.
  - Everything else is separate dots joined by bridges, as the reference draws them. This includes the crossing line at Kudanshita from 2020 (Tozai) and Jimbocho (Mita). It also includes the touching or overlapping pairs Nihombashi, Higashi-ginza, Monzen-nakacho, Tsukishima, Ningyocho, Morishita, Shibuya (Hanzomon/Fukutoshin), Kayabacho and Daimon. The remaining interchanges are separate as well: Ginza, Otemachi, Kasumigaseki, Kokkai-gijidomae, Tameike-sanno, Nagatacho, Korakuen, Kasuga, Yotsuya, Ichigaya, Ikebukuro, Shinjuku-sanchome, Meiji-jingumae, Higashi-shinjuku, Shinjuku, Roppongi, Hibiya, Mita, Oshiage, Kiyosumi-shirakawa and Kita-senju.
  - Drawing exception (spec §5 rule 3, applied 2026-10-02): separate shapes whose nearest points are closer than 0.4 R read as a lump, so they are one shape through the same real platform points (nothing moves): Aoyama-itchome (the Oedo dot 0.11 R from the Ginza/Hanzomon pill, from 2000), Omote-sando (Chiyoda, 0.31 R) and Iidabashi (Yurakucho/Namboku, 0.26 R). Monzen-nakacho (0.46 R) stays two overlapping dots.
  - No platform is snapped to a crossing point or a corridor centre any more (the earlier crossing circles at Nihombashi, Higashi-ginza, Monzen-nakacho and Tsukishima, and the corridor placements at Aoyama-itchome and Omote-sando, are undone). The only exception is Sumiyoshi, which the reference draws as one circle.
- Final audit (2026-10-03). Station dots stay at their real platforms projected onto their own tracks; tracks follow OSM. Checks: OSM route ways, platform ways and stop positions projected with leave-one-out 12-station local fits (median platform residual 1.36 units); every interchange rendered at full and app-maximum zoom (rsvg and Chromium).
  - **Side by side, exactly.** Where two lines share a corridor they now touch exactly, centre distance 1 W, instead of leaving hairline gaps (up to 0.6 units) or partial overlaps (up to 1.4 units). Each fix moved only the later line, within 1.2 units, onto the exact offset of the other, with smooth tangent-continuous blends. Platform points on the moved line were re-projected onto it at the same platforms. The corridors:
    - Yurakucho/Fukutoshin, Wakoshi – Kanamecho
    - Shinjuku/Hanzomon, Kudanshita – Jimbocho
    - Chiyoda/Mita, Otemachi – Hibiya – Uchisaiwaicho
    - Namboku/Mita, Shirokane-takanawa – Meguro
    - Ginza/Hanzomon, Shibuya – Akasaka-mitsuke
    - Ginza/Marunouchi at Akasaka-mitsuke
    - Marunouchi/Chiyoda at Kokkai-gijidomae
    - Tozai/Oedo and Namboku/Oedo at Iidabashi
    - Marunouchi/Oedo, Hongo-sanchome – Kasuga
    - Yurakucho/Namboku, Ichigaya – Iidabashi
    - the tram beside the Fukutoshin at Zoshigaya
  - **Mita Line bulge.** Between Otemachi and Hibiya the Mita Line bowed up to 5.2 units (1.7 W) away from the Chiyoda Line at Nijubashimae, apparently for clearance. OSM puts both lines under Hibiya-dori, so the Mita now runs beside the Chiyoda there. The Nijubashimae dot overlaps it, as the real platform does (spec §5 placement).
  - **Jogs at stations.** Two tracks had been bent to reach their platform point; both are straight again and the platform re-projected: the Chiyoda Line at Otemachi (an S-jog of about 1 unit) and the Asakusa Line at Ningyocho (up to 2.6 units off OSM; the dot moved 1.1 units toward its OSM platform). The Shinjuku Line terminus at Shinjuku was 8 units (about 115 m) east of its real platform, OSM way 670952109, the Keio New Line platform. It now ends at the platform centre, west of the Oedo platform it crosses over, and the 1980–1997 circle moved with it. The Shinjuku Line and Oedo dots now overlap (0.83 R apart) and stay separate.
  - **Joints and corners.** Every track piece now meets the next tangent-continuously. Nine corners at station joints were removed: Mitsukoshimae (Hanzomon) 14.4°, Kasumigaseki (Marunouchi 12.8°, Chiyoda 8.3°), Ikebukuro (Yurakucho 8.0°, Fukutoshin 5.8°), Aoyama-itchome (Hanzomon) 3.0°, and under 2° at Tokyo, Ginza and Takadanobaba. 118 corners inside paths were smoothed: 46 on the Liner's polyline (up to 31°), 11.7° on the Oedo Line near Monzen-nakacho and on the Chiyoda Line at Yoyogi-uehara, and smaller ones elsewhere. Four zero-length or near-zero segments were dropped. The 1.3° corner on the 1939 Toranomon – Shimbashi piece is kept so that its 1939-09-16 handover stays exact. Faint seams across a track at some butt-cap joints, for example the Tozai Line at Kudanshita, appear in rsvg renders with exact, tangent-continuous geometry and do not show in Chromium. They are a renderer artefact.
  - **Geography.** A sea-coloured strip now covers the anti-aliased seam along the old bottom canvas edge (y = 1718.54, x 1178–2364), like the existing right-edge strip. The rest of the geography was checked for corruption (spikes are real piers), seams at the other old edges (no visible seam in Chromium), stations in water (only Higashi-ojima, which is real) and rivers. The Kanda River runs from its Inokashira source. No river ends abruptly. The other small rivers (Shakujii, Meguro and so on) are absent both inside and outside the original artwork, which is consistent.
  - **Events.** All 108 previous dates were re-checked against ja.wikipedia line and station articles and Tokyo Metro/Toei releases (Wayback copies). Two changes resulted: Korakuen – Kasuga moved to 2000-12-12, and the Akabane branch was added (1932-12-01, 1972-11-12). No changes to the map happened between 2020-06-07 and 2026-10-02. The Yurakucho Toyosu – Sumiyoshi and Namboku Shirokane-takanawa – Shinagawa extensions have been under construction since 2024-11-05, due in the mid-2030s. The Oedo extension to Oizumi-gakuen-cho is still a plan. The 2025 Azabudai Hills passage is not a designated transfer. Toei's 2021 Japanese sub-names (Daimon 「浜松町」, Iwamotocho 「秋葉原」) are not in its English names.
  - **Left as they are.** Each is documented or within fit noise:
    - The out-of-station staggers at Ueno-hirokoji/Ueno-okachimachi/Naka-okachimachi and Awajicho/Ogawamachi (dots up to 7.7 units along their tracks), Shibuya's Ginza circles and Hanzomon platform (4.9 units).
    - Naka-meguro (2.9 units along, at the edge of the fit).
    - Motoyawata, whose OSM platform tags are ambiguous with JR.
    - Tracks 1–1.4 W from OSM, notably the Ginza Line between Tameike-sanno and Toranomon, the Hibiya Line south of Ningyocho beside the Hanzomon, and the Tozai Line near Minami-sunamachi, rebuilt in 2024.
    - The tram's documented displacements to meet heavy-rail markers.
    - The Marunouchi/Namboku pair between Yotsuya and Akasaka-mitsuke, which keeps a clear gap of about 2 units.
  - **Doubts kept.**
    - Asakusa (Ginza – Asakusa Line) is dated from the 1960-12-04 opening. Through ticketing began 1961-06-01 (ja.wikipedia 浅草駅), whereas Shimbashi is dated by its through fare.
    - Shibuya Ginza–Hanzomon (1978) and New Line Ikebukuro (1994) may have been in-gate transfers. Tokyo Metro's 2022 exit-gate list names only Ginza–Fukutoshin at Shibuya.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): the Tokyo Rapid Railway openings of 1938-12-20 and 1939-01-15 (two pieces each) grow as one path each. They are handed over in place on 2020-01-03 and 1939-09-16 respectively. 12 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.
- Use the operator’s historical-platform and Shibuya-relocation plans above, plus the station-specific histories below, to distinguish these real relocations from drawing adjustments.
- Namboku/Mita shared track and Marunouchi/Ogikubo predecessor accounting need line-specific length definitions; summing advertised line lengths can double-count physical track.
- Toden Arakawa Line and the Nippori–Toneri Liner (added 2026-09-26) are simplified lines (§8): tracks only, 0.4 W. Their geometry comes from OpenStreetMap route relations [9254425](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9254425) and [3423146](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/3423146) (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; API snapshot 2026-09-26), projected with the retained Tokyo WGS84→SVG affine and simplified at 0.15 units. Each line is displaced locally, with a Gaussian taper, to pass through the designated heavy-rail marker: Minowa 20 units (the tram terminus is drawn at Minowa, not at Minowabashi), Nishi-sugamo 19.5, Oji 11 and at most 6 elsewhere. North and south of Zoshigaya, where OSM puts the tram and the Fukutoshin Line in one corridor, the tram touches the Fukutoshin (centre distance 2.1 units, since 2026-10-03; it was offset 3.6 units, which left a hairline gap); it still crosses into the Zoshigaya marker. The section kilometres come from the stop-distance table and sum to Toei's 12.2 km and 9.7 km. The wartime suspension of 1944 to 1946-07-10 is omitted under §7. The 1925–28 split stops at Otsuka and the 1915 Oji terminus south of the main line are below drawing scale. The Akabane branch (added 2026-10-03; [王子電気軌道][ty-oji-ja], [東京都電車][ty-toden-ja]: Oji-yanagita – Kamiyabashi 1926-03-28, Kamiyabashi – Akabane 1927-12-15, Oji-ekimae – Oji-yanagita 1932-12-01, closed 1972-11-12) ran along Kita-hondori, above today's Namboku Line, to the Akabane stop at the Kan-hachi crossing beside Akabane-iwabuchi. It is one track from the drawn Oji-ekimae junction along the Namboku Line's drawn course (the two never coexist), shown from 1932-12-01: before that it was detached from the network (§8 isolated lines). Its 3.7 km is the drawn length at the tram's own scale (12.2 km over its present drawn length); no published section length was found.
- The Liner's northern end (y ≈ −105) lies above the original opening frame but inside the viewBox.
