### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Recovered original artwork: [Shenzhen Metro (Rapid Transit) System Map.svg](<https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shenzhen_Metro_(Rapid_Transit)_System_Map.svg>), Wahsaw, CC BY-SA 4.0. Its revision predates some additions. Geography for later lines was supplemented with mapped track and station coordinates, not inferred solely from a current schematic.

- Added/revised alignments: [Line 3](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2287559), [Branch Line 6](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14953716), [Line 7](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6781618), [Line 8](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13176926), [Line 12](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14944728), [Line 13](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/18470804), [Line 16](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/15059917).
- Additional cross-checks: [Line 5](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2752389), [Line 11](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9318441). Small offsets remain around separate paid-area markers; a smooth curve is not a surveyed centreline.
- Longhua Tram and Pingshan Skyshuttle are simplified. The Skyshuttle drawing was deliberately adjusted to reach the selected metro interchange markers, like the existing Guanlan representation. This is **not evidence that the actual tracks pass through those metro platforms**. Real walking/paid-area arrangements must be taken from station plans.
- Use the Line 13 engineering report above for an independent alignment cross-check; future planned connections shown there are not historical service.
- Operators: stations show `metro` (Shenzhen Metro) or `mtr` (MTR Shenzhen). Line 4's first section switches on the 2010-07-01 handover, which has its own event; its later sections and all of Line 13 show MTR from opening (spec §5).

- OSM position audit (2026-09-29): Line 5 between Grand Theater and Huangbeiling crossed Line 2 twice; it now runs one track width south of Line 2 the whole way, as OSM shows the two sharing one corridor. Line 2 there follows OSM within 1 unit (it had been 3.3 north near Grand Theater), which puts Line 5, Dongmen and Hubei (Line 5) 3.5–3.6 units south of their OSM sites. Line 11 Huaqiang South – Hongling South moved 6–11 units north onto OSM, and Gangxia North – Huaqiang South follows OSM within 1 unit east of Fuxing; east of Gangxia North, Line 11 stays one track width south of Line 14, which shares the corridor. Hongling South (Line 11) moved 6 units but stays 12 from its site (12.2 from the Line 9 circle, which it must stay separate from). Line 11 runs one track width beside Line 9 through Shenwan (it had swung 9.6 units south to clear the Shenwan circle). Line 13 at Houhai, Shenzhen University, Fenghuang Town and Gongming Square was redrawn from 8–10 units off to within 0.6–2.3. Line 14's Baolong – Jinlong curve and Aobei – Universiade section and Line 5 near Xingdong and south of Baigelong were redrawn from up to 10–12 units off to within 0.9–2.6. Honganwei (37 units), Jinlong (21), Guantian (9), Nantou Ancient City (7) and Heshuikou (7) slid along their tracks to OSM. Futian Checkpoint (Line 4) stays 9.5 units from its site (it would overlap the Line 10 circle). Dates, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged. Final check (2026-09-30; made exact to 0.05 units on 2026-10-03): lines sharing a corridor are drawn exactly 1 W apart, one side each: L4/L6 (Hongshan – Shenzhen North), L12/L20, L3/L14 (Buji, Universiade), L1/L11 and L7/L9 (Chegongmiao), L2/L14 (Gangxia North), L9/L12, L5/L7, L11/L20 and L6/Branch Line 6. At Universiade L14, L16 and L3 run three abreast, touching, between L16's two crossings (L14 and L3 up to 0.9 W off OSM there; exact since 2026-10-03), and at Guangmingcheng L13 and Branch Line 6 run side by side, with no weaving. Line 6 at Yinhu keeps to the south side of Line 9. Silian and Railway Park slid about 7.5 units to their OSM platforms. Hubei's Line 2 and Line 5 circles are 2.55 r apart so the connector shows. Also 1 W apart: L9/L11 at Hongshuwan South, L2/L11 at Futian, L7/L14 at Huangmugang, L1/L5 at Qianhaiwan and L2/L5 at Huangbeiling.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: each line's platform comes from OSM (stop positions of its route relation, or a parallel platform way), projected through the station fit onto the drawn tracks. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Bridges at Maling, Shopping Park, Houhai and Fumin follow the Wikimedia line map's bends; OSM has almost no in-station walkways here. The same pass redrew 13 track sections along OSM (Line 1 Xiangmihu–Shopping Park 8.3 units off, Line 5 north of Yijing 8.2, Line 3 Tianbei–Cuizhu 7.1 and others) and slid Bihaiwan 7.3 units to its platform. Track ends lie on their platform points.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): a station's platforms in earlier periods had sat up to 1.1 units from the same platforms later (Qianhaiwan, Buji, Grand Theater, Houhai, Universiade), leaving the 2011 Qianhaiwan Line 5 track end 0.3 off; every period now uses one point per platform. Hongling South's out-of-station circles still touch (real platforms closer still). Line 4's loop south of Hongshan and Line 12 crossing Line 9 at Nanyou match OSM.
- Interchange composition (2026-10-01, spec §5 rule 1): Shenzhen is a reference map, so the README Wikimedia Shenzhen line map (drawn about December 2022) decides every station and line it shows. Every platform stays at its real OpenStreetMap point. One shape where the reference draws one dot or pill: Laojie, Huangbeiling, Tai'an, Huangmugang, Hongshuwan South and Nanyou (pills), Chegongmiao 7/9 and Gangxia North 10/11/14 (pills), and Convention and Exhibition Center, Window of the World, Bao'an Center, Antuo Hill, Huaxin, Hongling North, Lingzhi, Wuhe, Nanshan, Yinhu and Songgang 6/11 (one dot). Everything the reference draws as separate dots is separate dots joined by a bridge, even where the dots touch or overlap. That covers Jingtian, Qianhaiwan, Hongshan, Guangming, Shenzhen World, Shenzhen World North, Airport North, Airport East, Chiwan, Chegongmiao 1/11, Shixia, Tianbei, Qianwan, Xili, Buji, Universiade 3/14 and every passage interchange. Lines newer than the reference follow rule 2 (one shape only for shared track or a full stacked crossing). No Shenzhen station has either, so all of these are separate dots too: Line 13 at Shenzhen University, Houhai, Keyuan (L-shaped node), Yuehaimen (T node), Liuxiandong, Huaqiang South, Gongming Square, Fenghuang Town, Shangwu and Guangmingcheng (双岛四线 cross-platform, own tracks); Line 16 at Universiade (cross-platform with Line 14) and Pingshanwei (T node); Line 5 at Grand Theater (box beside Line 2's); and Line 12 at Songgang (node at the platform end).
- Smoothness check (2026-10-01): No track turns more than 12° at any vertex. Six tiny backward hooks (0.03–0.5 units), left where dated track sections meet at Window of the World, Shuanglong, Fumin, Huangbeiling and Huaqiang South, were removed, so each section ends on its platform point along its own direction. The four places where two lines cross twice in a short distance all match OSM: Line 11 crosses Line 1 near Zhuzilin and again east of Xiangmihu, Line 11 crosses Line 5 at Baohua and south of Guiwan, and Line 3 and Line 14 cross north and south of Buji. Each is drawn as smooth parallel tracks one track width apart between the crossings.

- Close shapes (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate dots whose shapes were under 0.4 R apart now form one shape through the same real platforms (nothing moved): Gangxia 1/10 (0.08 R), Taoyuan 1/12 (0.20 R), Futian 2/3 in both periods (0.39 R), Lianhuacun 3/10 (0.34 R), Tongxinling 3/6 (0.36 R), Shuanglong 3/16 (0.35 R) and Shenzhen North Station 4/5 in both periods (0.06 R). Every other separate pair is 0.4 R or more apart (rechecked 2026-10-03).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), stations: every circle and platform was compared with its OSM stop (median along-track offset 0.04 units; 514 marker points). Songgang Park moved 9.4 units east onto its platform (it sat about 200 m west), and Renmin South (Line 9) 4.3 units east onto its platform beside the Line 1 track it passes under (accuracy over clearance; the tooltip lists Line 9 only). Futian Checkpoint (Line 4) and Hongling South (Line 11) keep the out-of-station stagger (9.5–13 units from their sites). Nankeng and Zuopaotai East differ from their stop positions by 3 units but sit inside their OSM station areas; they were left.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), slivers: lines sharing a corridor now touch to within 0.05 units. Universiade (Lines 14 and 3 had 0.4–2-unit gaps either side of Line 16; their platforms moved 0.58 and 0.83 units sideways with the tracks); Qianhaiwan (Line 11 covered most of Line 5 north of the station, up to 2.6 units; Line 11 now runs exactly 1 W west of Line 5 between their crossings and Line 1 is eased off Line 5 at the station, platforms moving 1.41 and 1.07 units sideways); Line 9 now touches Line 2 after crossing it west of Hongshuwan South (was a 0.3–1.9-unit sliver) and Line 11 touches Line 9 through Shenwan; hairline gaps of 0.05–0.5 units were closed by shifts of at most 0.2 units on L1/L11 (Xiangmihu, west of Chegongmiao), L2/L14/L11 (Gangxia North), L2/L5 (Huangbeiling – Grand Theater), L3/L14 (either side of Buji), L4/L6 (Hongshan – Shenzhen North Station), Branch Line 6/L13 (Guangmingcheng), L9/L12 (Nanyou), L11/L20 (Airport North) and L12/L20 (Shenzhen World, Shenzhen World North). Lines 12 and 2 south of Sea World were redrawn on their OSM courses (both had been 3.6–5.2 units east, with a 1–2-unit sliver between); they now cross cleanly near Shekou Port. The Pingshan Skyshuttle leaves Pingshan beside Line 16 instead of running on top of it. Remaining narrow wedges are where lines converge on stations or cross at shallow angles (Sea World north, Gangxia North, after crossings).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), track courses: compared with the OSM railway centrelines through the station fit (old global fit with local correction; the P1 geo.py fit agrees within 0.6 units median), every track is within about 1.3 W. Corner cuts above 4.3 units were redrawn along OSM where the result stays smooth: Line 2 Xiangmei North – Jingtian (5.4 → 0.4 units), Line 3 near Lianhuacun (4.7 → 1.5), Line 10 Shanglilang – Mugu (4.3 → 2.2; Shanglilang slid 0.2 to its stop), Line 12 Waterlands Resort South – East (5.0 → 1.3) and Huaide – Fuyong (4.4 → 1.7), Line 14 east of Silian (4.3 → 1.5) and Line 5 Xiashuijing – Changlong (4.5 → 0.4). Line 3 into Futian Bonded Area, Line 10 south of Bei'er Road and Line 12 around Qiaotou West / Fuwei (4–5.9 units) were tried and left: following OSM's polyline corners there produced visible kinks. Joints, track ends and the 0.5-unit centreline rule were rechecked: all exact.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), events and names: no line, extension, infill station, rename or closure happened between 2026-06-29 and 2026-10-02 (operator news to 2026-09-22, Transport Bureau news to 2026-09-24, zh-wiki revised 2026-09-28); Line 13's Xili High Speed Railway Station is still unopened (expected 2028); Line 13 south (Tide Park – Dongjiaotou), Line 15 and the 2027–2029 lines are not open. Fixes: Huanggang (Line 4) appears on 2007-06-20 (public trial operation); the number-plus-name line names start 2013-10-18; the Grand Theater – Hongling South connector was removed (not a designated transfer); English names follow the operator map (OCT, Shenzhen North Station, Honganwei, Convention & Exhibition Center, Branch Line 6); Branch Line 6 is 11.1 km (6.13 + 4.944), not 11.3. Known limitation: English station names were pinyin ("Ke Xue Guan", "Shi Jie Zhi Chuang", "Shao Nian Gong", "Hui Zhan Zhong Xin") until 2010–2011 on Lines 1 and 4; no switch date was found, so the translated names are shown throughout. zh-wiki says Line 4 was shown blue before 2010-07-01 (uncited); not modelled.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), geography: the original artwork's coastline matches the OSM coastline (median 0.33 units, p90 0.84 inside the old canvas); no seam shows at the old canvas edges in Chromium. Added, to keep inclusion consistent with the lakes already drawn (Shiyan Lake 5,200 sq units, Luotian Reservoir 4,200): Yantian Reservoir (OSM relation 417265, 5,100 sq units) and Qinglinjing Reservoir (relation 3209074, 3,700, above the 3,650 overview threshold); and the Shenzhen–Zhongshan Link West Artificial Island (way 689375211, Bao'an District, 400 sq units, above the islet threshold), as Shenzhen land. Rivers narrower than about 3.5 units (Pingshan River, Maozhou and Shajing tributaries) stay undrawn, as before; the drawn Longgang River continuation follows the OSM banks.

## Hangzhou (`hangzhou`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/hangzhou/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/hangzhou/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/hangzhou/map.svg).

Scope: Hangzhou Metro. Hanghai Intercity and Shaoxing Line 1 appear on the official map only as connections and are excluded (spec §8).

### Primary records and other focused references

- [Hangzhou news: Line 1 public rides, 19 November 2012][p-hz-preview1] — **New**. Free public trial rides (免费试乘) 18–21 November 2012, the first public riding and the date used under the spec §7; ticketed trial operation followed on 24 November.
- [Central government: Hangzhou Metro opens, 24 November 2012][p-hz-regular1] — **New**. Regular service date, named in the 18 November event.
- [Zhejiang Online: Line 1 ticketed trial operation from 24 November, 14:30](http://zjnews.zjol.com.cn/05zjnews/system/2012/11/23/018965441.shtml) — **New**.
- [Hangzhou news: Line 2 south-east section opens for trial operation, 24 November 2014](https://hznews.hangzhou.com.cn/chengshi/content/2014-11/24/content_5538094_0.htm) — **New**.
- [Hangzhou news: Line 2 trial rides, 17 November 2014][p-hz-preview2] — **New**. Free trial rides 18–22 November 2014 (the date used); regular service 24 November.
- [Hangzhou news: East Railway Station transfer guide][p-hz-east-square] — **New**. 6 November 2021 Line 6 opening and separate East Square paid area.
- [Hangzhou Metro release: Shentangqiao passage opens tomorrow][p-hz-shentang-open] — **New**. Operator-authored notice reproduced by Hangzhou news: paid-area passage opens 1 November 2022.
- [Hangzhou government: 2021 station-name approval][p-hz-name-approval] — **New**. Approval of names; does not alone establish the later 26 January 2022 passenger-signage change.
- [Government account: Zhijiang Culture Center station rename][p-hz-zhijiang-name] — **New**. Effective 1 February 2024, formerly Zhipu Road.
- [Hangzhou news: Jingchang Road opening][p-hz-jingchang] — **New**. Announces 30 June 2025 infill opening.
- [Hangzhou environmental authority: airport express engineering report][p-hz-19-plan] — **Recovered**. Route and station geography for Line 19; distinguish approved alignment from operating history.
- [Zhejiang Online / Qianjiang Evening News: two station renames][p-hz-renames-2022] — **New**. Reports operator confirmation: Dongxinyuan and Linpingnan names take effect on 26 January 2022.
- [China Association of Metros: 2025 operating-line statistics][p-gz-camet] also covers the 2025 Hangzhou Line 5 extension.
- Completeness check (2026-10-03): [杭州地铁][hz-network-zh], [杭州地铁9号线][hz-9-zh] and [杭州地铁10号线][hz-10-zh] list no opening, closure, rename or interchange change after 26 July 2025 (Ducheng Ecopark) up to 2 October 2026. Line 9 phase 2 (Long'an – Tangqi) began trial running (试运行, no passengers) on 15 September 2026 and is not drawn; Line 3 phase 2, Line 10 phases 2–3 (towards Deqing), Lines 12, 15 and 18 remain under construction, and Line 19's Tiaoxi is still unopened.

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

The supplied Hangzhou SVG is the geographic base, but its exact upstream artwork URL/revision has not been recovered. Do not attribute it to an unrelated Commons schematic. Later additions were checked against station coordinates and mapped track, supplemented by the airport express engineering report.

- Reconstructed/corrected corridors: [Line 3 main](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13538220), [Shima branch](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14280625), [Line 5](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/10386952), [Line 7](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13061278), [Line 9](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13060896), [Line 19](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/14613131).
- [Line 1](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/4627560) and [Line 10](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13535687) were comparison alignments. The later audit corrected Gudang Xincun, Yicheng Road and Pinglan Road positions.
- East Railway Station and East Square remain separate paid areas even after eligible tickets gain continuous fares. Shentangqiao’s actual passage opening has its own 1 November 2022 source.
- Unopened Tiaoxi and deferred intermediate platforms must not be inferred open from the full planned project length. Verify operating extent before using a line-total kilometre figure.
- OSM position audit (2026-09-29): Line 19 between Wensan Road and West Lake Cultural Square was drawn straight up to 14.8 units off OSM; it now follows OSM within 0.5. The Shentangqiao, West Lake Cultural Square and East Railway Station (East Square) markers and their earlier circles moved 3–15 units onto the real platforms. Fengloucun (23 units), Xinjie (21), Chuyun Road, Zhenning Road and Yingzhong (8–10) slid along their tracks to OSM. Line 3 made a knot at Gudang Xincun, running west to a misplaced OSM stop position (node 9814728120, about 650 m off), back, and on; it now follows the two OSM track ways within 0.2, with Gudang Xincun at the centre of its OSM station area (29 units from its old position). Dates, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged. Shared corridors are now drawn 1 W apart with single clean crossings: Lines 3, 5 and 16 at Lvting Road (Line 3 in the middle, Line 5 on the north side where it turns north), Line 1 beside Line 7 into Xiaoshan International Airport, Line 9 beside Line 1 through Coach Center, Line 6 west of Line 4 at Zhejiang Chinese Medical University, and Line 19 south-west of Line 6 north of East Railway Station (East Square), crossing it south of the station. Dates, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: platform points are the OSM platform ways of each line's route relation, projected with a local station affine and placed on the drawn tracks. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Five stretches 5–9 units off OSM were redrawn (Line 10 at Huayuangang, Line 9 Sanbao–Yudao, Line 3 Wulinmen–Wulin Square, Line 8 at the Qiantang, Line 5 at Lvting Road), and Line 19 now runs south-west of Line 6 north of East Square and crosses it south of the station, as in OSM (up to 10.5 units). Zhijiang Culture Center and Xipu Road slid 8 units to their platforms. Track ends and split points lie on their platform points.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): Line 19's approach to East Square follows OSM west of its merge with Line 6 (removing a 50° hook beside Goujulong), and Line 2's 2014 Qianjiang Road terminus ends on the station's Line 2 platform (1.7 units). Shentangqiao from 2022-09-22 to 2022-11-01 is two separate stations at their real platforms, 13.7 units apart, whose circles touch.
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): a smoothness pass replaced the six remaining angular vertices inherited from the source drawing (Line 1 at Xixing, a 139° spike under the marker, and at Coach Center; Line 5 south of North Jianguo Road; Line 6 near Weiye Road; two on Line 16 east of Qingshanhu) with tangent-continuous curves (moves under 0.4 units), and no two lines weave.
- Interchange composition (2026-10-01, spec §5 rule 1, reference map): the README Wikimedia line map (`Hangzhou_Metro_Linemap.svg`, which shares this map's canvas and shows the network of early 2022, before Line 19, the central Line 3, Line 9's 2022 extensions and western Line 7) decides each station it shows; platforms stay at their OSM points. One shape where the reference draws one dot or pill: Coach Center (1/9), Pengbu, East Railway Station (1/4) and Qianjiang Road (2/4) pills, Lvting Road (5/16, and Line 3 since 2022, whose drawn track runs inside that pill and whose platforms lie under the Line 5 island), Xintiandi Street (3/4) and Zhejiang Chinese Medical University (4/6) short pills across their side-by-side lines, and Jiangling Road and Chengzhan circles on their stacked crossings. Hangxing Road (10/4), a two-dot station in the reference whose platforms lie 0.39 R apart, is one pill through both real platforms (spec §5 rule 3, 2026-10-02). Everything else is separate dots joined by a bridge, overlapping where the platforms are close: the reference's two-dot stations (Hemu, Shanxian, Jinjiadu, Middle Qingliu Road, Olympic Sports Center, Jianshesan Road, Changhe, Qianjiang Century City, People's Square, Nanxingqiao, North Jianguo Road, Datieguan, Sanba, Jinjiang, Xiaoshan International Airport 1/7, South Wenhai Road, Citizen Center, Binkang Road, Fengqi Road) and, under rule 2, every station or line newer than the reference, none of which shares track or crosses fully stacked: T and L layouts (Wensan Road, Chuangjing Road, Huanglong Sports Center, Xueyuan Road, Sanbao, Jiangcheng Road), cross-platform pairs on their own tracks (Wulin Square and West Lake Cultural Square 1/3, Guanyintang, West Railway Station), side-by-side platforms (Xiaoshan International Airport's Line 19, Yongsheng Road, East Railway Station (East Square)) and passages (Shentangqiao, West Lake Cultural Square's Line 19, Yudao, Wulinmen, Qianjiang Road's Line 9).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), corridors: wherever two lines run beside each other they are now exactly 1 W apart (strokes touching), with no partial overlaps or hairline slivers. Fixed: Line 19 beside Line 7 into and past Xiaoshan International Airport (4.3–4.95 apart, plus a lens-shaped gap) and Line 1 beside Line 7 there (0.13 hairline); Line 4 beside Line 1 from East Railway Station to Pengbu (down to 3.65); Line 3 beside Line 1 between West Lake Cultural Square and Wulin Square (down to 2.7); Line 4 beside Line 2 through Qianjiang Road (3.5–4.8, Line 4 on the north-east side as its tracks lie outside Line 2's); Line 8 leaving South Wenhai Road (4.25–4.9; its first 30 units redrawn parallel to Line 1); Lines 16 and 5 either side of Line 3 into Lvting Road (4.3 and 0.1–0.2 hairlines); Line 19 beside Line 6 north of East Square (0.25 hairline) and Line 9 beside Line 1 at Coach Center (0.13). At Xintiandi Street Line 4 had been drawn on top of Line 3 for 70 units; in OSM Line 3's tracks run north of Line 4's through the station and Line 4 crosses Line 3 west of it, so Line 4 now runs 1 W south of Line 3 from that crossing to where Line 3 turns north, and the marker is a pill across both platforms. At West Railway Station Line 19 lay on top of Line 3 for 38 units; Line 19's tracks straddle Line 3's (cross-platform), and Line 19 is now 1 W east of Line 3, the side it turns to, with its terminus platform 5.2 units east and the two platforms separate dots (0.8 R apart). The line that already followed OSM stayed put; platforms on the moved line were re-projected onto it, which lengthens the Pengbu, East Railway Station (1/4) and Qianjiang Road pills to exactly 1 W. Corridor ends carry the offset as a decaying translation so the curves beside them keep their shape.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), alignments: fourteen stretches 3–5.3 units off the OSM centreline outside any shared corridor were moved onto it (Line 1 east of Coach Center, into West Lake Cultural Square and four stretches of the airport branch; Line 2 between North Jianguo Road and Qingling Road; Line 3 at Qilun Square; Line 4 at Gaotingba; Line 5 at Nanxingqiao; Line 6 near Gaoqiao and at Xiangshan Campus China Academy of Art; Line 7 near Kanshan and west of Yongsheng Road; Line 8 near Cangbeicun; Line 19 near Chuangjing Road and from west of Wensan Road to Shentangqiao). Line 19 between East Square and Yudao had left Line 6 50 units too early and ran up to 8 units (200 m) east of its real course; it now runs 1 W east of Line 6 past Yuanbaotang (whose circle overlaps it, as the real tracks do) to just north of Tanhua'an Road, as in OSM, and then on the OSM line to Yudao (Yudao's Line 19 platform moves 3.7 units). The 294 vertices where a track still turned by 1–12° (polyline corners) were rounded (moves under 0.7 units); no vertex now turns by more than 1°.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), station positions: 53 stations (54 platform points) were 2.0–7.5 units (50–180 m) along their track from the projected OSM platform centre — the earlier passes had accepted up to 1.5 W. Each now sits at that centre on its own track, moved only where the global fit, the local fit and a leave-one-out local fit agreed in direction and all exceeded 2 units (largest: Jingfang 7.5, Pinglan Road 7.1, Zhongtai 6.3, Huayuangang and Yongjiang Road 5.7, Moyetang 5.3, Yongfu and Qiaotoubao 5.1). Pinglan Road's PTv2 stop nodes still carry `proposed:railway=station` and sit 7 units from the mapped platform and station node; the platform was used. Wubao, Liubao and Ducheng Ecopark, missing from the route relations, use their stop positions. Where the station is also a split point (Cuibai Road, Jinxing) the split moved with it along the unchanged geometry; Line 1 at Xianghu now ends 2.5 units shorter, at its platform. Interchange platforms moved the same way at Wensan Road (Line 10), Yudao (Line 9), West Lake Cultural Square (Line 19), Jiangcheng Road (Line 5, with its earlier circle), Guanyintang (Line 7) and East Railway Station (Lines 1 and 4 in opposite directions, so its pill now runs through both real platforms). `data-km`, dates and `data-lines` are unchanged; the Coach Center circle of 2012–2021 stays on the branch platform (now Line 9), 5 units from the Line 1 point of the 2021 pill, as before.
- Geography (2026-10-03): a continuity check of every named OSM river and canal against the drawn water found three broken waterways outside the original artwork, now filled from their mapped banks with only exposed banks outlined: the Jiangnan Canal, which stopped 8 km short of the Grand Canal at Tangqi (relation 10452599, way 520982699 and relation 10918099 along ways 71191063/512865632, side drains pruned); a 21 km middle reach of the Fenshui River above Tonglu (relation 10612951, with the Fuchun relation 334800 at the confluence); and a 5 km reach of the Cao'e River near Shangyu (way 4546261). The East Tiaoxi still begins at its mapped confluence near Pingyao and the Cao'e above 29.68°N has no mapped banks; both are left as drawn.

## Guangzhou / Foshan (`guangfo`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/guangfo/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/guangfo/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/guangfo/map.svg).

Scope: the Guangzhou and Foshan metro networks together, with the APM and the Haizhu, Huangpu and Nanhai trams (trams as tracks only). The Gaoming Tram (高明区现代有轨电车示范线, Foshan, opened 2019-12-30, service suspended since 2024-08-06) is left out: a 6.6 km line in Gaoming with no connection to the rest of the network, it would only appear as an isolated fragment far west of the metro. Guangzhou's intercity railways appear on the official map only as connections and are excluded (spec §8). The header shows both the Guangzhou Metro and Foshan Metro logos, and station tooltips use `guangzhou` and `foshan`.

### Primary records and other focused references

- [China Association of Metros: 2025 operating-line statistics][p-gz-camet] — **New**. Industry statistical table: opening dates, operating lengths and station counts, including GZ 10/12 and Huangpu Tram 2, and Hangzhou Line 5 extension.
- [Southcn: Chigang Line 12 opening][p-gz-chigang] — **New**. 13 February 2026 opening of previously bypassed Line 12 platforms.
- [Southcn: Foshan Line 3 through operation][p-gz-f3-through] — **New**. Reports Foshan rail authority approval: 18 June 2026 full connection. Need separate evidence for deferred Foshan Railway Station.
- [China News Service: Foshan hub opening][p-gz-foshan-station] — **New**. 1 July 2026 railway/metro station opening, distinct from 18 June through running.
- [Guangdong Transport Department: Nanhai Tram extension][p-gz-nanhai-open] — **New**. 29 November 2022 extension; retrospectively confirms 18 August 2021 initial opening; Linyuexi same-platform transfer without leaving the paid area.
- [Guangzhou government: South Railway Station paid-area passage][p-gz-south-transfer] — **New**. 21 January 2024, linking Foshan Line 2 to Guangzhou Lines 2, 7 and 22.

| 1997-06-28 | Line 1: Xi Lang - Huang Sha paid sightseeing service begins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | [Guangzhou cyberspace office: Line 1 at 25](https://gzwxb.gov.cn/context/contextId/205622) "1997年6月28日…一号线西塱站至黄沙站一期工程开始观光试运营"; [广州地铁1号线][gz-1zh] (5-yuan fare, 30-minute headway); [Yangcheng Evening News, 27 June 2017](https://web.archive.org/web/20200607075023/http://news.ycwb.com/2017-06/27/content_25130510.htm) "当时'观光运营'的1号线票价是来回5元"; [1997 sightseeing tickets (地铁观光票, 5 yuan) on Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Former_paper_tickets_for_Guangzhou_Metro_since_1997~1999.jpg). **Note (spec §7):** paid sightseeing trial operation (观光试运营) counts, so this is the opening. The first train carried about 500 invited guests, and opening-day crowds were given numbered tickets to ride on a later day (YCWB); the Chinese Guangzhou Metro article's uncited "7月2日，1号线正式对公众开放" is not used against the official history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 1999-02-16 | Line 1: Huang Sha - Guang Zhou Dong Zhan paid sightseeing service begins, running over the whole line                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [Southern Metropolis Daily via Sina, 17 February 1999](https://web.archive.org/web/2005/http://news.sina.com.cn/richtalk/news/china/9902/021704.html) "广州地铁一号线面向社会公众开放的第一班地铁…从自动售票机购得两张单程票…观光期间地铁运行时间每天从8时30分至22时…每12分钟开出1班车"; [Guangzhou Daily via Sina, 3 March 1999](https://web.archive.org/web/2010/http://news.sina.com.cn/richtalk/news/china/9903/030324.html) "自2月16日全线开放观光至昨日止…15天共有139.2万人次乘坐地铁…从今天起，地铁将全线封闭…6月28日重新开放正式运营"; [Guangzhou urban construction archive](https://web.archive.org/web/20140317122015/http://www.gzuda.gov.cn/news/view.asp?id=XW200302251351523598&fdID=CL200301290021207522) "1999年2月16日至3月2日全线观光运营"; [广州地铁1号线][gz-1zh]. **Note (spec §7):** paid public sightseeing on the whole line, daily 8:30–22:00 every 12 minutes with single-journey tickets from ticket machines, so Huangsha – Guangzhou East appears on 16 February. Whether the 1997 Xilang – Huangsha sightseeing was still running until then is not established (the same report says the line had been in full system testing since January 1999); it is drawn continuously from 1997. |

| 2014-12-31 | Haizhu Tram: Canton Tower - Wanshengwei paid trial-ride period begins                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [Nanfang Daily via People's Daily, 30 December 2014](http://cpc.people.com.cn/n/2014/1230/c87228-26296628.html). It gives the 开通试乘期 from 31 December 2014 to 11 February 2015 as daily service from 9:00 to 17:00 at a 13-minute headway, with first and last trains posted at stations and a 2-yuan day ticket ("试乘纪念券…当天可多次试乘") on sale at every station. From 12 February service moved to 试运营 with 羊城通 and single-journey tickets. Also: [Haizhu district page](https://www.haizhu.gov.cn/hzdt/ztlm/tzhz/rjhj/lyjd/csmp/content/post_9173297.html) "2014年12月31日正式开通试运营"; [Bendibao, 3 February 2015](http://jt.gz.bendibao.com/news/201523/180533.shtml); [Haizhu Tram][gz-tram]. **Note (spec §7):** despite the "试乘" (trial ride) label, the opening period was paid public service on a timetable, not a free trial-ride promotion, so it counts. From 12 February 2015 the line moved to 全线试运营 (regular service), recorded as its own event. Pati (Beer Museum) did not open with the line; the simplified tram draws no stop markers.                                                                                                                                 |

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

Recovered base artwork: [Guangzhou Metro Map en.svg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Guangzhou_Metro_Map_en.svg), ASDFGH, CC BY-SA 3.0. The user-supplied `og.svg` preserved Foshan geometry; `ref.svg` was a later network cross-check, not a replacement for geographic alignment. Those input filenames alone are not durable external citations.

- Modern additions/corrections: [Line 3](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9841062), [5](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/7483883), [7](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/7520751), [10](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/19283541), [11](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/18132492), [12 east](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/19283546), [12 west](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/19283549), [13](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6728313), [14](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/8338723), [22](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13987999), [Huangpu Tram 2](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/19382702).
- Restored/extended Foshan corridors: [Line 2](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13604443), [Line 3](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/15054264), [Nanhai Tram](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/13103097). Use dated notices for which part of these modern routes was open at each event.
- Ersha Island and other added stations were recalibrated against geographic coordinates. Chinese map coordinates may be GCJ-02 while OSM is WGS84; mixing them shifts stations systematically. Bézier smoothing remains a presentation adjustment; interchange dots are moved off their real platforms only to put stacked platforms on their drawn crossing point, or to square a pill across parallel lines.
- Western canvas/rivers were extended using mapped water geometry to avoid clipping inherited rivers. That edit is a present-day background repair, not a history of land reclamation or river changes.
- Nanhai’s Linyuexi paid-area transfer is explicitly supported by the Guangdong Transport Department notice. APM/metro and several tram walking links must not be assumed to share paid areas merely because a passage exists.
- OSM position audit (2026-09-29): Line 22 between Guangzhou South and Shiguanglu ran up to 34 units (720 m) south of OSM and now follows it within 0.5; Line 12 at Baiyun Culture Square dipped 12–18 units south to the Line 2 platform and now runs through its own OSM station; the two platforms are joined by a bridge. Foshan Line 2 Shiliang, Flower World, Shagang and Shiwan, Foshan Line 3 Yuebu, Zhen'an and Shunde College Railway Station (both termini, tracks re-cut), and APM Tianhenan and Huacheng Dadao slid 9–19 units along their tracks to OSM. Huacheng Dadao's real site is beside Line 5, which doesn't stop there; it is kept on its real position. Dates, `data-lines` and `data-km` are unchanged.
- Second OSM pass (2026-09-29), each finding confirmed by both a 12-station local fit and the whole-network affine: Line 22 now reaches its real Guangzhou South platform about 9 units (190 m) east of Lines 2/7. The Line 22 platform is a separate dot joined to the Line 2/7 blob by a bridge; from 2024-01-21 the Foshan Line 2 platform is bridged in too, and before that its connector ends on the Line 2 or Line 7 platform. Line 22 Shiguanglu – Panyu Square, Line 7 at Dashadong, Line 11 at Datang and under Guangzhou Railway Station (whose Line 11 station has not opened), Line 3 Renhe – Gaozeng and its Haibang terminus, Line 12 at Xunfenggang, Foshan Line 3 Gaocun – Tanzhou and at Shunde OCT Harbour Plus, and the APM Huacheng Dadao – Canton Tower now follow OSM. Shijing, Midea, Nanchong, Xianchong, Shiguanglu, Tanzhou, Beijiao West, Shunde OCT Harbour Plus, Guangzhou Opera House and Haixinsha moved 5–11 units to OSM. Wuyangcun (Line 10) moved to 13.5 units from the Line 5 circle, the closest §5 allows for an out-of-station pair, 2.5 units from OSM. Line 3 Tiyu Xilu – Shipaiqiao follows its real northward arc (it was up to 16.5 units south). North of Tiyu Xilu it runs 1 W beside the Linhexi line, the two straddling the corridor they share, then curves east. It passes under the Line 1 Tianhe Sports Center circle (the tunnel is about 70 m from that station) and clears the APM Tianhe Sports Center South circle (about 160 m). Line 22 Xilang – Fangcun runs 1 W west of Line 1, which stays on OSM with its stations (on its real side since 2026-10-03; it had been drawn east of Line 1). Left as drawn: Changping (whole-network fit 10 m; the local-fit residual was an edge artefact); the APM's Linhexi and Canton Tower circles, which §5's spacing for out-of-station pairs holds beside Line 3's; and the Guangfo Line termini, where OSM's ways continue past the station. OSM node 5230570817 (官湖) carries a wrong `name:en` ("Yufengwei"). Final check (2026-09-30): Line 4/Line 12 (Guanzhou – Higher Education Mega Center South) and Line 5/Line 13 (Miaotou – Xiayuan) are drawn 1 W apart, one side each (Line 12 on the south-west side, its real side, since 2026-10-03). Single-line circles that preceded an interchange sit on the same drawn point as their platform in the later marker (22 circles moved up to 7.5 units). Shizhou slid 9 units to its platform. The Foshan Line 2 connector at Guangzhou South follows the marker change on 2022-03-31. Lines sharing a corridor are drawn exactly 1 W apart, one side each: L11/L21 and L18/L22 into Tianhe Park and Panyu Square (around their shared OSM track), L11/L12 at Chisha (after one crossing), L7/Foshan L3 at Beijiao Park, L5/L11 at Zhongshanba, L14/L21 at Zhenlong, L3/L9 at Gaozeng, L10/L22 south of Xilang, and L22 west of Line 1 from Fangcun to Xilang (Line 1 and its stations stay on OSM); Line 2 and Lines 3/14 south of Jiahewanggang stay closer because the three lines share one alignment.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: 174 of 177 platform points are OSM platform ways beside each line's route ways, projected with a 12-station local fit (median 22 m). Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. At Tianhe Park and Panyu Square, where OSM has one shared track, the last ~25 units of Lines 11/21 and 18/22 run W/2 either side of it (up to 3.8 units). Bridges at Modiesha, Nancun Wanbo and Huangcun follow the Wikimedia line map's bends. The same pass redrew 17 track sections 1.2–2.1 W off OSM and moved Meidi Dadao and Gongye Avenue South onto their stops; track ends and joints lie on their platform points.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): every single-line circle that preceded an interchange sits exactly on its platform's drawn point, with its track ends (largest moves Dashadong 7.3, Longtan 4.7, Guicheng 4.4 and Caihong Bridge 4.3 units). The sections redrawn along OSM are smoothed over about 8 units with 25-unit tapers, removing small jogs carried by the OSM ways (Line 18 south of Xiancun and others); Line 14's 2017–2018 hook at Zhenlong and an S-wiggle in Line 12 at Guanzhou are gone. Kept: Line 3's bend at Tiyu Xilu (the branch junction, inside the marker); the Linhexi and Wuyangcun out-of-station pairs; Shixi and Gongye Avenue South, separate stations 260 m apart whose circles touch.
- Interchange composition (2026-10-01, spec §5, rules 1–2). Guangzhou uses rule 1: the README's Wikimedia Guangzhou line map decides each station it shows. That edition is from about 2022–23, with Lines 18 and 22 and the Foshan lines but not Lines 10–12 or the newer extensions. Platforms stay at their real OpenStreetMap points. One shape where the reference draws one dot or pill: Gongyuanqian, Zhujiang New Town, Kecun, Wanshengwei, Yuzhu, Kuiqi Lu, Dongping, Wanhua, Higher Education Mega Center South 4/7, and the pills at Jiahewanggang 2/3 and Zhenlong 14/21. Stations and lines newer than the reference use rule 2. Shared track: none. Full stacked crossing: Higher Education Mega Center South 12, where the zh.wikipedia station article says the platforms form a 卄 and Line 7 crosses over Line 12; it joins the 4/7 dot in one shape. Every other interchange is separate dots at the real platforms, joined by a bridge. The dots overlap where they are close, which is often almost completely at the reference's two-dot crossings: Tiyu Xilu, Changgang, Nanzhou, Lijiao, Yantang, Chebeinan, Ouzhuang, Tanwei, Cultural Park and Suyuan. The other separate interchanges are Gaozeng, Tianhe Coach Terminal, Shayuan, Beijiao Park, Jiahewanggang 14, Guangzhou South (2/7, 22 and Foshan 2), Panyu Square (18/22 and 3), Yangji, Huangsha, Dongshankou, Haizhu Square, Guangzhou Railway Station, Guangzhou East, Shibi, Hanxi Changlong, Huangcun, Yuancun, Chen Clan Academy, Xicun, Modiesha and Nancun Wanbo, all drawn separate in the reference. Under rule 2, T and L nodes are separate too (zh.wikipedia layout text): Jiangtai Road, Ruyifang, Julong, Wufeng, Longtan, Guicheng, Yufengwei, Shuixi, Xinshixu and Fangcun (but see the 0.4 R exception below). So are the cross-platform pairs on their own tracks (Tianhe Park 11/21, Chisha) and Tianhe Park 13. Side-by-side boxes are separate as well: Xilang 1/10/22, Fangcun 22, Chebei, Zhongshanba, Shahe, Higher Education Mega Center North and Xiayuan. Passages make the rest separate: Datang, Haibang, South China Normal University, Dongxiao South, Guanzhou, Caihong Bridge, Shachong, Yangang, Donghu, Xunfenggang, Chigang, Luogang, Dashadong and Baiyun Culture Square. Guangzhou South's Line 22 has no dot in the reference, which runs the track through the 2/7 pair, so rule 2 applies and it stays a separate dot behind a passage.
- Track fix (2026-10-02): at Yuancun, the Line 21 (2019–2024) and Line 11 (from 2024) track joint and its platform dot moved 5.1 units (about 110 m) south, along the existing curve, onto the real platform centre. The source is OpenStreetMap platform ways 601701977/601701978 with a 12-station local fit. The bend just north of the joint is now tangent-continuous, and the Line 5 dot did not move.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): Line 2 of 2002-12-29 (two pieces, handed over 2010-09-25), the Haizhu Tram of 2014-12-31 (three pieces, handed over 2024-11-13), Line 21 of 2019-12-20 (two pieces, handed over 2024-10-02) and Huangpu Tram Line 2 of 2025-06-20 (three pieces) each grow as one path. Two stretches still regrow after a gap that was already in the history: the Haizhu Tram's Canton Tower East–Liede Bridge South piece on 2025-07-01 (from the network end), and Tianhe Park–Yuancun, which closes with Line 21's shortening on 2024-10-02 and reopens as Line 11 on 2024-12-28. 3 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.
- Drawing exception for near-coincident shapes (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump, so they became one shape through the same real platform points at 22 markers: Changgang, Chebeinan, Cultural Park, Fangcun (1/11), Haizhu Square, Jiangtai Road, Julong, Lijiao, Longtan, Nanzhou, Ouzhuang, Shayuan, Shuixi (7/21), Suyuan, Tanwei, Tianhe Park, Tiyu Xilu, Wanshengwei (with the tram), Xilang (10/22), Yantang and Yufengwei. After the 2026-10-03 realignment below, Haizhu Square, Lijiao, Longtan, Shayuan and Yufengwei are 3.5–6.8 units (≥ 0.4 R) apart again and are two dots with a bridge; Guicheng and Ruyifang, now 0.8 and 1.0 units apart, became one shape; Xilang's Lines 10 and 22 are separate dots on their real sides of the Line 1 terminus.
- Final audit, tracks (2026-10-03). Every track was compared with its line's OpenStreetMap route ways (snapshot 2026-10-01, the 12-station local fit; the 15 Line 22 extension ways 1462151553, 970344578, 1462151554, 970344581, 833936949, 1057518928/29/40/41/44/45/53, 885878227 and 970344573/75, still tagged `railway=construction` in OSM, were added). Three corridors had the lines on the wrong sides of each other: Line 22 Xilang – Fangcun now runs 1 W west of Line 1 (it was east; OSM puts it under the west side of Huadi Avenue), Line 12 follows OSM through Guanzhou, crossing Line 4 there, and runs on Line 4's south-west side to Higher Education Mega Center South (Line 4 and Line 12 straddle their shared OSM midline), and Line 13 runs north of Line 4 through Chebei and crosses it east of the station. Line 10 now starts at its real Xilang platform beside the Line 1 terminus, and east of Wuyangcun it follows OSM along Line 5 (touching it, north side) past the Line 5 station before turning north to Yangji East (it had cut diagonally, 9 units off OSM, to keep clear of the Line 5 circle; spec §5 does not move tracks for clearance). 53 further stretches that were 2.5–5.8 units off OSM, on Lines 2–14, 18, 21 and 22, the Guangfo Line and Foshan Line 3 (largest Line 11 at Shachong 5.8, Line 12 at Xinshixu 5.5, Line 13 east of Yuzhu 5.5, Line 11 at Ruyifang 5.1), now follow OSM within about 0.6 units. Lines running side by side were set to touch exactly (1 W centre spacing, no sliver or partial overlap): Line 2/Line 7 into Guangzhou South, Line 5/Line 11 at Zhongshanba, Line 18/Line 22 into Panyu Square, Line 3/Line 9 into Gaozeng, Line 14/Line 21 into Zhenlong, Line 8/Guangfo Line through Shayuan, Line 7/Foshan Line 3 through Beijiao Park, Line 6/Line 3 into Tianhe Coach Terminal, Line 11/Line 12 into Chisha, Line 4/Line 13 through Chebei, and Lines 2, 3 and 14 at Jiahewanggang (Line 14 north of the station now crosses Line 3 where OSM does). Trams: Huangpu Tram Line 1 follows OSM from Changping to its own Xiangxue stop and touches Line 21 along Kaichuang Avenue, Huangpu Tram Line 2 starts at that stop, Nanhai Tram Line 1 starts at its OSM Leigang stop and touches Foshan Line 2 from Linyue Xi to Linyue Dong, and the Haizhu Tram touches Line 8 into Wanshengwei. 17 track ends and joints moved 1.5–4.6 units onto their OSM platforms (Chentougang 4.6, Guangzhou East 2.7–3.0, Guangzhou Opera House 2.8, Xinsha 2.6 and others; Pazhou keeps its out-of-station stagger, Huangcun would overlap Line 21, and Jiangnanxi is the 2010 hand-over point). 16 same-line joints were made tangent-continuous (Line 7 at Guangzhou South, Line 14 at Jiahewanggang, Line 5 at Wenchong and others) and 721 small corners (0.3–20°) inherited from the artwork's polylines were smoothed. `data-km` is unchanged; the `data-takes-over` continuations were rebuilt as exact pieces of their parents.
- Final audit, stations (2026-10-03). 57 single-line circles whose OSM platform centre lay 1.5–4.9 units along the track from the circle moved onto it (Flower World 4.9, Jiaomen 4.7, Gaocun 4.7, Dadun 4.6, Guanhu 4.3 and others; the circles had been placed on OSM stop nodes, which often sit at a platform end). Interchange platforms that coincided with those circles moved with them, and every other platform keeps its place along the redrawn track. Median along-track distance from the OSM platform centre fell from 0.37 to 0.13 units (90th percentile 2.17 to 1.15). Left on purpose: the out-of-station staggers at Linhexi, Canton Tower, Pazhou, Wuyangcun and Tiyu Xilu – Tianhenan (connector lengths unchanged); Huacheng Dadao beside Line 5; the Xiaogang circle of the 2002–2010 Line 2 curve, which OSM no longer shows.
- Final audit, geography (2026-10-03). The preserved artwork was checked against OpenStreetMap river polygons in central Guangzhou and Foshan Chancheng/Shunde (banks within about 1–2 units). Five seams where the artwork meets the expanded geography had steps of 2–9 units or a narrow expanded channel: the bottom edge at x ≈ 2555, 3025 and 3303 and the right edge on the two Dongjiang channels (y ≈ 2285 and 2458); each is now joined by a smooth bank over 12–25 units outside the artwork (group `seam-joins`). The Sanshui stream that stopped at the old western edge at (0, 1884) now continues along its OSM channel to the Beijiang (ways 9769483, 48791728, 164513077). The Tanjiang no longer stops abruptly at 112.90 E: its OSM river polygons (14, along waterway 潭江) carry it about 2,700 units upstream, with two unmapped reaches filled by the centreline at 6 units; the western reach beyond a longer gap in OSM is left out. All three additions use the expanded geography's transform (the Tanjiang matches the drawn reach to a median 0.12 units after a (−1, +7) shift).
- Final audit, events (2026-10-03): no further opening, closure, rename or interchange change took place in the Guangzhou or Foshan networks between 2026-07-01 and 2026-10-02. Still under construction on that date: Line 12's middle section (Guangzhou Gymnasium – Ersha Island, 8.8 km, in operational testing from August 2026, opening planned for the end of 2026), Line 13 phase 2 west (Chaoyang – Tianhe Park, 25.3 km, in operational testing from August 2026), the Line 18 northern extension (expected 2027), Foshan's Nanhai Tram Line 2 (before the 2027 Spring Festival), Huangpu Tram Line 2's southern section and Foshan Line 4 ([Guangzhou Daily, 27 January 2026](https://news.dayoo.com/guangzhou/202601/27/139995_54921533.htm); [21jingji, 24 August 2026](https://www.21jingji.com/article/20260824/herald/ed8f5d608f3c760cec8f480047b12f25.html); [Guangzhou Daily, 19 September 2026](https://news.dayoo.com/guangdong/202609/19/139996_55005329.htm); [zh.wikipedia 佛山地铁](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-hans/%E4%BD%9B%E5%B1%B1%E5%9C%B0%E9%93%81)). Line 11's Guangzhou Railway Station platform, bypassed since 2024-12-28, is still not shown as open; no opening was found.

## Chengdu (`chengdu`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/chengdu/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/chengdu/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/chengdu/map.svg).

### Primary records and other focused references

- [Chengdu Metro app API: station list][p-cd-chengdu-metro-app-api-station-list] — **New**. Every line, official English station name and transfer line; the live copy of 2026-09-24 was compared with an archived copy of 2024-07-10. The transfer lists are the test for designated interchanges (§6).
- [Chengdu Rail Transit: English station list (archived 2017–2023)][p-cd-chengdu-rail-transit-english-station-lis] — **New**. Pre-2023 English station names; more than 70 captures from 2017-12-08 to 2023-01-05.
- [Official network map, February 2023 (archived)][p-cd-official-network-map-february-2023-archi] — **New**. Pre-revision English names; the December 2024 and December 2025 editions show the post-July-2023 names, Line S3 and Tram Line 2.
- [Sichuan Online, 2025-09-16][p-cd-sichuan-online-2025-09-16] and [China News Service, 2025-12-05][p-cd-china-news-service-2025-12-05] — **New**. Operator figures for Line 17 phase 2, Line 13 and Line 30 (lengths, stations, first public day).
- [Red Star News via Sina, 2026-09-24][p-cd-red-star-news-via-sina-2026-09-24] — **New**. Announces the Line 2 east section's return on 2026-09-28 on its new alignment.
- [Wikimedia Commons: Chengdu Rail Transit icon][p-cd-wikimedia-commons-chengdu-rail-transit-i] — **New**. Source of the logo; public domain as a text logo, with a trademark notice. The app preserves the complete mark’s shapes and proportions, with its original blue fills and no added background.
- Each event row below cites the notices and reports behind that date; station lists and English names otherwise follow the operator app and the archived English station list.

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

- **Artwork.** The supplied SVG is an Illustrator export of a geographic Chengdu Metro map (roughly the mid-2024 network: it has Qingdao Road but not Line 27 or the Line 8 phase 2 extensions). Its upstream source and licence are not recorded. Lines are outlined strokes; their centrelines were recovered exactly from the two sides of each ribbon (§12). Stripe-drawn shared stretches (Lines 5/6 at Xibei Bridge, 18/19 to the airport) were rebuilt as full-width parallels, and Line 1’s doubly drawn trunk at Sihe as one track with the Wugensong branch leaving it.
- **Added lines.** Lines 13, 27, 30 and S3 and the extensions of Lines 8, 10 and 17 follow OpenStreetMap route relations ([OSM: Line 13][cd-osm-line-13], [OSM: Line 27][cd-osm-line-27], [OSM: Line 30][cd-osm-line-30], [OSM: Line S3][cd-osm-line-s3], [OSM: Line 8][cd-osm-line-8], [OSM: Line 10][cd-osm-line-10], [OSM: Line 17][cd-osm-line-17]), retrieved 2026-09-24. Coordinates were fitted to the artwork with an affine transform on 20 line termini, then a Gaussian local correction from 329 matched stations (median residual 1.1 units, about 20 m).
- **Water and outside land.** Water is the union of OpenStreetMap `natural=water`, `waterway=riverbank` and `landuse=reservoir` areas retrieved 2026-09-24, through the same fit; ponds under 60 square units are dropped and outlines simplified at 0.4 units. Land outside [OSM: Chengdu municipality boundary][cd-osm-chengdu-municipality-boundary] is tinted. The background is present-day geography throughout playback.
- **Western extent.** The frame extends 1,552.494 units westward to put Tianfu Square at its horizontal midpoint. All original coordinates shift right by that amount; track shapes, station alignment and scale are unchanged. The added western water areas use the same geographic fit and 2026-09-24 OpenStreetMap data, with the municipality boundary extended across the new frame.
- **Placement exceptions.** Line 30’s Financial City North stands at its real platform beside Line 18, 6.6 units from Line 18’s centreline (accuracy over clearance, spec §5; the earlier 4.5-unit clearance move was undone on 2026-10-03). At the airport, Lines 10 and 19 run in parallel closer than the marker clearance (tolerated shared corridor, §5). Line 10’s Terminal 2 of Shuangliu International Airport stands at the nearest point on Line 10 to its platform that keeps it 2.1 R (15.7 units) from the East of Terminal 2 platforms (§5), about 14 units from the platform; one connector joins them from 2023-11-28.
- **Tram.** Chengdu Tram Line 2 is drawn as simplified track; its metro interchanges shown in `data-lines` are the same-named Chengdu West Railway Station (from 2019-12-27), Tianhe Road (2019-12-27) and Wangcong Temple (2020-12-18, when Line 6 opened). The official map also marks Xipu Campus ↔ Xingye North Street and Longyin ↔ Zitonggong; they are not included (different names, no dated designation).
- **Kilometres.** Published line totals (China Association of Metros 2024 and operator releases) govern: Line 18’s 69.39 km is split by drawn length because its published 55.95 km first section conflicts with station spacing (≈48.2 km); Line 3’s phases 2 and 3 and Line 4’s 2017 extensions share their published remainder by drawn length; Line 19 counts the shared Line 18 track from Tianfu Station at Line 18’s own allocation (total 99.7 km; the operator says over 100 km).
- **Colours.** The artwork’s colours are Pantone values (Line 1 Blue 072 C, Line 2 171 C, Line 7 310 C, Line 10 293 C, Line 17 352 C, Line 18 3165 C, Line 19 2718 C) and are kept; Lines 13 and 27 use OpenStreetMap’s values in the same family (103 C, 299 C). The operator app uses a separate screen palette.
- OSM position audit (2026-09-29): Zitonggong (Line 6, 20 units) and Muhua Road (Line 19, 10 units) slid along their tracks to their OSM positions. A geometry scan found hooks and hairpins in 24 track paths (the path overshooting a station centre and doubling back, or running to it, back and on). Most were hidden under station markers, but Line 19's jog about 20 units west of Tianfu Park showed today, and the Line 3 end at Taipingyuan stuck out of its circle from 2016-07-31 to 2017-09-06. Each is replaced by a smooth curve through the same station centre (within 0.03–0.84 of the old line); every track still ends at the same point, and joins at Taipingyuan, Lianhua, Shilidian and Jitouqiao now meet at matching angles.
- OSM audit (2026-09-30): Liulichang's 2017–2020 circle, Qingjiang West Road and Xinghe slid 8 units along their tracks; Huangtianba's Line 9 terminus extended 9.3 units to its platform; Line 18 runs 1 W west of Line 1 along Tianfu Avenue between Hongshi Park and Guangzhou Road. Line 30's Yuhong Road and Fenshui (deferred openings, "玉虹路、分水暂缓开通") are not drawn.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: each line's platform is the mean of its OSM stop positions, mapped with one local correction per station onto the drawn tracks. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Five stretches about 1 W off OSM were redrawn and twelve circles slid 5–8 units to their platforms (largest Wenquan Avenue, Wenjiashan). Circles and platforms lie on their tracks and track ends on platform points; at Jiujiang North the Jinxing track's last 10 units are a Line 17 approach to the north platform until 2023-09-22 and a Line 19 approach to the south platform after it.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): every circle and platform point lies exactly on its line's track on every date it serves (moves of at most 0.4 units), and every track end on a platform point (Line 17 at Jitouqiao 2.8 units, S3 at Futian 1.9). The last 10 units of the Jinxing–Jiujiang North track are split into a Line 17 approach to the north platform (2020-12-18 – 2023-09-22) and a Line 19 approach to the south platform, 0.1 km each from that track's 19.8 km, so the 2020–2023 through route no longer jogs 3.5 units inside the station. Shiyang and Shiyangdong overlap at their real platforms (no transfer, about 250 m apart).
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01, spec §5 rules 1–2): Chengdu is a reference map, so the Wikimedia line map (the same artwork shifted x + 1552.4) decides every station and line it shows. Lines 13, 27 and 30, the Line 8 extension (Longgang), the Line 17 extension, the Line 10 extension (Hongpailou, Gaoshengqiao's Line 10) and S3 are newer than that map, so they follow rule 2, using the transfer types in zh-Wikipedia's 成都地铁车站列表 and the station articles. Platforms sit at their OSM positions. Only a one-shape crossing goes on the drawn crossing point, and separate dots are not squared. One shape where the reference draws one: Tianfu Square, North Railway Station and Tianfu Commercial District (one circle); Chengdu University of TCM 2/4/5 (one pill); Xibei Bridge (stacked islands each serving 5 and 6); Jiujiang North, plus Lines 18/19 at Tianfu Station, Sancha, Futian, Terminal 1&2 and Airport North (shared track); Taipingyuan's Lines 3 and 7 (its dot on the 3 × 7 crossing); Chengdu West's tram stop with Line 4; and Fengxihe's Lines 17/19 (one platform, renamed service). One shape under rule 2: Dongpo Road (十字节点, a full stacked crossing). Every other interchange is separate dots joined by a bridge. That includes stations the reference draws as two touching dots, even where the platforms nearly coincide and the dots overlap (Luomashi, Sichuan Gymnasium, Chunxi Road, Chengdu Second People's Hospital, Chengdu East, Dongdalu Road, Yipintianxia, Sima Bridge, Culture Palace, Yushuang Road, Shuangqiao Road, Wuqing South Road, Shuangliu West, 2nd Beizhan West Road, Shenxianshu, Jincheng Avenue, Yixin Lake, Southwest Jiaotong University, Dongguang, Liulichang, Financial City East, Sanyuan, Huaxing, Jitouqiao, South Railway Station, Incubation Park, Western China Int'l Expo City and Taipingyuan's Line 10). It also covers the newer T/L nodes (Xinnanmen, Hongpailou, Qingyang Taoist Temple, Provincial Orthopaedics Hospital, Jinfu, Jianshe North Road, Jinshi Road, Longzhuayan, Erxianqiao, Jingjusi, Zhujiang Road, Longgang, Peifeng, Xiaonan Street), the concourse and passage transfers (Weijianian, East of Terminal 2, Huaxiba, Huiwangling, People's Park, Yangxi Flyover, Hongxing Bridge, Dongzikou, Chengdu First People's Hospital, Sanguantang, Sichuan Normal University, Jiaozi Flyover, Gaoshengqiao's Line 10) and Futian's S3, which shares islands with Line 18 but runs on its own tracks.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): Line 17 of 2020-12-18 (three pieces, handed over 2023-09-22, when Jinxing–Jiujiang North becomes Line 19) and Line 19 of 2023-11-28 (two pieces) each grow as one path. 2 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.

- **Final audit (2026-10-03): tracks.** At the app’s maximum zoom (about 0.9 CSS px per unit) gaps or overlaps under about 0.3 units do not show, so this pass fixed the visible ones. Where two lines share a corridor, one now touches the other exactly (offset W) instead of leaving gaps of 1–6 units or partly overlapping it: Line 18 beside Line 1 along Tianfu Avenue (Century City – Haichang Road, and exact again from the side swap to Western China Int’l Expo City); Line 4 beside Line 2 from its merge west of Chengdu University of TCM (one smooth curve replaces a dip and bump); Line 5 beside Line 6 through Xibei Bridge (Line 5 now crosses Line 6 in one curve east of the station); Line 13 beside Line 6 between Sanguantang and Jiuyan Bridge. Stretches 2.5–4.9 units off their OSM route relations were redrawn on their real courses: Line 1 along Tianfu Avenue (four stretches), Line 3 at Longqiao Road and into Shuangliu West Railway Station, Line 6 at Xipu and through Xibei Bridge, Line 8 (two stretches), Line 9 and Tram Line 2 at Chengdu West Railway Station (both about 5 units west for 100 units), Line 10 at Jinhua, Line 18 east of Science City and Line 19 (four stretches). Platforms on a corrected track moved with it, perpendicular to the track. The remaining deviations of up to 6.5 units are corridor offsets (Lines 18, 19 and S3 to the airport; Lines 3 and 10 into Taipingyuan). No `data-km` changed. Tram Line 2 still crosses Lines 2 and 6 at shallow angles where it runs in the street above them; these are real positions and are left as crossings. Renderer note: at Jiujiang North, the exact, tangent-continuous joint between the Jinxing – Jiujiang North track and the Line 19 approach can show a faint seam in Chromium.
- **Final audit (2026-10-03): stations.** Each platform point was checked against OSM stop positions in two independent ways: a local fit that leaves the station’s own control out, and the station’s chainage between its two neighbours along the OSM route. 28 platform points slid along their own tracks to the platform centre where both checks agreed on 3–6.5 units (about 70–155 m). The largest were Xinglong (6.5), Qilong (6.2), Xindao (6.0) and Tuanjiexinqu (5.0). Shilidian (4.9) and Wannianchang (4.1) moved together with the track joints there, and Chengdu West’s Line 4 platform by 3.4. After the pass the residual median is 0.4 units and the 90th percentile 1.7. Financial City North (Line 30) returns to its real platform (OSM station node 13380485918). Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 of Shuangliu (Line 10) and East of Terminal 2 keep the out-of-station stagger. Composition is unchanged, including the 0.4 R merges; the pill ends at Chengdu University of TCM and Xibei Bridge follow their platforms.
- **Final audit (2026-10-03): geography.** Inside the metro area, the drawn water banks agree with current OSM water polygons (`natural=water`, `waterway=riverbank`, `landuse=reservoir`) to a median of 0.65 units (90th percentile 2.2). Fixes:
  - The Fu River (涪江) at the north-east edge no longer breaks for about 130 units below the dam: OSM way 1358419804 and relation 6835470 fill the gap between relations 18693438 and 21311845.
  - An isolated stretch of the Qiuxi River (球溪河) south of the municipality was removed: it started and ended abruptly, and comparable tributaries outside the municipality are not drawn.
  - 16 water specks under 5 square units were removed, along with a canal stub drawn 5 units off its canal near Hexin Road.

  No station is in water before or after. Known limits: rivers stop where OSM bank mapping stops (the Baimo / Nan River above Qionglai; the Qingbaijiang’s west end at the municipal boundary). A few river stretches west of the centre are up to 5 units off OSM.

- **Final audit (2026-10-03): events.** Every entry from 2024 on was re-checked against news reports and zh.wikipedia, and no date changed. As of 2026-10-02 these are built but unopened, so they are not drawn: Bairendian (Line 27), Yuhong Road and Fenshui (Line 30), the Line 10 platforms at People’s Park and Wenweng Shishi, Longquanyi Railway Station (Line 2) and Lujia (Line S3). Hejiang (Line 19) is a turnback station closed to passengers. Apart from the Line 2 east section’s return on 2026-09-28, nothing opened, closed or was renamed between 2025-12-20 and 2026-10-02. Sources: [川观新闻, 2025-09](https://sichuan.scol.com.cn/ggxw/202509/83121414.html); [光明网, 2025-12-15](https://m.gmw.cn/2025-12/15/content_1304263968.htm); [Sichuan Online, 2025-12](https://sichuan.scol.com.cn/ggxw/202512/83172366.html); [Sichuan Online, 2026-09](https://sichuan.scol.com.cn/ggxw/202609/83330005.html); [zh.wikipedia: 成都地铁车站列表](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-cn/%E6%88%90%E9%83%BD%E5%9C%B0%E9%93%81%E8%BD%A6%E7%AB%99%E5%88%97%E8%A1%A8).

<a id="beijing"></a>

## Beijing (`beijing`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/beijing/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/beijing/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/beijing/map.svg).

New map and research, **24 September 2026**. Public passenger history begins on **15 January 1971**, when trial operation began with tickets sold against work-unit letters; restricted-access service counts under the spec §7 opening rule. The 1969 inauguration and the military tracks are not public openings. Includes the subway, Capital and Daxing airport railways, S1, and Xijiao / Yizhuang T1 as simplified tracks. The last recorded change is **30 June 2026** (Tongyun Men); the present-day review also includes the May 2026 Pingguoyuan interchange. A final review on **2 October 2026** found no later change: Line 22 has been in no-passenger trial operation since 25 August 2026 and is due to open at the end of the year. Temporary suspensions do not erase built infrastructure. National/suburban rail, construction projects and never-opened platforms are outside scope.

### Primary records and focused references

- **Early openings:** [Beijing Transport Vocational College’s historical account](https://www.bjjt.edu.cn/info/2005/19929.htm) records 1971-01-15, **1971-08-15**, 1971-11-07 and 1973-04-23; August 15 takes precedence over August 5 in the English summary table. The [Beijing Subway chronicle for 1971–1980](https://web.archive.org/web/2013/http://www.bjsubway.com/node/1842) gives the terms. From 1971-01-15 the trial operation had "实行内部售票，接待参观群众。售票办法，凭单位介绍信" (internal ticket sales, visiting groups, tickets only with a work-unit letter). The 1971-08-15 (Yuquan Lu) and 1971-11-07 (Gucheng) extensions ran on the same terms. Then "1972年12月27日，北京地铁由原凭证出售地铁票，改为免证件出售地铁票". Restricted-access service counts under the spec §7 opening rule, so Line 1 opens on the three 1971 dates; the change to sale without papers on 1972-12-27 is recorded as its own event, and so is the formal opening of 15 September 1981 ([北京地铁1号线](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-hans/北京地铁1号线) "1981年9月15日北京地下铁道一期工程正式验收…地铁一期工程运营线路从苹果园站至北京站区段正式对外开放"; [CCTV, 2021](https://m.news.cctv.com/2021/09/14/ARTIJ7l456BYqiLlhXnnh0hM210914.shtml) "1981年9月15日，全长27.6公里的北京地铁一期工程正式交付运营"). Neither changes the map. The 1971-09-13 – 11-06 and 1973-08-12 – 1974-06-30 war-preparedness stoppages are temporary suspensions (spec §7) and are not drawn. The [municipal history](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/gate/big5/www.beijing.gov.cn/ywdt/gzdt/202410/t20241005_3911383.html) corroborates the 1987 loop reorganization.
- **Line 13 eastern opening:** the [transport commission](https://jtw.beijing.gov.cn/xxgk/xwfbh/201912/t20191209_1007437.html) gives **2003-01-28**, correcting January 9 in some station lists. [Beijing’s construction gazette](https://zjw.beijing.gov.cn/bjjs/gcjs/sznj/zjcg/sz/10934391/2021020215473385426.pdf) covers the 1991–2010 projects.
- **Olympic Sports Center:** [the October 10 contemporary report](https://travel.sina.com.cn/around/2008-10-10/114429534.shtml) says the station first opened on **October 9**, rather than October 10 in the summary chronology. The same report says the whole Olympic branch "昨天(9日)清晨起…开始面向普通乘客开放" (opened to ordinary passengers from the morning of the 9th). Before that it could only be ridden with Olympic tickets or credentials ("乘客需要相关票证才能换乘到这条线上"). Restricted-access service counts under the spec §7 opening rule, so the branch opens on **2008-07-19** (Beitucheng is a Line 8/10 capsule from that day); Olympic Sports Center, which the Olympic service did not serve, opens on 2008-10-09.
- **Xi’erqi relocation:** [December 25, 2010 contemporary report](https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2010-12-25/125121705654.shtml). The new building was north of the old one; reported building separation is not a platform-centre coordinate. The map does not draw that separation: the pre-relocation marker shares the new station's point.
- **Qinghe reroute:** [transport commission construction notice](https://jtw.beijing.gov.cn/xxgk/xwfbh/201912/t20191209_1007592.html) and [February 17 contemporary report](https://news.sina.cn/gn/2019-02-17/detail-ihrfqzka6456088.d.html). The new alignment carried trains from **2019-02-17**; the station itself opened **2019-12-30**, not December 28. Track and station dates are deliberately separate.
- **Fares/transfers:** [2007 unified-fare report](https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2007-10-10/161514056608.shtml), [Dongzhimen’s original 2003 transfer arrangement](https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2003-01-23/0334884481.shtml), [Xizhimen’s transfer history](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/西直门站), and the [operator’s current ticket rules](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/page/instructions.html). Airport railways retain separate fares and operators, with internal station-complex capsules under the spec’s cross-system rule. Muxidi and Dazhongsi remain separate stations with connectors.
- **Muxidi:** [municipal transfer explanation](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202401/t20240117_3537679.html); a promised future paid-area corridor is not an opened corridor. [Dazhongsi’s station history](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/大钟寺站) describes the separate Line 12 / 13 stations.
- **2024 openings:** [municipal opening report](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/ywdt/gzdt/202412/t20241215_3965616.html), covering Lines 3/12 and Changping’s Jimen Qiao extension / Zhufang Bei.
- **2025 delayed stations and extensions:** [Dahong Men, November 8](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202511/t20251109_4266635.html); [MTR’s Line 17 middle-section opening release](https://www.mtr.com.hk/archive/corporate/en/press_release/PR-25-094-E.pdf); [Beijing Subway notices](https://www.bjsubway.com/) for Line 18 and Line 6’s Luyang extension on December 27; [the national urban-rail association’s 2025 new-section inventory](https://infosharingp2-oss.camet.org.cn/resources/manual/2026/01/04/759313381470277.pdf).
- **2026:** [Wangjing Xi on Line 17, January 31](https://english.beijing.gov.cn/livinginbeijing/transportation/beijingsubway/202601/t20260131_4480193.html); [Pingguoyuan’s three-line interchange, May 16](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202605/t20260516_4653696.html); [Tongyun Men, June 30](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202606/t20260629_4737846.html), [confirmed after opening](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202607/t20260701_4741334.html). On May 16 Line 1 returns to Pingguoyuan (closed since 2020-04-18, see Rebuild closures) directly into the new three-line capsule.
- **Rebuild closures (spec §7):** Pingguoyuan's Line 1 station closed "从2020年4月18日首班车起" for the Pingguoyuan hub and Line 1 branch works; passenger service ran Gucheng – Sihui Dong, trains turning empty at Pingguoyuan ([transport commission notice](https://jtw.beijing.gov.cn/xxgk/xwfbh//202004/t20200414_1803816.html), [新京报](https://m.bjnews.com.cn/detail/158717958715547.html)). It reopened on 2026-05-16 as the three-line interchange ("封站改造六年", [新京报](https://www.bjnews.com.cn/detail/1778909112129527.html)), so Gucheng – Pingguoyuan is drawn closed 2020-04-18 → 2026-05-16. Bajiao Amusement Park has been closed since 2025-06-02 with trains passing without stopping, for rebuilding as the interchange with the Line 1 branch; reopening is planned for May 2027 ([Beijing government notice](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202505/t20250524_4097185.html), still closed per [京报网, 2026-05-15](https://news.bjd.com.cn/2026/05/15/11746393.shtml)). Its marker ends on that day; the track is unchanged. Shorter closures after which the same stations reopened are temporary suspensions and are not drawn: Sanyuanqiao (Line 10) 2022-12-24 → 2023-03-18, Dongsi Shitiao (Line 2) 2023-11-25 → 2024-02-28, and Gucheng / Babaoshan 2026-02-15 → 2026-05-16 ([notice](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202602/t20260209_4503352.html)).
- **Not open as of the review (2 October 2026):** Line 22 (Hongmiao – Pinggu) began no-passenger trial running on 25 August 2026 ([municipal notice](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202608/t20260825_4836108.html): "8月25日…22号线（红庙—平谷）正式开启空载试运行…年底基本具备开通条件"), so Line 14's Hongmiao is also still unopened; Line 17's Guangqumen Wai remains deferred ([Beijing MTR line page](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/service/line/line-17.html): "其中广渠门外站暂缓开通"); the City Subcenter line upgrade of 1 July 2026 is suburban railway (outside scope); [Fushouling exit-design procurement, September 24](https://ggzyfw.beijing.gov.cn/jyxxggjtbyqs/20260924/5726978.html), [Guangqumenwai Line 17 construction permit](https://ghzrzyw.beijing.gov.cn/zhengwuxinxi/tzgg/dc/202606/t20260623_4712158.html). No speculative Line 22, M101, Line 13 split, Line 1 branch or Daxing Airport Express northern extension is drawn. Gaojiayuan, Hongmiao and Taoranqiao on Line 14 also remain unopened.

### Event-by-event source index

Descriptions are the map’s event inventory. Openings that skipped stations opened later carry the spec §10 clause “initially bypassing …” (or “with … unopened” for stations still closed), added 2026-10-03 from the line and station histories and the map's own station dates (the zh Wikipedia line and station articles, e.g. 双井站, 垡头站, 二里沟站, 军事博物馆站, 丰台东大街站, 安德里北街站, 角门东站, 望京东站, 大屯路东站 and 朱房北站, and Beijing MTR's English [Line 14](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/en/service/line/line-14.html), [Line 16](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/en/service/line/line-16.html) and [Line 17](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/en/service/line/line-17.html) pages); Line 10's 2013-05-05 section completes the loop ([北京地铁10号线](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京地铁10号线): "…至此10号线成为一条完整的环线"). The line histories above provide the baseline references; the focused records above settle the early-service, 2003, 2008, relocation, transfer and recent-opening corrections. Routine station upgrades, entrances, rolling stock, fares without a transfer-topology change, and temporary closures are not extra build events.
