### Names: decisions and remaining evidence gaps

- The 1984 northern section is labelled **Second Phase**, then **Loop Line** from 1987-12-28, then **Line 2** from 2002-07-24, following the [Chinese system chronology](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京地铁). The last exact day is a secondary historical reference, not a newly recovered primary naming notice. “Line 1” is used as the English name of the original first-phase service; the later Chinese change from 一线 to 1号线 does not create a different English name.
- **Fuba Line → Line 1**, 2000-06-28; **Airport Express → Capital Airport Express**, 2019-09-24 ([contemporary report](https://ie.bjd.com.cn/a/201909/24/AP5d89ca83e4b021e796143804.html)); **Line 1 / Batong**, 2021-08-29, models the merged service and permanent retirement of the redundant Sihui/Batong and Sihui Dong/Line 1 platforms. It is a combined service label, not a claim that the two infrastructure lines ceased to have administrative identities.
- **Broadcasting Institute → Communication University of China**, 2007-04-11, follows the April 12 contemporary report cited by [the station history](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/传媒大学站) ([archived report](https://web.archive.org/web/20171205143554/http://news.163.com/07/0412/18/3BT8B3GM000120GU.html)). The university’s 2004 rename was not the station rename.
- **City Railway / Line 13:** the numerical designation was already used at opening ([contemporary 2002 report](https://news.sohu.com/22/35/news203453522.shtml)); a [2025 retrospective](https://xinwen.bjd.com.cn/content/s6940aa98e4b06b6f7a7f8649.html) instead describes 2003-12-31 as formal naming. The map uses Line 13 from its first public day, without presenting the retrospective as a definite rename. **Olympic Branch / Line 8** likewise coexisted as names; it is not given a fabricated rename date.
- **Unresolved historical names:** Lixin → Gongzhufen (1980s), Bajiaocun → Bajiao Amusement Park (1990s), Xinhua Jie → Heping Men (1987), and Gucheng Lu → Gucheng (2008) lack verified exact days in the retrieved evidence. Markers retain current names; Line 1's 1971 terminus was then called Lixin. [Beijing Daily’s archive investigation](https://news.bjd.com.cn/2025/09/24/11321556.shtml) specifically contradicts treating the amusement park’s 1986 opening as the station rename. [The January 31, 2008 Gucheng reconstruction report](https://news.sina.com.cn/c/2008-01-31/021913356273s.shtml) still uses Gucheng Lu; the February 1 facility opening is not evidence of an exact rename day. Do not “complete” these by inventing January 1 dates.
- **Dahongmen Nan** (大红门南, Line 8) was misspelled _Dahongman Nan_ in the SVG label; corrected 2026-10-03 to the operator's English timetable spelling (bjsubway.com/en, archived 2026-02-05) and Amap. It is a typo fix, not a rename.
- English names use consistent current translations across a physical station. Beijing’s 2020–24 English-signage revisions were gradual and differed by operator/station; they are not modelled as simultaneous station renames. Qinghe’s added Chinese 站 is not a new English station identity. The proposed 2026 Tongzhou Beiguan rename is not recorded as an implemented change.
- **Line 1 1971–1972 and the Olympic branch (restricted access):** 1971's 试运营 sold tickets
  only against work-unit letters, and unrestricted sale began 1972-12-27
  ([Beijing Subway chronicle](https://web.archive.org/web/2013/http://www.bjsubway.com/node/1842)).
  Line 8's Olympic branch carried only Olympic ticket and credential holders until 2008-10-09
  ([Qianlong via Sina](https://travel.sina.com.cn/around/2008-10-10/114429534.shtml)). Under the
  spec §7 rule restricted-access service counts, so both appear on the earlier date with events
  naming the restricted service; the later opening to all passengers (1972-12-27, 2008-10-09) and
  Line 1's formal opening (1981-09-15) are separate events. Whether organised groups of citizens rode Line 1 in
  1969–1970, before trial operation, is not established (the 1965–1970 chronicle page was not
  retrieved); the recorded 1971-01-15 stays. Line 4's 2009-08-31 ride for about 200 relocated
  residents ([北京地铁4号线](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京地铁4号线)) was a one-off thank-you
  event, not public riding, and is not drawn. No other line had public rides before its recorded
  opening in the sources checked (Lines 5, 13, Batong, the 2010 lines, Xijiao and Yizhuang T1).

### SVG geography, identities and measurement limits

- **No starting map artwork:** railway ways, stop positions, Beijing’s municipal boundary ([OSM relation 912940](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/912940)) and water geometry were retrieved on **2026-09-24** from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), © OpenStreetMap contributors, [ODbL 1.0](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright). The SVG and preview are derived, edited geographic illustrations. The logo is [AlgaeGraphix’s public-domain geometric artwork](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Beijing_Subway_simplified_logo.svg), with JaJaWa’s official-colour revision. Stations on Beijing MTR's Lines 4, 14, 16, 17, 19 and the Daxing Line also show Beijing MTR's own emblem from each line's opening, cropped from [its Chinese Wikipedia logo file](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BJMTR_logo.svg) without the “京港地铁 BJMTR” lettering. That file is marked non-free (a trademark used under fair use).
- Coordinates use **WGS84 / UTM zone 50N (EPSG:32650)**, then `x = (easting − 408000) / 20`, `y = (4466000 − northing) / 20`, in a `4400 × 5300` viewBox. This places 1 km at 50 SVG units. Track, water and land use the same projection. The [Amap current network](https://map.amap.com/service/subway?srhdata=1100_drw_beijing.json) cross-checks current stops and English spellings; Zhufang Bei’s missing OSM stop position uses Amap coordinates with **GCJ-02 converted to WGS84**, projected onto the mapped railway.
- Curves follow rail-way vertices, simplified at 9 m and interpolated with cubic Béziers. Lines sharing a corridor are drawn 1 W apart around their OSM centre; elsewhere tracks follow OSM within about 2 units. Contiguous opening spans remain single paths, split only for actual historical changes, reassignments or reroutes. No per-station track fragmentation, station text, legend artwork or background labels are embedded.
- The original Line 1 connector uses [OSM way 114647613](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/114647613). Between Sihui and Sihui Dong Line 1 follows its mapped course and the Batong Line (2003–2021) is drawn 4.8 units south of it, where the real tracks run side by side (the 0.2-unit overlap of the two same-coloured tracks hides an anti-aliasing seam); since 2021 the merged line runs straight along Line 1's course. Qinghe’s old alignment uses **2018-01-01 OSM history**, replaced on 2019-02-17. Older small track shifts and rebuilt platform footprints without recovered engineering drawings remain generalized; present-day geometry is not proof that every metre was unchanged since opening.
- Capital Airport Express includes both the outbound route and the return branch from [relation 2062999](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/2062999). Its reversing Terminal 3 spur is traversed twice by the continuous SVG path, but physical route kilometres are counted once. It is not an invented triangle between airport station points.
- The geography is **present-day throughout playback**. Beijing land is the normal land colour; neighbouring Hebei is the foreign-land colour, including the Daxing Airport approach. Lakes and mapped riverbank polygons preserve holes; river/canal centreline buffers fill gaps where OSM has no bank polygon. Those small-watercourse widths are cartographic estimates, not historical or surveyed banks. Land and water simplification tolerances are 12 m and 7 m respectively.
- Xizhimen, Dongzhimen, Sihui and Sihui Dong retain their separate-fare/out-of-station phases. Muxidi and Dazhongsi have distinct station IDs; circle-to-interchange replacements share an identity with dated `--YYYY-MM-DD` versions. Pingguoyuan's Line 1 circle ends when the station closes on 2020-04-18; the 6/S1 interchange (2021-12-31) stands alone until the three-line interchange opens on 2026-05-16, when a separate Line 1 track ends at the rebuilt platform. Xijiao/T1 have tracks only except memberships at Bagou/Rongchang Dongjie, following the simplified-service rule.
- **Kilometres are approximate by opening stage.** Modern totals use the published line overviews, checked against [the operator’s interstation-distance tables](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/service/line/distable/line-1.html). These definitions differ: construction length, running length and station-centre distance can include different turnbacks/overruns. Values are allocated and rounded to one decimal per historical span; they are not SVG arc lengths. The sum currently shown is **903.1 km**, not the municipal **909 km** headline. That definition/allocation discrepancy remains unresolved; the map does not force an arbitrary extra 5.9 km into a section. Line 14 (2026-09-29 correction): the stages use the operator's published lengths, 12.4 km west (2013), 14.8 km east (2014) and 16.6 km middle (2015) ([People's Daily Beijing, 2021](http://bj.people.com.cn/n2/2021/0529/c14540-34750727.html), [MTR Beijing 2014](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/article/5d510c19ebb1a36f5ef59940.html), [Beijing Youth Daily 2015](https://web.archive.org/web/20151227003439/http://epaper.ynet.com/html/2015-12/25/content_173678.htm)). Xiju – Beijing South (2021) gets the 7.0 km remainder of the operator's current **50.8 km** ([line overview](https://www.mtr.bj.cn/service/line/line-14.html)), matching the 6.78 km station-to-station distance. The municipal "剩余段长约4公里" and 47.3 km total ([2021-12-14 notice](https://www.beijing.gov.cn/fuwu/bmfw/sy/jrts/202112/t20211214_2560258.html)) count only the Dongguantou – Jingfengmen new build. Tram stops are deliberately excluded from the station statistic, and Line 1/Batong is one current legend entry, so app counts must not be equated with the official “30 lines / 541 stations” per-line inventory.
- OSM position audit (2026-09-29): Longzexi (Line 18, 19 units) and Changchun Jie (Line 2, 10 units) slid along their tracks to OSM. The Airport Express now ends on its Dongzhimen platform point. Bajiao Amusement Park is drawn closed from 2025-06-02 (see Rebuild closures).
- OSM audit (2026-09-30): Xinfadi's Line 19 bulge removed (the 2026-10-03 corridor pass now puts Line 19 and the Daxing Airport Express 1 W apart about their OSM centre, Xinfadi within 1.1 units of its platform). Historical circles moved to their platforms (Fuxingmen 1984, Dongzhimen Line 13 2003, Suzhou Jie 2008, Shuangjing 2008, Beijing South 2009, Lize Shangwuqu 2021), with track splits, connectors and later interchanges following. Dazhong Si (13) and the National Art Museum were later moved onto their real platforms (2026-10-03, below). Changchun Jie's tracks now split at its moved centre. Line 16 runs 1 W west of Line 9 at Fengtai Nanlu, Line 3 1 W south of Line 12 into Dongba Bei, the Changping Line 1 W west of Line 13 from Xi'erqi, crossing to its east side about 0.5 km north of Qinghe where OSM crosses (it runs east of Line 13 through Qinghe, 2026-10-03); Line 1 is straight through Gongzhufen on its OSM alignment.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: 234 OSM platform points (platform ways matched to each line's route relation, else stop positions), projected with the exact UTM 50N formula onto the drawn tracks. There is no line-map reference. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Sanyuan Qiao's Line 10 and Airport Express platforms are separate boxes (OSM levels −4 and −2), the Airport Express drawn 1 W north-west of Line 10 through the station (track moved up to 5 units). Bridges are straight, since OSM maps no in-station walkways. Capsule-fitting bends of about 1.2 W at some 40 crossings follow OSM again; corridors are 1 W apart (Changping/13 symmetric about the OSM centreline at Xi'erqi, 17/13, 8/6, 16/4). Every track end at a station lies on its platform point or circle centre (largest trims: Fuxingmen Line 2 7.0 units, Pingguoyuan S1 6.5, Huazhuang Batong 6.3, Dongguantou Nan 6.3); 96 circles moved onto their platforms (up to 8.7 units, Liuli Qiao). Pingguoyuan's 2026 Line 1 track is split off at the rebuilt station; Sihui and Sihui Dong 2007–2021 are two dots at the real side-by-side platforms (2026-10-03).
- Final audit (2026-10-01): Line 6 runs straight through Pingguoyuan on its OSM alignment, 1 W north of S1, replacing a 76° hook; nine circles 0.25–0.29 units off their tracks now sit on them (Bei Yuan, Zhangzizhong Lu, Lishuiqiao Nan, Yongtaizhuang, Jijiamiao, Zuojiazhuang, Anzhen Qiao, Jiangtaixi, Anzhenmen). The Airport Express reversal at Terminal 2 and its loop are real route features. Out-of-station pairs keep the spec stagger: Dongzhimen 2003–2007 as recorded; Xizhimen 1984–2008's Line 2 circle sits on its own track at its platform (2026-10-03; it was 2.6 units off the track); Sihui/Sihui Dong 2003–2007 put the terminating line's circle at its real terminus and stagger the through line's circle 12.6 units along its own track.
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): every track is tangent-continuous (no direction jump over 12°). Short stubs left by end trims at Dongzhimen (Airport Express, both sections) and Xi'erqi (Changping Line, 2010) are removed, so each track ends on its platform point with its own tangent. The Line 9 approach to National Library, the S1 joint at Jin'anqiao and the Changping crossing north of Qinghe are single smooth Bézier bends (changes of 2.1 units or less, within 1 W of OSM or of the corridor spacing). The only sharp turn left is the real reversal at Terminal 2, inside its circle.
- Interchange shapes (2026-10-01, spec §5 rule 2; Beijing has no reference line map): one shape only where the lines share track or their platforms cross one over the other in plan (a full "+"), judged from zh Wikipedia 车站结构/换乘 sections and OpenStreetMap platforms (where the crossing falls along each platform). No Beijing interchange has two lines on the same tracks. Full stacked crossings, one circle on the drawn crossing: Beitaipingzhuang, Caishikou, Capital University of Economics and Business, Ciqikou, Ciqu, Dongsi Shitiao, Erligou, Haidian Huangzhuang, Huilongguan Dongdajie, Huixin Xijie Nankou, Hujialou, Jianguomen, Jiaomenxi, Jiulongshan, Lize Shangwuqu, Liuliqiao, Shuangjing, Suzhou Jie, Tuanjiehu, Xizhimen (Lines 2/4) and Xuanwumen. Everything else is separate dots at the real platforms with a bridge, overlapping where close: cross-platform and side-by-side pairs on their own tracks (Beijing West, Guogongzhuang, National Library, Xi'erqi, Zhuxinzhuang, Qinghe, Huazhuang, Universal Resort, Dongbabei, Yancun Dong, Fengtai Nanlu, Jin'anqiao, Shilihe, Caoqiao), T and L layouts where one platform's end meets the other (Fuxingmen, Gongzhufen, Beitucheng, Beijing South, Chaoyangmen, Changchunqiao, Chaoyang Park, Jintai Lu, Mudanyuan, Workers' Stadium, Dongguantou Nan, Cishousi, Lishuiqiao, Pingguoyuan, Songjiazhuang), and platforms joined by passages or halls. Separate parallel platforms are not squared across the corridor. Renmin University (2026-10-02) is a T, so it is two dots: zh Wikipedia describes a T-shaped transfer by three one-way passages, with the Line 4 platform at the west end of the deeper Line 12 platform, and the Line 12 exits E/F are about 120 m east of the crossing (OSM).
- Close platforms (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump even fully zoomed in, so they are drawn as one shape through the same platform points, which do not move: Gongzhufen (Line 1 and Line 10, 0.26 R); Jintai Lu (Line 14 and Line 6, 0.27 R); Mudanyuan (Line 10 and Line 19, 0.38 R); National Library (Line 4 and Line 9, 0.36 R); Pingguoyuan (Line 1 and Line 6, 0.39 R); Workers Stadium (Line 17 and Line 3, 0.39 R). Pairs 0.4 R or more apart stay separate dots. Caoqiao (Line 19 and Daxing Airport Express) was one shape at 0.21 R until the 2026-10-03 corridor pass put each line on its own drawn track at its own stops (0.51 R): two dots.
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): Line 1 of 1971-01-15 (three pieces, handed over 1987-12-28), the Fuba Line of 1999-09-28 (two pieces, handed over 2021-08-29), Line 13 of 2002-09-28 (three pieces, handed over 2019-02-17) and the Batong Line of 2003-12-27 (two pieces, handed over 2021-08-29) each grow as one path. 1 other single-piece opening now grows from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.
- Final audit (2026-10-03). **Tracks:** a per-date sliver check of every pair of lines found side-by-side runs that neither touched nor kept a standard gap; they are now exactly 1 W apart (touching), symmetric about the centre of the two lines' OSM centrelines where both are offset, otherwise with one line kept on its course: Line 7 / Line 1-Batong Huazhuang – Universal Resort (they overlapped almost completely), Lines 13/17 at Wangjing Xi and north of Dongzhimen, Daxing Airport Express / Line 19 Caoqiao – Xinfadi (and the DAE's 1.5-unit hook at Caoqiao removed), Changping / Line 13 Qinghe – Xi'erqi (crossing moved to where OSM crosses), Lines 13/18 west of Longzexi, 6/8 at Nanluogu Xiang, 2/8 east of Qianmen, and shorter runs at Zhuxinzhuang (8), Dongzhimen (13 beside 2), Guogongzhuang (9), Fengtai Nanlu (16), Beijing West (7), Dongbabei (3), Sanyuan Qiao (12 beside the Capital Airport Express), Jin'anqiao (6 beside S1), Songjiazhuang (5 beside 10) and Bagou (the Xijiao Line beside Line 10, not on top of it). The sliver check went from 70 runs to 29; those left are shallow crossings, junctions of one line's own branches, the same-colour Line 1/Batong overlap of 0.2 and the Sanyuan Qiao station knot. Takeover pieces stay identical to the tracks they continue (1971/1987 Line 1–2, 2002/2019 Line 13, 1999/2021 Line 1, 2003/2021 Batong). `data-km` is unchanged (published lengths). Crossings at a shallow angle, branch junctions and the Sanyuan Qiao station knot are left as drawn. **Stations:** dots moved to the real platform centre (OSM platform ways, or the midpoint of a line's two stop positions): eleven Line 8 stations whose circles sat on one stop position at a platform end (Tianqiao, Jinyu Hutong, Muxi Yuan, Haihutun, Dahongmen Nan, Heyi, Donggaodi, Huojian Wanyuan, Wufutang, Demao and the Yinghai terminus with its track end, about 3 units each), Gaoloujin (3.2), Wangjing Nan (2.7), Qiaowan (4.0); clearance shifts undone (accuracy over clearance): Xinjie Kou on Line 19 (6.5), the National Art Museum terminus on Line 6 (6.7, with the 2018/2021 joint), Guangqumen Wai beside Line 17 (6.0), and Dazhong Si (13) at its platform until the 2024 out-of-station pair (a new element `station-dazhong-si-13--2024-12-15` keeps the spec stagger from then); dots earlier slid along their tracks for spacing returned to their platforms with the corridors (Universal Resort 7, Huazhuang 7, Qinghe Changping, Wangjing Xi 17, Sihui/Sihui Dong). Checked and left: crossing circles within R of their platforms (Caishi Kou, Liuli Qiao, Jiulongshan, Jianguomen and others), Renmin University, Changchun Qiao and Anhua Qiao T layouts (Line 12 platforms beside, not under, the crossing; [安华桥站](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/安华桥站) "位于既有8号线车站东侧"), Shangdi Software Park (its OSM stop is still tagged under construction), Pingguoyuan 1973–2020 (no evidence on the old platform). **Geography:** the principal rivers missing from the canvas were added as 2.4-unit symbolic centreline buffers of OSM `waterway=river` (Overpass, 2026-10-02): the Juma (Beijing's Daqing system) with the North/South Juma, Baigou and Daqing, the Dashi through Fangshan, the Ju through Pinggu with the Ji Canal to the sea, and the Sanggan and Yang headwaters of the Yongding (which had stopped at their confluence in mid-canvas); fills cover old bank strokes at the joins. 23 simplification spikes and 8 stray sliver fragments (<0.8 units wide) were removed from `inland-water`. The Haihe banks in Tianjin differ from OSM's Haihe centreline by up to about 60 units east of the city; not changed without imagery (outside Beijing).

<a id="nanjing"></a>

## Nanjing (`nanjing`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/nanjing/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/nanjing/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/nanjing/map.svg).

Checked through **2026-10-02** (no opening, closure or rename between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-02). The map includes the sixteen operating metro/suburban lines
(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9), plus Hexi and Qilin trams as
simplified tracks. S4 and the trams are the operator's own lines (spec §8). S4 includes its operating Chuzhou section; the unbuilt connection into
Nanjing and its reserved stations are not shown. Lines 9, 11 and the other announced
extensions are not treated as open. The [September 23 operator service announcement](https://www.nanjing.gov.cn/zzb/hdhy/hygq_72666/202609/t20260923_5916215.html)
and [April S2 opening report](https://www.jiangning.gov.cn/sjb/xwzx/gzdt/202604/t20260424_5829714.html)
were checked alongside the individual line histories. This is a construction history:
COVID, flooding, repairs, service hours and temporary testing suspensions do not remove
unchanged infrastructure.

### Opening and conversion chronology

The English and Chinese [system history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanjing_Metro),
[station inventory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nanjing_Metro_stations) and individual
line articles were used as indexes, then compared with contemporary reports. In particular,
under the spec §7 rule Line 1 appears on May 15, 2005 with weekend sightseeing (观光运营)
between Xinjiekou and Xiaohang. The weekend sightseeing ended on July 31 and the line carried
no public until August 12 (a pause the map does not draw, spec §7), when every station between Maigaoqiao and Xiaohang opened with daily
fare-paying "simulated operation" (模拟运营), which reached Olympic Stadium on August 26. The
September 3 start of trial operation (试运营), the regular opening, is its own event.

The "Map change" column summarises each date's `events.json` descriptions rather than copying them.

### Geometry, identities and distance

- Drawn from railway ways and stop positions in [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/),
  © OpenStreetMap contributors, [ODbL 1.0](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), retrieved
  September 24, 2026. All railways and geography share EPSG:32650, at 50 SVG units/km.
- Line 6's track is way 736817854; its OSM route relations 21457471/21457468 (partial, eight stops) were checked 2026-09-30, and Shiyueguangchang was moved 11.7 units to their stop positions. Pegasus Park (白马公园), mapped on the line, has not opened. Current route relations: 1533791, 3413088, 7885542, 9588280, 17417176, 15336345,
  1529760, 7913265, 19979191, 7913253, 15804056, 13200480, 9584584, 9588173,
  9584574; tram routes 16159337 and 16159339. These supply alignment, not opening dates.
- OSM audit (2026-09-30): Line 6 and Line 4 run side by side 1 W apart on Banchang Street (Gangzicun – Huayuanlu), and Line 4 and Line 2 between Xianhemen and Jinmalu (Line 4 crosses Line 2 at Jinmalu, whose shared platforms are one marker). Fuguishan stays at its OSM construction footprint (OSM station node 1.1 units away; Amap places it 12–14 units off; no stop position yet). Xingxuelu moved on 2026-10-03 to the stop positions mapped after the opening (nodes 14237795853/14237795854): 12.5 units east of the footprint, where Amap, the OSM station node, station building and four entrances also put it.
- The retired Andemen approach is recovered from pre-conversion relation 1529760/version 19;
  the old Hexi southern alignment from way 736715174/version 9. Recovering deleted OSM
  nodes is a cartographic reconstruction, not evidence of service dates. The reusable track
  north/west of those changes is not duplicated into one path per station interval.
- Background land is present-day Jiangsu, relation 913012; Anhui has the foreign-land fill.
  Yangtze bank polygons preserve islands; Xuanwu, Mochou, Shijiu, Gucheng and Jinniu lakes
  use mapped polygons. Historical shoreline changes are not animated. Minor ponds and streams
  are omitted. Curves simplify mapped vertices; they are not survey drawings.
- Marker versions share a stable identity through circle-to-interchange upgrades. Zhushanlu is the
  explicit out-of-station exception. Tram stops are omitted apart from their existing heavy-rail
  interchange markers, per the shared specification.
- The current inventory has **313 line/platform memberships at 274 distinct marker identities**.
  Official headline station totals often count a transfer once for each line: the December 2025
  announcement's 267 equals the sum of platform counts before adding S2's sixteen and S4's ten.
- `data-km` uses published route/section lengths rounded to tenths; the early Line 1 sightseeing
  and reused western sections are apportioned within the published line totals. These subdivisions
  are approximate, not surveyed distances. Current metro/suburban paths sum to **656.9 km**;
  including the simplified trams gives **673.7 km**. This does not exactly reproduce the roughly
  625.7 km headline metro total published before Line 6 plus Line 6's 32.4 km: published construction and operating lengths differ. No invisible
  length or phantom track was added to force a match.
- [Nanjing Metro logo](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Nanjing_Metro_Logo.svg): public-domain
  geometric mark; the Commons SVG was corrected by Tomchen1989 using the operator's mark.
- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: the map is an exact UTM 50N projection at 50 units/km (median station residual 0.3 units), so OSM stop positions give each line's platform directly, placed on its drawn track (and, since 2026-10-03, the drawn track runs on the OSM centreline at every station outside the side-by-side stretches below). There is no line-map reference. Which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Station jogs of 5–6 units on Lines 2, 3, 5 and 7, left from earlier straight markers, were redrawn to OSM, and the Qilin tram follows OSM into Maqun (up to 14.7 units) to end at its stop. Maqun is a Line 2 circle until 2017-10-31 and an interchange from then. Track ends and split points lie on their platform points.
- Final audit (2026-10-01): Andemen's three-way Line 1 junction now meets at the Line 1 platform, removing a 2-unit hook beside the 2005–2014 circle, and S6's Maqun start no longer hooks back under the marker; every station lies on its line and every track end on a platform point.
- Smoothness pass (2026-10-01): a smoothness pass drew Lines 2 and 7 through their shared corridor at Mochouhu (about 1.1 km, OSM tracks 1–2 units apart) as parallel tracks 1 W apart around the OSM centre, Line 2 on the north side, crossing once where Line 7 turns north (they had overlapped and crossed back and forth); Mochouhu now reads as one blob across both lines. The source corners at Xinjiekou (Line 1, 27°) and Youfangqiao (Line 2, 13°) became tangent-continuous curves. Remaining double crossings are not weaves: Line 1's 2005–2014 Xiaohang approach and Line 10 share one alignment but never coexist, and S1 and S3 cross once inside the Nanjing South marker (stop order) and once where S1 really turns south.
- Interchange composition (2026-10-01): spec §5 rule 2 (no reference line map), from the zh.wikipedia 车站结构 sections and the OpenStreetMap stops. One shape only for **shared track**: Nanjing South's S1/6 (Line 6 runs through onto S1's tracks, 贯通运行) and Konggangxinchengjiangning's S1/S7 (同台换乘 with through trains); and for a **full stacked crossing** (one platform directly over the other's middle): Minggugong (Line 6's platform passes under Line 2's, 十字交叉; one circle on the drawn crossing), Zhongsheng (立体十字交叉; one circle) and Wutangguangchang (stairs at the middle of both platforms; one circle on the drawn crossing since 2026-10-03, when Line 3 was put back on its real course and both stops came within R of the crossing, 1.9 and 2.9 units; it had been a short pill while Line 7's stop lay just over R from the jogged crossing). Yuantong (Line 1/10 over Line 2, 垂直换乘) and Caochangmen (节点换乘通道 between the Line 7 and Line 4 platforms) stay one pill through their real stops: the sources do not say whether the platforms cross at their middles. Everything else is separate dots at the real platforms joined by a bridge, overlapping where close: T and L nodes where one platform's end meets the other (Xinjiekou, Xiaozhuang, Luotanglu, Shanghailu, Daxinggong, Jimingsi, Fuzimiao, Jiyindadao, Dajiaochang, Guanghuamen, Fujianlu, Wanshou; Xinjiekou and Jiyindadao are now one shape under the 0.4 R exception below), cross-platform pairs on their own tracks (Nanjing South's Lines 1/3 and its S3 beside S1/6, Xiangyulunan's S1 outer / S9 inner tracks), side-by-side or parallel stations (Andemen, Xishanqiao, Gangzicun, Jinmalu's ground and B1 islands joined through the concourse), and passages and concourse walks (Nanjing Railway Station, Gulou, Sanshanjie, Youfangqiao, Mochouhu, Maqun, Taifenglu, Kazimen, Chengxindadao, Yunnanlu, Yongchulu, Jichangpaodaojiuzhi, Yuantong's Hexi tram stop, and Nanjing South's 240 m corridor). Earlier single-line circles sit on their own line's platform in the interchange that follows.
- Close platforms (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump even fully zoomed in, so they are drawn as one shape through the same platform points, which do not move: Fujianlu (Line 5 and Line 7, 0.12 R); Fuzimiao (Line 3 and Line 5, 0.35 R); Gangzicun (Line 4 and Line 6, 0.38 R); Gulou (Line 1 and Line 4, 0.27 R, from 2026-10-03); Jinmalu (Line 2 and Line 4, 0.07 R); Jiyindadao (Line 5 and S1, 0.26 R, from 2026-10-03); Maqun (Line 2 and S6, 0.14 R); Nanjing South Railway Station (S1 and S3, 0.09 R; with Line 6 from 2026-09-29, one circle, 0.05 R); Shanghailu (Line 2 and Line 5, 0.20 R); Xinjiekou (Line 1 and Line 2, 0.19 R, from 2026-10-03); Xishanqiao (Line 7 and S2, 0.08 R). Pairs 0.4 R or more apart stay separate dots (Taifenglu 0.48 R, Jimingsi 0.49 R and Yunnanlu 0.55 R after this audit).
- Track fix (2026-10-02): S6 now ends at its real Maqun platform centre, 6.8 units (135 m) west of its old end. The source is OpenStreetMap island platform way 982363793, beside the Line 2 viaduct. The track leaves along the platform and rejoins its earlier curve about 11 units east. East of the station it is drawn touching Line 2 (exactly 1 W from its centreline since 2026-10-03, where it had overlapped Line 2 by up to 0.5 units), up to about 3.3 units south of the OSM tunnels, so it stays visible beside Line 2. The S6 dot moved with the track end and now overlaps the Line 2 dot (0.14 R apart, their real separation).
- Track segments (2026-10-02, spec §4 one growth per event): Line 1 of 2005-05-15 (two pieces, handed over 2014-06-01) and the Hexi Tram of 2014-08-01 (two pieces, handed over 2021-05-07) each grow as one path. 2 other single-piece openings now grow from the end that meets the network already open. Geometry, km and colours are unchanged; this was checked by km per line on every date and by a tracks-only pixel comparison on every change date and the day before.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), tracks: markers are dots at the real platforms, so nothing needs a track to bend round a marker any more. Twenty interchanges still had a station jog of 2–6.7 units (about 1 W) in one or both lines, left from the earlier pill markers: Xiaozhuang (Lines 1, 7), Nanjing Railway Station (1, 3), Gulou (1), Xinjiekou (1), Sanshanjie (1, 5), Yuantong (2), Daxinggong (2), Youfangqiao (2, S3), Luotanglu (2), Taifenglu (3), Wutangguangchang (3), Jimingsi (3), Kazimen (3, 10), Chengxindadao (3, 5), Caochangmen (4), Yunnanlu (4), Jiyindadao (5), Zhushanlu (1, 5), Dajiaochang (10) and Yongchulu (S3). Those 14 tracks now follow the OSM route-relation centreline (midway between the two running tracks) there, refitted as tangent-continuous curves (within 0.08 units of it). The platform points at the same OSM stops were re-projected, along with the predecessor circles and Zhushanlu's connector: 41 points moved 1.5–6.7 units, nearly all sideways. Track pieces meeting at a moved station move together (Line 1 at Xinjiekou, including the 2014 takes-over piece; Line 2 at Youfangqiao). Line 5 ends at its real Jiyindadao platform, 6.0 units from its old end. Zhushanlu's out-of-station circles keep their stagger from the drawn crossing (13.6 units along Line 1, 11.2 along Line 5; 2.08 R apart). Line 2's dog-leg between Olympic Stadium East and Yuantong is gone. Track lengths changed by under 0.5%; `data-km` is unchanged (spec §4).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), side-by-side stretches: neighbouring lines in a shared corridor now touch exactly (centres 1 W = 5.0 units apart, 3.5 for the tram beside a metro line). Before, they had hairline background gaps (5.1–5.7 units) or partial overlaps (2–4.9 units). This covers Line 6/Line 4 on Banchang Street, Line 4/Line 2 from Xianhemen to Jinmalu on both sides (the convergence now lies under the Jinmalu marker), Line 7/Line 2 at Mochouhu (Line 7's dot moved 0.2), S6/Line 2 east of Maqun, S9/S1 for 150 units south of Xiangyulunan, S3/S1 on the western approach to Nanjing South, Line 3/Line 1 south of Nanjing South (Line 3's platform moved 0.9) and Line 10/Line 1 north of Andemen. S9 used to start on S1's track 6.3 units north of the stop. It now starts at its real cross-platform stop, beside the S1 dot. The Hexi tram had run on top of Line 2 (Olympic Stadium East – Yuantong, and at Yuzui) and of S3 (Pingliangdajie – Wuhoujie). It is now drawn touching them on its real side (north-west of Line 2, north of S3). It passes under the shared S3 circles and ends inside the Olympic Stadium East and Yuzui circles, as a simplified line may (spec §8); the 2014 and 2021 pieces were edited identically. The remaining short wedges, where lines diverge or converge at an angle, are natural.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), joints: seven tangent jumps (2–20°) and tiny leftover pieces (0.01–0.5 units long) on Lines 1, 3, 7 and 10 and on S3 and S7 were smoothed by local refits that move the line by at most 0.24 units. Every track end lies on a platform point of its line, and every platform lies on its line (within 0.5). The two takes-over continuations still lie on the tracks they replace (within 0.0005).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), Line 6 stops: OSM gained stop positions for Xingxuelu, Xingzhijie and Yanjiangxincheng after the opening (snapshot 2026-10-02); those circles moved 12.5, 2.4 and 0.5 units along Line 6 to them. Fuguishan, Hongshanxincheng, Yingtiandongjie, Zhongheqiao and Nanjing Hospital of C.M. still have no stop positions and stay at their footprints and station nodes (all within 2.5 units).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), geography: checked against the OSM waterway lines (river/canal) and river/canal polygons over the whole canvas (Overpass, 2026-10-02) and all water in central Nanjing. The water rings are valid, no station lies in water, and the central lakes, the outer Qinhuai and the Yangtze banks match OSM. Minor channels are omitted by design: the inner Qinhuai, the moats and the dense Taihu-plain canal network. The 64 needle-like tips (under 0.2 units wide) are narrow tails of the mapped polygons, for example the 2 km tail of way 1525414032 (滁河, `water=lake`) north of Liuhe, so they were kept. No geography was changed.

### Remaining evidence gaps

These are limitations, not verified exact-date claims:

1. **Early sightseeing extensions:** contemporary reports establish the May 15 Xinjiekou–Xiaohang
   sightseeing and the August 12 all-station service. Earlier plans mentioned June trips to Gulou
   and July trips to Maigaoqiao, but no implemented start date was established for either (a later
   personal account describes a June 4 Gulou trip). The map does not invent June 1 / July 1 dates,
   so track north of Xinjiekou starts on August 12. The May 12 rehearsal for invited press and
   newspaper readers is not drawn: how the readers were chosen is unknown, so it is not shown to
   have been open to the public (spec §7).
2. **Linjiang / YOGSP:** a secondary station account places the addition of “YOGSP” in December
   2016, without a verified day. The stable base name **Linjiang** is retained across the timeline;
   the full later suffix and its transition remain unencoded. It is not backdated to opening.
3. **Caochangmen and Xuzhuang subtitles:** Chinese institutional prefixes changed to subtitles in 2018. The cited approval is February 13; reports describe implementation in March. The map uses
   the English base names throughout, rather than claiming a synchronized English signage change
   on the approval date. Other inconsistent English abbreviations in the network (CPU, NJCI,
   NMU / JIETT) likewise do not establish dated operational renames.
4. **Invited-group rides not counted:** Line 2's 23–26 May 2010 "部分市民代表试乘" (citizen
   representatives, known only from Baidu Baike) is not treated as public riding; Line 2 keeps
   its recorded opening.

Validation checks SVG/legend/event boundary agreement, station memberships, unique IDs, path counts
and distances. Browser checks exercise all event dates and adjacent days in both directions,
search identities, highlighted-line filtering, tooltip dismissal, mobile resize and the home preview.
These checks validate the implementation; they do not resolve the historical evidence gaps above.

<a id="chongqing"></a>

## Chongqing — Rail Transit (`chongqing`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/chongqing/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/chongqing/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/chongqing/map.svg).
Research cutoff: **2 October 2026**. New geographic artwork, not a converted network diagram.

### Scope and line histories

Includes Lines 1, 2, 3 (including its airport branch), 4, 5, 6 (including the Chongqing East branch),
9, 10, 18, the Loop Line, International Expo Line, Jiangtiao, Bitong and the simplified Bishan
SkyShuttle. The Expo branch has its own legend identity, using its longstanding 国博线 name.
The 3 and 6 branches retain their parent line identity. Through trains on 4/Loop/5 and 5/Jiangtiao
do not duplicate the underlying infrastructure.

Openings follow the spec §7 opening rule: the first day the public could ride, including paid
sightseeing, trial operation, free trial rides and experience weeks. Temporary maintenance, accident, epidemic and integration-test
suspensions do not erase built lines. No never-opened stations or proposed extensions are drawn.
This is the rail-transit network, not every historical transport mode in Chongqing: the separate
river cableways, funiculars, escalators, national railways and scenic park rides are outside scope.

The following secondary line histories and their station tables were read as an inventory and
cross-checked with dated announcements. They also index intermediate stations not named in the
short event descriptions. Recovered Weibo/WeChat citations are identified explicitly; recovering
a citation does not mean the original post was independently retrievable.

### Date and interchange decisions

- **Line 2:** the first public rides were paid sightseeing, followed by trial running and then
  regular service; every stage is drawn (spec §7). Contemporary Chongqing papers carried on Sina
  (event rows above) establish which stations passengers could board or leave at:
  - **2004-11-06, Daping–Zoo, weekend mornings.** Tickets were sold only at Daping and Zoo. Trains
    paused at Yuanjiagang, Xiejiawan and Yangjiaping so riders could look at the platforms, then went
    on. Nobody could start or end a journey there, so only the termini are shown.
  - **2004-12-11, Jiaochangkou–Zoo, weekends.** Riders could board or alight only at Jiaochangkou,
    Daxigou, Daping and Zoo ("只在大溪沟和大坪停留上下客").
  - **2004-12-28, daily trial running.** Nine stations: Jiaochangkou, Linjiangmen, Daxigou,
    Niujiaotuo, Liziba, Daping, Yuanjiagang, Yangjiaping and Zoo. Huanghuayuan, Zengjiayan,
    Fotuguan and Xiejiawan were skipped.
  - **Later stations.** Huanghuayuan opened 2005-02-09, Xiejiawan by 2005-03-31 (display bound, day
    unreported), Fotuguan 2005-04-09 and Zengjiayan 2005-06-15 (zh-wiki; bounded by contemporary
    reports). Regular service (正式运行) began 2005-06-18
    ([People's Daily Chongqing, 2020](http://cq.people.com.cn/n2/2020/0618/c365405-34095403.html)).
  - **Not counted.** The October 2004 载人模拟运行 carried invited riders only. zh-wiki's
    2005-06-18 (Huanghuayuan) and 2006-07-10 (Xiejiawan) conflict with the contemporary reports and
    are not used. The 2004 sightseeing and trial-running fares are not recorded (spec §10).
- **Gaomiaocun:** October 17, 2011, as in the Chinese station chronology and contemporary
  October 13 announcement. The English opening table's November 17 date is inconsistent.
- **Line 6 north:** December 31, 2013 adds five operating stations, including Jinshansi.
  Caojiawan, Xiangjiagang and Tiansheng open later. An opening table that counts four omitted Jinshansi.
- **Bitong:** appears on December 26, 2024 with the free "欢乐体验周" (happy experience week),
  which ran without a break to the January 2, 2025 start of 初期运营, recorded as the opening
  (spec §7). Bishan is an
  out-of-station interchange during the week, because riders changing to Line 1 had to leave the
  gates, and in-station from January 2 ([12371.gov.cn](https://m.12371.gov.cn/content/2024-12/24/content_480523.html);
  [CNR](https://cq.cnr.cn/jr/20250107/t20250107_527033802.shtml) "支持站内换乘"). Qinglonghu was not
  one of the eight opened stations.
- **SkyShuttle:** free public trial rides at five stations, including both termini, ran February
  15–24, 2021 ([Chongqing Daily via chinanews](http://www.cq.chinanews.com.cn/wap/news/2021/0222/39-19761.html)).
  The line then carried no public until regular operation on April 16; that pause is not drawn
  (spec §7), so the SkyShuttle stays on the map from February 15.
  Individual SkyShuttle stops are omitted under the shared simplified-service rule.
- **Paid areas:** Shapingba's Line 1, Loop and Line 9 markers remain separate until September 30,
  2022; Xiejiawan's Line 2/Loop markers merge June 17, 2023. Guanyinqiao, Xietaizi, Yangjiaping and
  Yudaishan remain outside interchanges. Xietaizi has three separate station identities after its
  delayed Line 18 opening. The Line 18 opening notice identifies Fuhualu, Olympic Sports Center,
  Baijusi and Tiaodeng as in-station transfers from opening; no invented later conversion is added.
  See the [2026 operator network map](https://jtj.cq.gov.cn/zwgk_240/zfxxgkml/gggs/tzgg/202603/W020260302622398077574.pdf)
  and the dated passage notices above. The PDF's indexed text was available; direct PDF download
  was unavailable during this audit.
- **Cutoff:** Shunshuisi Park, Xinqiao, Youdiangang, Nanping's Line 10 platform and Qinglonghu
  remain absent. Line 15 (Jingkou – Liangjiang Film City first section) is not opened merely because
  its fare was published: the [September 8 fare notice](https://fzggw.cq.gov.cn/zwgk/zfxxgkml/jgxx/jgzc/202609/t20260908_16048650.html)
  sets the fares "暂定从2026年10月1日起…具体开始时间以试运营开始时间为准" (tentatively from 1 October,
  the actual start being the start of trial operation; [Tencent News summary, 11 September 2026](https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260911A0CMC800)),
  after the [August pre-opening safety assessment](https://jtysw.cq.gov.cn/sy_240/bmdt/202608/t20260819_15951204.html),
  non-passenger trial running from June 18 ([cq.gov.cn, 19 June 2026](https://www.cq.gov.cn/ywdt/jrcq/202606/t20260619_15765585_wap.html))
  and the [September 19 power-up report](https://www.cqnews.net/web/content_1550770814051643392.html).
  Re-checked on 2 October 2026, no report of passengers riding Line 15 was found, and the
  [zh.wikipedia network article](https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-cn/重庆轨道交通) lists no line opened since the
  Line 4 west extension of 10 February 2026 (Lines 15, 24 and 27 are still under construction there).
  Future project completion targets are not passenger opening dates.

### Rename rollout qualifications

These are implementation-date choices supported by dated reports, not claims that every sign
changed simultaneously:

1. **Chongqing North → Chongqing North Station South Square:** April 7, 2016 starts the reported
   formal rollout. Some signs were visible on March 22; the project was scheduled to finish April 30.
   [March signage report](https://news.ifeng.com/a/20160323/48123672_0.shtml), April report above.
2. **Jiangbei Airport → Terminal 2 of Jiangbei Airport:** December 25, 2017 is the dated new map
   attestation. Secondary accounts also give December 26 or the December 28 Line 10 opening;
   the exact first day of every English sign/announcement was not established.
3. **Pingchang → Happy Valley:** January 12, 2018 is the formal rename reported on January 19.
   [New platform signs were already reported December 3, 2017](https://www.cqtitle.com/new/gd/2017/1204/16876.html),
   while other signs and announcements still used Pingchang. Proposal/approval dates in March/July
   2017 are not treated as completed passenger-name changes.
4. **Four university names:** the operator starts the batch on December 1, 2019; physical signage
   work continues into March 2020. See the [university's rollout explanation](https://dwxcbwlgzb.swu.edu.cn/info/1028/3316.htm).
   Construction names and unimplemented proposals do not create passenger-history states.

### Geography, identity and distance

- Route alignments, stop locations, riverbanks and administrative boundaries are derived from
  [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), © OpenStreetMap contributors,
  [ODbL 1.0](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), retrieved September 24, 2026 (route relations,
  platforms and the waterways added on 2026-10-03: Overpass snapshots of 1–2 October 2026).
  All layers use EPSG:32648, at 18 metres per SVG unit. River polygons preserve islands and the
  Yangtze/Jialing confluence; Sichuan beyond the Chongqing boundary uses the foreign-land fill.
  Shorelines represent the current geography, not an animated hydrological history.
- OSM route relations: 2336457, 2353578, 2341149, 9597503, 7677819, 7913722, 2768661,
  19293566, 3474487, 14004563, 8300862, 15749313, 7662492, 10176833, 17135615 and 12759727.
  Chongqing boundary: 913069. These establish geometry, not historical service dates.
- Smooth cubic curves follow mapped railway ways; markers keep their real positions even where another line passes close by.
  The drawing is geographically based, not a survey or a claim of exact platform dimensions.
- **OSM geometry pass, 29 September 2026.** Tracks and markers found more than 1.5 track widths from their OpenStreetMap position were redrawn along the mapped railway ways (local fits on the nearest matched stations), with markers placed on their real platforms even where a line that does not stop there passes close by. Line 1 between Xiaolongkan and Gaomiaocun and the Loop Line between Chongqing Library and Shapingba now follow their alignments, putting Majiayan and Tianxingqiao on their real positions (both had been about 190 m off). Line 10 between Minxinjiayuan and Longtousi Park had been drawn 270–350 m east of its route; it now runs beside Line 3 through Chongqing North Station South Square and crosses Line 4 at the North Square, whose markers (including the 2017–2018 Line 10 circle and the 2011–2018 Line 3 circle) are on their real platforms; Line 3 between Longtousi and Shiziping no longer bows west. Lines 5 and 6 between Ranjiaba and Dalongshan, one shared corridor, are drawn side by side instead of splayed apart. Nanping (Line 3) is on its monorail platform where Line 10 passes without stopping. Shapingba's 2011–2022 Line 1 circle is on the Line 1 platform (it had been 490 m west); the separate 2018–2022 Loop and 2022 Line 9 circles stay staggered along their own tracks because the three platforms are too close for separate markers. Between Toutang and Baoshuigang, Lines 4 and 9 share one corridor, drawn 1 W apart with Line 4 on the north-west side and no weave. Both stations' markers are on the OSM platforms. The tight Line 2 bend north of Zoo is eased. At Fuhualu, Line 18 joins Line 9 from the south and runs 1 W south of it on OSM (both had been 1.2 W off), and Lines 9 and 10 run 1 W apart at Shangwanlu.
- There are 44 track paths, split at historical openings rather than every station, and 325 dated
  marker versions. At the cutoff, 276 marker identities are present. Separate outside interchanges
  count separately; simplified SkyShuttle stops do not inflate the heavy-rail station count.
- Published kilometres come from opening reports and the operator group's
  [April 2026 bond prospectus, printed pages 25–26](https://static.sse.com.cn/disclosure/bond/announcement/company/c/new/2026-04-22/245126_20260422_2LAT.pdf).
  Its opening-date column contains transcription errors and is not used to override contemporary
  opening notices. Lengths are rounded to tenths. Early staged Line 1/2/3 sections are apportioned
  within published totals; those subdivisions are estimates. Line 4's west section is approximately
  9.5 km after excluding the unopened 1.267 km Shunshuisi Park interval from the 10.8 km project;
  Line 9 excludes the unopened Xinqiao tail. Construction/project lengths therefore need not equal
  the sum of drawn passenger sections. No hidden track or length is added to force a headline total. Current drawn sections sum to 575.5 km, or 590.9 km including SkyShuttle.
- [CRT logo source](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chongqing_Rail_Transit_logo.svg): the existing
  green emblem is retained in its original proportions, with the accompanying wordmark omitted.
  The mark identifies the network; it is not newly drawn or an endorsement.

Validation: the spec checker, every event and adjacent day in forward/reverse playback, station
search (including historical names and separate same-name stations), line-filtered search,
tooltip dismissal, mobile resize, home preview and actual Bézier-to-marker clearance.
The checks validate the implementation, not the unresolved exact-day rollout questions above.

- Station markers (2026-10-01), spec §5: platform points are OSM platform ways (else stop positions), projected through a UTM 48 fit (0.2-unit residual) onto each line's drawn track. There is no line-map reference, so composition follows the platforms; which platforms form one shape is set out in the interchange shapes bullet below. Bridges are straight, as OSM maps no in-station walkways. Tracks that strayed from OSM were redrawn on it (largest: Line 1 Shapingba–Lieshimu, 5.9 units, Line 6 at Hongqihegou (5.9), the Loop north of Shapingba (6.6), Line 18 at Tiaodeng (7.5)); corridors drawn 2–2.5 W wide now run 1 W apart (Lijia, Yuelai, Min'an Ave., Chongqing West); the splayed ends at Yudaishan, Bishan and Tiaodeng meet at their real platforms. Track ends lie on their platform points. Xiaolongkan's and Lijia's early circles moved about 8 units to their platforms. Yudaishan's 2026 Line 4 circle is staggered 2.2 R west of the Loop circle (out-of-station); Fotuguan stays 2.1 R from Eling (no transfer).
- Final audit (2026-10-01, revised 2026-10-03): out-of-station circles that touch or overlap stand on real platforms or recorded decisions: Shapingba 2018–2022, Xietaizi (the Line 18 platform lies between the Line 1 and Line 5 platforms), Bishan's 2024–2025 out-of-station week and, since 2026-10-03, Yangjiaping (1.56 R): Line 18 now runs on its real course, 3.3 units further east, and both circles already sit 2.9 units from their platform centres, as far along their short platforms as they can go.
- Interchange composition (2026-10-01): spec §5 rule 2 (no reference line map), from the zh.wikipedia 车站结构 sections (levels, 股道) and the OpenStreetMap platform ways and stop positions. No Chongqing interchange shares track: every 同台换乘 pair runs on its own tracks. One shape only for a **full stacked crossing**, where one platform passes directly over the middle of the other: Hongqihegou (3/6), Chongqing North Station North Square (10/4), Shangxinjie (6/Loop) and Hongtudi (10/6), each one circle on the drawn crossing; and Ranjiaba, where the Loop's platform crosses directly under the stacked islands that Lines 5 and 6 share, so all three are one circle. Everything else is separate dots at the real platforms joined by a bridge, overlapping where close. That covers cross-platform pairs on their own tracks (Chongqing West Station, Tiaodeng's Line 5/Jiangtiao, Baoshuigang, Shangwanlu, Wangjiazhuang, Lijia, Dalongshan and Min'an Ave.), parallel stacked islands (Toutang, Fuhualu, Jiangbeicheng, Wulidian's Loop/6), side-by-side stations (Shiqiaopu, Yudong, Yuelai, Bishan's Line 1/Bitong), and T and L nodes, where one platform's end meets the other: Lianglukou, Zengjiayan, Central Park West, and Chongqing North Station South Square, whose Line 3, Line 10 and Loop are now three dots. It also covers passages and hall-to-hall transfers: Xiaoshizi, Jiaochangkou, Qixinggang, Daping, Niujiaotuo, Xiejiawan, Dashiba, Huahuiyuan, Hongyancun, Liyuchi, Central Park East, Nanhu, Olympic Sports Center, Xiaolongkan, Jiazhoulu, Jiangbei Airport T2, Baijusi, Sigongli, Wulidian's Line 9, Tiaodeng's Line 18, Bishan's SkyShuttle and Shapingba (three island stations whose passages opened in 2022; the 2018–2022 out-of-station circles stay staggered).
- Close platforms (2026-10-02, spec §5 rule 3): separate shapes closer than 0.4 R read as one lump even fully zoomed in, so they are drawn as one shape through the same platform points, which do not move: Wulidian (Line 6 and Loop line, 0.30 R). Pairs 0.4 R or more apart stay separate dots.
- Smoothness (2026-10-01): the three corners left over from earlier joint moves were made tangent-continuous by turning both Bézier handles at the node onto their bisector, a sub-unit change: Line 3 at Lianglukou (12°), Line 4 east of Tangjiatuo (11°) and the Expo line at Yuelai (34°). Smaller joint corners (3–9°) were treated the same way. No shared corridor weaves. Out-of-station pairs on crossing lines are staggered along their own tracks to 2 R within their platforms: Xiejiawan 2019–2023 (2.4 units each from the platform centres since 2026-10-03, when Line 2 moved onto its course) and Guanyinqiao (1.95 each); Yangjiaping is 1.56 R (above).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), tracks: markers are dots at the real platforms, so no track needs to bend round a marker. Every track was compared with its OSM route relations (snapshot 2026-10-01), allowing a line in a shared corridor to sit anywhere from the corridor centre to 1 W out on its own side. Stretches that strayed more than 1.5 units (27 m) outside that were redrawn on OSM: Line 9 from Gaotanyan past Tianlilu (3.8 units west; both circles moved onto their platforms, 3.1 and 2.4 units), Line 1 at Daping (3.1 south; its dot moved 2.9), Jiaochangkou (3.1, pushed by Line 2's undrawn tail track) and near Shapingba/Xiaolongkan (3.5), Line 18 at Yangjiaping (3.8 west), Line 6 at Huahuiyuan and Hongqihegou (3.3; the Huahuiyuan markers moved 3.0 and the Hongqihegou crossing circle 1.9, now within 0.4 of both platforms) and at Xiaoshizi (2.2), Line 3 near Guanyinqiao and Jiazhoulu (2.1), Line 2 near Xiejiawan (2.3), Line 10 south of Zengjiayan (2.2; Zengjiayan itself was left as drawn so its Line 2/10 pair stays at 0.40 R), the Loop at Nanhu and near Erlang (2.3) and Line 9 north of Xingke Ave. (2.0). Platform points were re-projected at the same OSM platforms (with the same offsets for staggered circles), and track ends and joints moved with them; `data-km` is unchanged (spec §4).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), side-by-side corridors: neighbouring lines in a shared corridor now touch exactly (centres 1 W = 5.0 units apart) instead of leaving hairline gaps (5.3–6.7) or overlapping (2–4.9). Shangwanlu: Line 10 had bulged 5.6 units north of its course at the cross-platform station (8.9 from Line 9); it now runs 1 W beside Line 9 from their junction to the crossing, and the dots overlap on the shared island (0.65 R). Yuelai – Wangjiazhuang: the International Expo Line follows OSM (it had wobbled up to 4.2 units) and Line 10 runs 1 W beside it, crossing once where the real tracks cross; the Wangjiazhuang terminus dots now overlap at the shared platform (they had been 8 units apart). Chongqing West Station: the Loop's 3.5–5.7-unit bulge is gone; Line 5 and the Loop run 1 W apart about the centre of their interleaved tracks. Also Shiqiaopu – Xietaizi (Lines 1/5, which had woven and half-overlapped), Toutang – Baoshuigang (4/9), Min'an Ave. (4/Loop; Line 4 now leaves westward in one curve instead of half over the Loop), Yudaishan (4/Loop), Ranjiaba – Dalongshan (5/6), south of Wulidian (6/9), Fuhualu (18/9) and Tiaodeng (Line 18 beside Line 5/Jiangtiao). Where a line joins or leaves a corridor it does so in one smooth curve. Wulidian's Line 6/Loop pair is left as it is (one shape).
- Final audit (2026-10-03), joints and curves: 48 micro-segments (under 0.5 units) were merged and all 60 node corners over 0.3° (up to 5.8°, Line 4 east of Tangjiatuo) and 17 same-line joints that turned 0.2–1.5° were made tangent-continuous; no node or joint now turns more than 0.3°.
- Final audit (2026-10-03), geography: the water outline is checked against OSM banks and the named-river centrelines over the whole canvas. Two hidden patches were replaced by fixes in the outline itself: a slit across the Yangtze near Changshou (formerly covered by a separate fill with notched bank strokes) is closed, and a thin spike under Line 1 on the Liangtan River (formerly painted over by a land-coloured rectangle) is removed. Simplification artefacts removed: a 9-unit land crack off Chaotianmen, five bank notches and spikes, six sliver "islands" 0.06–0.4 units wide (drawn as hairline cracks by the bank stroke; the longest 12.5 units in the Yangtze at Tangjiatuo), three specks glued to the river edge, a zero-area sliver and a 6-unit² pond. The Fu River stopped 7 km above its mouth because the lower reach's OSM banks are unnamed (ways 102276456, 102301898); it now reaches the Jialing at Hechuan. Two rivers of the drawn rivers' width class (Yulin 103 m, Qu 379 m) were missing: the Qijiang (mean 124 m; way 652540402, relations 127661 and 9079499, with a 152-unit symbolic channel at the southern canvas edge where no banks are mapped) and the Qiongjiang to its Fu mouth (97 m; ways 1558165733–1558165776, relations 3637960–3637961). Dam seams on the Fu stay (Weituo, way 664346714; ways 928746822–928746823). Narrower rivers stay omitted as before; the Longxi below Changshou Lake (about 100 m wide but only 44 % of it with mapped banks) is not drawn. Zengjiayan's Line 10 platform point (the OSM platform) lies 0.4 units (7 m) inside the Jialing outline, as before, within the precision of the simplified bank.

<a id="xian"></a>

## Xi'an (`xian`)

Assets: [events](../src/assets/xian/data/events.json), [line names](../src/assets/xian/data/lines.json), [SVG](../src/assets/xian/map.svg).
New map and research, **27 September 2026**. New geographic artwork drawn from OpenStreetMap, not a converted network diagram.

### Scope

The map follows the operator's current official network map ([西安轨道交通线网示意图 / Xi'an Metro System Map][xa-official-map], version of 2026-06-29): Lines 1–6, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15, 16 and the **Xihu Line**, which the map draws as a normal legend line with its two open stations. The Xihu Line runs over national-rail track, but Xi'an Metro sells its tickets and runs its passenger service (China Railway Xi'an Group dispatches the trains), so it passes both scope tests (spec §8). Xianyang sections of Xi'an Metro lines (Line 1 phases 2 and 3, Lines 5, 14 and 16) are included.

- **Line 14 and the Airport Intercity.** The 西安北至机场城际 (Airport Intercity) opened on 2019-09-29 under 陕西城际铁路有限公司, a Shaanxi Railway Group company, with separate fares. Xi'an Metro took over its management from 2021-01-01 and merged it into Line 14 on 2021-06-29. Whether Xi'an Metro's 2019–20 maps drew it is not established; it is included as Line 14's predecessor (spec §8's operator family includes predecessors), labelled **Airport Intercity** until the merger, with a dated operator handover.
- **Excluded:** the Hi-Tech Zone SkyShuttle (西安云巴, also called the Hi-Tech Zone tram test line; opened 2024-08-12, run by 西安云巴交通运营有限公司 for the district, own fares, not on the official map); the out-of-service Qujiang sightseeing monorail and Kunming Lake ART line (tourist operators); national rail; Line 17 and other lines under construction; the Xihu Line's three unopened stations (昆明池, 马王, 五竹).
- **Own-land shading:** Xi'an's municipal boundary ([OSM relation 3226004][xa-osm-boundary]) is the own land. Xianyang (including the Xianyang parts of Xixian New Area and the airport), Weinan and the other neighbours use the outside-land colour; Line 1's phase 2 and 3 sections, the western parts of Lines 5 and 16 and most of Line 14 run across it.

Openings follow spec §7. Three lines had free public trial rides before opening and appear with those rides and stay on the map through the opening (spec §7), which is its own "opens" event: Line 2 (2011-09-08 – 11; tickets handed out through line-side communities), Line 1 (2013-09-09 – 10; trial-ride tickets) and the Airport Intercity (2019-09-23 – 24; free vouchers at any station, no ID needed). Every other pre-opening ride found (media, invited residents, 试乘证 holders, "体验官", open days) was invitation-only and is not drawn: Line 3 (2016-09-01), Line 4 (2018-12), Line 1 phase 2 (2019-09-22), Lines 5/6/9 (2020-12-07 – 09), Line 14 (2021-03-21, 2021-06-25), Xihu (2022-10-01), Line 6 phase 2 (2022-12-25), Line 1 phase 3 (2023-09-16), 2024-09-19 – 22, Line 8 (2024-12-22), Line 15 (2025-12-23) and 西安东站 (2026-06-26). No pre-opening rides were found for Line 2's 2014 and 2023 extensions, Line 16 or 机场（T5）; searches are not proof of absence. Temporary suspensions (including the December 2021 – January 2022 lockdown) are not drawn.

**Events after 2026-06-30 (checked 2026-10-03):** none up to 2026-10-02. 2026 is a gap year between construction plans ([界面新闻, 2026-02-24](https://m.jiemian.com/article/14030803.html): "2026年西安地铁建设将进入到空窗期"; its only 2026 item, Line 5's 西安东站, opened on 2026-06-30). The zh.wikipedia network table ends with that opening; Line 17 (to 富平) is under construction; the Xihu Line's 昆明池, 马王 and 五竹 are unopened; 木塔寺 and 木塔寺西 still have no transfer.

### Primary records and focused references

- [Official network map, 2026-06-29][xa-official-map] — **New**. Scope, legend colours, interchange symbols and the current English (romanised) station names; transcribed for all 248 stations. The operator's station API (`api-basicdata/lineStation/findLineAll`) was also read but is stale for renamed and new stations.
- [华商报 via Sina, 2011-03-25][xa-pinyin-2011] — **New**. "西安地铁一、二号线英文站名全部采用大写汉语拼音译法…北客站翻译成BEIKEZHAN". Xi'an has used capitalised Hanyu Pinyin station names since opening; every later renaming notice gives the "罗马字母拼写".
- [Xi'an Civil Affairs Bureau, 2022-09-20 (archived)][xa-rename-2022], [西部网, 2023-06-26][xa-rename-2023] and [Sina, 2025-07-25][xa-rename-2025] — **New**. Dated renames.
- [Operator colour reply on 人民网, 2020-04-08 (archived)][xa-colours-2020] — **New**. Pantone references for Lines 1–4 (3005 C, Red 032 C, 252 U, 319 C); Lines 5, 6 and 9 are 374 U, 2726 C and 1375 C in other replies.
- Each event row below cites the notices and reports behind that date.

**English names.** Labels use the official romanisation exactly as spelled and spaced on the 2026 map and in the renaming notices, written with ordinary pinyin capitalisation (GB/T 16159) instead of the all-capitals signage typography: `ZHONGLOU` → `Zhonglou`, `FENGCHENG 10 LU` → `Fengcheng 10 Lu`, `XI'AN BEIZHAN` → `Xi'an Beizhan`, `SHIDI-SANYIYUAN` → `Shidi-Sanyiyuan`. The airport stations keep their English (`Airport W.(T1/T2/T3)`, `Airport(T5)`); the commas of `AIRPORT W.(T1,T2,T3)` become slashes, as in the operator's API, because label syntax forbids commas (spec §2). Line 4's 北客站（北广场） is `Beikezhan (Beiguangchang)` from its signage (zh.wikipedia and Commons photographs). Lines are named `Line N`, `Xihu Line` and `Airport Intercity`.

**Logos and licences.**

- `xian-metro.svg`: the Xi'an Metro city-wall emblem, from [en.wikipedia File:Xian_Metro_logo.svg][xa-logo] (a local non-free file tagged SVG-Logo and Trademark, author given as Xi'an Metro Group). Graphic only, no lettering; its paths and colour are unchanged, with a comment added.
- `xazt.svg`: 西安中铁轨道交通有限公司 (XAZT), the China Railway (60 %) / Xi'an Rail Transit Group (40 %) PPP company that has run Line 9 under a 30-year BOT concession since it opened ([company profile][xa-xazt]). No vector or Commons file exists; the emblem was redrawn as vector geometry from the company's raster footer logo, with the "XAZT" lettering removed from its band. All rights reserved by the company; used for identification only.
- `shaanxi-railway.svg`: the emblem of 陕西省铁路集团 (Shaanxi Province Railway Group), parent of 陕西城际铁路有限公司, redrawn as vector from the group's raster logo on its archived site without the lettering. No logo of the subsidiary itself was found. All rights reserved; used for identification only.
- Both redrawn marks were rendered and compared with their sources (about 0.87–0.88 overlap ratio, the difference being the removed lettering and anti-aliasing).
